**Purpose.** The autonomous audit-fix loop (HANDOFF 2026-11-15, owner
goal) hinges on routing: an auditor's finding must carry machine-
checkable CLASS so the orchestrator can route without interpreting
prose — fix-worthy findings re-enter the implementation loop, spec
findings become human-review items, accepted residuals are recorded and
never re-litigated. §14.3's kinds cover what the supervisor decides and
observes about its own actions; none represents an audit finding. This
section adds TWO record kinds — `audit-finding` and
`audit-finding-update` — in the episode's decision log (S5,
`events/decisions.jsonl`), same envelope, same durability discipline.
§0.7 holds unchanged: control logic keys on the closed fields only;
free-text fields are advisory, never parsed.

#### 14.10.0 Rule register (NDR-a … NDR-v) — canonical statements (v33)

**Why this register exists (v22, Plan B).** Round-4 data (14 cycles +
confirming cycle 15, plateau at 4–5 MAJOR/cycle since cycle 9) showed the
findings split into (A) fold residue — a rule correctly changed at its
primary site surviving in contradictory form at duplicate statement sites —
and (B) new-fold-text gaps. The root cause is structural: every rule of
§14.10 is restated at 4–6 sites (precedence prose + disposition result
table + replay vectors + §14.12.2 class-B/O rows + summary paragraphs), so
a fold that sweeps semantically cannot be verified by grep anchors. The
plan is `docs/audits/g1-plan-b-canonicalization.md`; this register is its
execution against baseline v21. It changes NO ratified decision (non-goal:
any extraction ambiguity that would CHANGE behavior is escalated as
DECISIONS-REQUIRED, never resolved silently).

**Register doctrine (normative, v22):**

1. Each rule below is stated ONCE — the **canonical statement** in its
   register entry, plus (where the rule needs clause-level detail) a
   **declared expansion**: the entry's `*Expansion:*` field names a
   bounded, finite set of sites (one OR MORE — v23 R5-C16-6: v22 said
   "ONE named expansion site" while six entries declared multi-site
   expansions, making the fold boundary ambiguous; the fold rule is
   unchanged — a fold edits the entry plus EXACTLY its declared set —
   what changed is that a multi-site declaration is legal, an
   UNDECLARED site is not; a rule whose detail genuinely lives in two
   unmergeable places is declared as a two-site expansion, never left
   undeclared). An entry whose rule is self-contained in the entry
   declares `*Expansion:* (none — self-contained)`.
   The id (`NDR-a` … `NDR-v` — extended v27 R5-C19-1 with the cure
   protocol and effect-binding-exception entries) is stable forever; ids
   are never reused or renumbered.
2. Every OTHER location in §14.10 and its overlap zones (§14.9 fold-
   hygiene row, §14.12.2 class-B/O rows and the r4 chain-closure table,
   §14.12.6) states a PREDICATE plus `per NDR-<id>` and never a restated
   rule body. **Where a register entry (or its expansion) and any other
   text disagree, THE REGISTER ENTRY GOVERNS**; a diverging non-register
   text is a defect, corrected to a citation.
3. **Table-cell budget (§14.12.2 B/O rows, r4 chain table):** a cell may
   contain predicates, enums of record ids/codes, and `per NDR-<id>`
   citations; a rule BODY in a cell is a defect. Mechanically auditable:
   `scripts/g1-ndr-selfcheck.mjs` (wired into `npm test` via
   `scripts/quality-check.sh`) fails the build if (i) any
   `per NDR-<id>` citation resolves to no register entry, (ii) any NDR id
   is defined twice or any register entry lacks an `*Expansion:*`
   declaration, or (iii) a §14.12.2 B/O cell exceeds 150 words without
   carrying a citation. (A fourth candidate check — normative-marker lines
   living outside a register entry or registered expansion — is NOT
   mechanically decidable across the whole section and is deliberately
   left to the cycle audit, so the script never over-claims.)
4. **Fold-hygiene v2 (extends the §14.9 gate):** a future fold MAY edit
   (i) a canonical entry and its registered expansion site, and (ii)
   mechanical citation text — nothing else; the Change Ledger row lists
   the NDR ids touched and asserts `sites-edited = canonical only`. A
   fold that needs to change a non-canonical location first converts it
   to a citation (separate hygiene commit).
5. Every sentence DEMOTED from a statement site to a citation in this v22
   conversion is preserved verbatim (with its site) in
   `docs/audits/g1-ndr-conflict-log.md`, together with the round-4
   finding → NDR mapping, so each historical fold stays re-verifiable
   against the register instead of against prose scatter.

**Register (closed list):**

- **NDR-a — Entry modes & emission authority.** Exactly three legal
  (origin, proof) entry modes, and nullability is driven by MODE, not
  origin: (1) auditor intake — `origin:"auditor"`, originRef receipt,
  producer trio, via supervisor intake (which validates and mints the id);
  (2) owner-act — `origin:"owner"`, `ownerActRef` REQUIRED non-null, no
  originRef, never a receipt outcome; (3) supervisor-derived — records
  admitted WITHOUT an owner act, `origin` is EITHER `"auditor"` OR
  `"owner"` (whichever OBSERVED the defect — v23 R5-C16-1: v22's row
  said "owner-origin records" only, contradicting its own registered
  expansion, the §14.10.1 entry-mode table, which admits an
  auditor-observed supervisor-derived finding; the mode is defined by
  its PROOF, not by origin), originRef REQUIRED
  `{origin:"supervisor-derived", fromRefusalId}`, `ownerActRef` null,
  producer = supervisor session (the appender — observer ≠ appender:
  `origin` names who observed, `producer` names who appended); derived
  mode is the SUPERVISOR's filing privilege, never a worker's. Auditor
  workers append
  `audit-finding` records only; they never append updates and cannot
  originate an `origin:"owner"` line by ANY route; the owner never appends
  to the log directly. The two non-intake modes' records are excluded
  from intake accounting. All other (origin, proof) combinations are
  refused as malformed. *Applies:* `audit-finding`, `audit-filing`,
  derived records. *Expansion:* §14.10.1 entry-mode table (+ its scoping
  clauses) and §14.10.3 emission-authority opening. *Cited at:* §14.10.1
  origin/producer prose, §14.10.3 first paragraphs.
- **NDR-b — Accepted-fix evidence rule (minor exception is the only
  null-ref route).** `accepted-fix` requires a non-null `reproRunRef`
  naming a green re-run for EVERY finding, EXCEPT the one minor owner
  exception: `severity:"minor"` + disposition by an owner act + echoed
  non-empty reason + `reproRunRef == null` (orchestrator excluded). The
  exception excuses the ABSENCE of a run, never a bad one: a non-null
  reference must pass ordinary green-run validation regardless of owner
  reason. `repro.kind:"none"` is refused for non-minor findings for every
  producer; a minor kind:none finding reaches `accepted-fix` ONLY via the
  exception. **CHAIN-MEMBER DISCHARGE (v27 R5-C19-6 — the r4 chain table's
  minor-exception row applies this predicate; v26 cited this entry for it
  but the entry did not state it — it is canonical HERE now): an
  `accepted-fix` closed via the minor owner exception DISCHARGES an r4
  chain member ONLY where the member is minor AND the member's OWN
  effective link (per NDR-n step 2) is machine-checked
  (`reproDigest` equal); otherwise the member is UNCLEAN, needs its own
  disposition, and an already-closed member the run cannot reach is cured
  ONLY by NDR-p edge (1), forward-only (the exception excuses the ABSENCE
  of a run — it never validates a non-machine-checked member link).**
  *Applies:* `audit-finding-update`, dispositionBy, §14.12.2
  rule 4, r4 minor-exception chain row (v27 R5-C19-6). *Expansion:* §14.10.1 acceptance sentence + §14.10.2 minor
  exception text. *Cited at:* §14.12.2 rule 4, r4 chain table exception
  row, §14.10.3 `finding-disposition` payload `reason` rule (the reason
  echo binding is this rule's operand check, not an independent rule).
- **NDR-c — Claim equality.** Two claims are equal iff the NFC-normalized
  decoded JSON string VALUES are equal (both sides normalized) — never
  raw-byte equality of serialized payloads (the canonicalizer's mandatory
  NFC applies; the v9 "no normalization" byte reading is WITHDRAWN).
  *Applies:* `refiled` dispositions (drift resolution, integrity
  disposition), header-claim vs payload-claim comparison. *Expansion:*
  §14.10.3 filing-replay clause. *Cited at:* filing-integrity-disposition
  `refiled` binding, replay vectors.
- **NDR-d — Refusal binding: general rule + EXHAUSTIVE two-class
  exception.** General rule: every permanent refusal record binds its OWN
  immediate predecessor (the intake-validation prefix; `{intakePrefixEndId,
  intakePrefixSha256}`), and replay re-derives its diagnostic over exactly
  THAT bound prefix and its class-defined verification source, never
  against the evolved prefix. Exception classes, jointly exhaustive with
  the general rule: (i) a PINNED re-adjudication refusal R2 (the P(W)
  adjudication itself refused; its diagnostic derives over P(W)) binds the
  withdrawal's frozen P(W) — established by identity (the protocol's
  cross-binding clauses), not adjacency — because recovery may append
  unrelated records between W and R2; (ii) an APPEND-LEGALITY-GATE
  refusal (per NDR-j) binds its OWN immediate predecessor under the
  general rule — its checks evaluated the append-time prefix. The class
  is determined by the refusal's own derivation and is REPLAY-CHECKABLE
  from the record + outcome `pinnedVerdict` pair (eligibility ⇒
  predecessor-bound; refusal ⇒ P(W)-bound); a binding mode inconsistent
  with the re-derived pinned verdict is a malformed candidate, never an
  outcome; never from an asserted label. *Applies:* every
  terminal-by-refusal record, re-adjudication outcomes, replay
  validation. *Expansion:* §14.10.3 binding paragraph (R5-C7-3 /
  R5-C10-2 / R5-C13-5). *Cited at:* terminal-outcome summary, outcome
  same-act binding clause, §14.12.2 O row.
- **NDR-e — Byte provenance: canonical labels.** `bytesSource` is a
  REQUIRED field and a deterministic function of durable records ONLY
  (replay-computable for any landed effect; recovery never guesses and
  never re-runs to fill it). Closed enum `"content-addressed" |
  "fresh-spool" | "none"` (`"embedded-R1"` DELETED — physical source is
  unobservable from durable records; the label is a content-only
  function): `"content-addressed"` exactly when the consumed bytes
  RE-DIGEST to the act's `draftSha256` (any outcome kind;
  `observedSha256:null` — the digest match against the act IS the
  provenance); `"fresh-spool"` only with NO embedded bytes (a
  draft-derivative condition judged over observed bytes named by
  `observedSha256`) — under current admission rules this is a RESERVED
  label with no domain; the validator NEVER fabricates it; `"none"` only
  for FILESYSTEM-OBSERVATION (drift) refusals where no draft bytes exist
  to consume. `observedSha256` is non-null EXACTLY when
  `bytesSource:"fresh-spool"`. The act-digest re-check of a MIXED
  refusal's `adjudicatedDraftBytes` is CONSTITUTIVE of the refusal
  (per NDR-f): mismatch ⇒ malformed record on the integrity route —
  NEVER a `"fresh-spool"` outcome label (an outcome label can never
  waive the act-byte binding; the v19 `!=` ⇒ fresh-spool branch is
  DELETED). *Applies:* `audit-filing-readjudication-outcome`, recovery,
  refusal validation. *Expansion:* §14.10.3 byte-provenance-fields
  paragraph AND §14.10.3 recovery-reconstructibility clause (bounded —
  v25 R5-C18-6: the clause's per-outcome label-assignment algorithm IS
  this entry's "deterministic function of durable records ONLY" rule
  spelled to case level; v24 R5-C17-6 reclassified it a citation while
  the normative algorithm stayed in place, so the declared boundary and
  the text disagreed — doctrine 1 (v23) permits a bounded FINITE set of
  declared expansions, so the honest fix is to declare the site, not to
  relabel it; a conforming fold changing the label-assignment algorithm
  now MUST sweep this expansion). *Cited at:* kind-(d)
  recovery duty, §14.12.2.
- **NDR-f — MIXED check class: joint re-derivation.** Exactly the four
  correction codes (`correction-bad-target`, `correction-ambiguity`,
  `correction-severity-decrease`, `correction-route-mismatch`) form the
  closed MIXED class: re-derive JOINTLY over the bound prefix AND the
  digest-verified `adjudicatedDraftBytes` TOGETHER — header operands
  (target id, proposed severity, proposed route) from the verified bytes,
  target state/lineage from the bound prefix. Prefix-only or bytes-only
  re-derivation is INCOMPLETE for this class and validation that runs
  either alone has not validated anything. A MIXED (or draft-derivative)
  refusal missing `adjudicatedDraftBytes`, or whose bytes fail the
  re-digest to the act's `draftSha256`, is a malformed record →
  integrity fault (never silently honored). *Applies:* refusal-record
  validation, re-adjudication inputs, gate checks. *Expansion:* §14.10.3
  check-class paragraph. *Cited at:* binding paragraph, append-legality
  gate, determinism clause (3).
- **NDR-g — `intake-refusal` fault predicate (closed ONLY-list).** An
  `intake-refusal` fault arises ONLY from: failed LOG-DERIVATIVE
  re-derivation over the bound prefix; failed DRAFT-DERIVATIVE
  re-derivation over embedded bytes; failed MIXED joint re-derivation;
  embedded bytes ABSENT / MALFORMED / DIGEST-MISMATCHED on a
  draft-derivative or MIXED refusal; a missing or malformed binding pair;
  a self-contradictory field. Nothing else raises the kind. *Applies:*
  `owner-filing-integrity-fault` minting. *Expansion:* §14.10.3 fault
  paragraph. *Cited at:* fault-list copy, §14.12.2 O row, §14.10.2
  intake-refusal paragraph ("every failure mode" site) and its
  re-adjudication paragraph (the two sites that restated this ONLY-list
  in prose — cycle-16 audit F4: they are application copies of this
  entry, not independent rules).
- **NDR-h — Filing-integrity faults: shape, identity, exclusion.**
  Record `{faultTs, actId, failingCheck:"effect-record"|
  "findingRef-artifact"|"act-payload"|"intake-refusal"|
  "readjudication-group", refusalRecordId:string|null, evidenceRefs[]}`
  (supervisor-authored, envelope-carried). `refusalRecordId` is REQUIRED
  non-null for `intake-refusal` (must resolve in-log to an intake-refusal
  with `refusedActId == actId` AND appear among the fault's
  `evidenceRefs[]`), REQUIRED null for the DAMAGE kinds (non-null is
  malformed). Identity: damage kinds `(actId, failingCheck)` for all
  time — one undispositioned-record-per-identity, never re-minted by
  post-disposition re-observation; `intake-refusal` is EVENTFUL
  `(actId, failingCheck, refusalRecordId)` — a disposed intake-refusal
  fault NEVER suppresses a later distinct forged-refusal attempt. Class-B
  exclusion: the DAMAGE kinds (incl. `readjudication-group`) exclude the
  act from class B on the record's EXISTENCE (open OR disposed); an
  `intake-refusal` fault excludes ONLY while UNDISPOSITIONED. Disposition
  results are per NDR-l; predicates at the finalization rows are per
  NDR-m. *Applies:* every act with a recorded fault, finalization.
  *Expansion:* §14.10.3 fault paragraph + precedence-by-kind clause.
  *Cited at:* §14.12.2 B row, O row, disposition-op text, replay vectors.
- **NDR-i — Withdrawal determinism (serialized adjudication protocol).**
  The `withdrawn` disposition record W carries the re-adjudication prefix
  binding `{readjudicationPrefixEndId, readjudicationPrefixSha256}` =
  the id + running digest of the record IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING W — P(W),
  the pre-disposition prefix; **never W's own digest** (no record
  contains its own digest — a self-referential digest is a
  cryptographic fixed point); W is consumed BY IDENTITY (validated
  well-formed against its own predecessor binding; fields consumed as
  verified record content named by W's record id). Withdrawal +
  adjudication + outcome form ONE serialized unit under the same S5
  flock critical section, with append order **W → effect (finding OR
  refusal R2) → outcome LAST** (the outcome's required id closes the
  group). Exactly ONE `audit-filing-readjudication-outcome` per
  withdrawal (`withdrawalDispositionId` is the durable 1:1 identity; a
  second outcome is malformed, never appended). Determinism means:
  (1) one outcome per withdrawal; (2) all replays agree with the landed
  outcome; (3) pinned-prefix re-checkability — the outcome's
  log-derivative (and, for MIXED codes, joint per NDR-f) verdicts
  re-derive over P(W) and MUST match the record — mismatch is a
  history-integrity-fault, fail closed. No append after W moves P(W),
  W, or W's content. *Applies:* `filing-integrity-disposition`
  `withdrawn` of an `intake-refusal` fault, re-adjudication, recovery.
  *Expansion:* §14.10.3 serialized-protocol paragraph + determinism
  clause. *Cited at:* crash-recovery rule, vector (vii), §14.12.2.
- **NDR-j — Append-legality gate + CLOSED failure-to-diagnostic
  mapping.** The frozen prefix pins the adjudication's VERDICT INPUTS;
  it does NOT exempt the resulting effect from intake legality at append
  time. Once the P(W) adjudication finds the effect eligible (initial
  run or recovery re-run), the supervisor — in the SAME critical section
  — evaluates, over the THEN-CURRENT prefix together with the verified
  draft bytes, the same MIXED-class intake-legality checks (per NDR-f)
  a fresh append of A's finding would pass (lineage linearity: the
  target carries no other correction; target state; severity/route
  comparisons). Legal ⇒ effect + outcome append as specified. A legality
  COLLISION ⇒ no effect; refusal R2 appends carrying the ORDINARY
  diagnostic selected by the CLOSED MAPPING OF GATE FAILURES TO
  DIAGNOSTICS (no new code), bound under the general predecessor rule
  (per NDR-d class (ii)), outcome records `outcome:"refused"` with
  `pinnedVerdict:"eligible"`, `pinnedVerdictCode:null`. Frozen means
  pinned VERDICT INPUTS — never "the later log cannot change legality";
  every append must satisfy its append-time prefix. *Applies:*
  re-adjudication landing (both kinds), recovery re-runs. *Expansion:*
  §14.10.3 append-legality-gate paragraph. *Cited at:* two-class binding
  exception (NDR-d), recovery kinds (a)/(c), outcome binding clause.
- **NDR-k — Crash-recovery duty, TOTAL by candidate kind.** State: W
  durable, outcome absent. Recovery enumerates ALL candidates over the
  UNION of kinds (any `audit-finding` with originating act A appended
  after W; any refusal of A bound per NDR-d appended after W); every
  candidate MUST re-validate. EXACTLY ONE valid candidate ⇒ recovery is
  granted ONE replay-only duty — deterministically re-derive the pinned
  verdict over P(W) + the candidate's durable bytes (VALIDATION, not
  adjudication: appends nothing, mints no effect) — then, by kind:
  **(a) APPLIED finding:** its own effect validation is the owed
  verification; the pinned check re-derives the P(W) verdict over P(W) +
  the finding's DURABLE BYTE AUTHORITY — the finding's IMMUTABLE
  `findingRef` ARTIFACT (written at intake; `sha256(findingRef bytes)`
  == record `claimDigest` == act `draftSha256`, bound two-ways), parsed
  exactly as intake parsed the spool draft — and requires `eligible`;
  a re-derived REFUSAL contradicts the landed applied effect ⇒ forged
  candidate ⇒ group-fault path; missing artifact/transient read ⇒ retry;
  deterministic digest mismatch against either bound ⇒ post-effect
  `findingRef-artifact` damage on the SAME group-fault route, never an
  outcome; conforming ⇒ outcome `applied` + `pinnedVerdict:"eligible"`,
  `pinnedVerdictCode:null`. **(b) PINNED refusal (P(W)-bound):**
  re-derive over P(W) + its embedded/re-digesting bytes; the re-derived
  code MUST equal `diagnosticCode`; conforming ⇒
  `pinnedVerdict:"refused"`, `pinnedVerdictCode ==` re-derived code.
  **(c) GATE refusal (predecessor-bound, NDR-j):** collision diagnostic
  verified over its append-time prefix by the ordinary rule; the pinned
  duty re-derives the P(W) verdict and requires `eligible` — a re-derived
  REFUSAL means the gate refusal asserts `eligible` against a
  pinned-REFUSED prefix ⇒ forged, group-fault path (the assertion is
  PROVEN by re-derivation, never trusted from the binding mode);
  conforming ⇒ `pinnedVerdict:"eligible"`, `pinnedVerdictCode:null`.
  **(d) BYTE-FREE drift refusal (`bytesSource:"none"`, per NDR-e):** no
  draft bytes exist; the duty runs over the refusal record's OWN
  RECORDED `spoolObserved` observation (current filesystem state NEVER
  substitutes), re-deriving the drift verdict over P(W) + that recorded
  observation; conforming ⇒ `pinnedVerdict:"refused"`,
  `pinnedVerdictCode ==` re-derived drift diagnostic == R2's own
  `diagnosticCode` — NO drift case is ever "eligibility-shaped": a
  re-derivation returning `eligible` contradicts the landed P(W)-bound
  refusal ⇒ forged candidate ⇒ group-fault path (replay binding clause
  (1) demands `refused` + code on every P(W)-bound refused outcome).
  Failure route, ALL kinds: transient re-derivation failure ⇒ retry;
  deterministic failure ⇒ the prefix contradicts the pinned-input
  guarantee ⇒ group-fault path; candidate/check mismatch ⇒ group fault,
  never an outcome. NO candidate ⇒ re-run the adjudication over P(W)
  with the NDR-j gate. TWO OR MORE candidates of ANY combination, or a
  candidate failing re-validation ⇒ `readjudication-group` fault
  (per NDR-h): recovery NEVER picks a winner, never silently discharges,
  never re-mints; the fault's only exit is `withdrawn` (`refiled`
  INEXPRESSIBLE), which RETIRES the group — no re-adjudication owed —
  and terminalizes per NDR-l. *Applies:* supervisor restart between W
  and the outcome. *Expansion:* §14.10.3 crash-recovery paragraph.
  *Cited at:* byte-provenance amendment, outcome-binding clause,
  §14.12.2 B row.
- **NDR-l — Terminal taxonomy & class membership.** An act's terminal
  effect states are EXACTLY: **applied** | **terminal-by-refusal** |
  **terminal-by-damage** | **terminal-by-disposition** |
  **terminal-by-cancellation** (v27 R5-C19-5 — a confirmed, unsettled
  `residual-cure` act exited by `residual-cure-cancel` per NDR-u:
  NOTHING is owed — neither a class-B item nor a class-O item, the
  cancellation record IS the clearing evidence — reachable by THAT op
  class only); plus the named
  non-terminal durable replay state **`readjudication-owed`** (class B,
  drain-progressing, until the re-adjudication outcome lands), and
  **claim-retired** (a disposition-retired claim: the act is
  terminal-by-damage and NOTHING is owed — neither a class-B item nor a
  class-O item; the disposition record is the clearing evidence replay
  checks). Per-state membership: a permanent filing refusal (per NDR-d,
  exhaustive over drift, mapping, the correction-lineage refusals, and
  any finding-schema intake failure — codes preserved; transient I/O
  retries, never terminalizes; an unmapped code = contract defect)
  makes the act terminal-by-refusal, its effect set empty-by-refusal,
  cleared ONLY by a conforming `filing-drift-resolution` naming it
  (per NDR-o) — it is never simultaneously terminal and owed (the
  unresolved refusal CONDITION is its class-O item, per NDR-m). Damage-
  kind dispositions: `refiled` ⇒ terminal-by-damage with the fresh
  finding as live evidence, no O/B item; `withdrawn` ⇒ terminal-by-
  damage + claim-retired, no O/B item. An `intake-refusal` fault:
  open ⇒ class O; `refiled` ⇒ terminal-by-disposition (claim stands via
  the accepted fresh filing), nothing owed, ever; `withdrawn` ⇒
  `readjudication-owed` (class B) until the outcome lands (applied ⇒
  applied; new bound refusal ⇒ terminal-by-refusal). A
  `readjudication-group` `withdrawn` ⇒ terminal-by-damage +
  claim-retired — the invalid R1 (if any) is PERMANENTLY
  fault-superseded, never restored to standing, never a resolution
  target, regardless of whether the group arose from R1's invalidity or
  candidate corruption (replay needs no case split; the group's OWN
  damage terminalizes the act). *Applies:* effect fold, finalization
  rows, every disposition outcome. *Expansion:* §14.10.3
  precedence-by-kind clause. *Cited at:* §14.12.2 B row, O row,
  disposition result table, replay vectors.
- **NDR-m — Finalization B/O predicates.** The finalization O predicate
  is the UNDISPOSITIONED fault CONDITION only — never the record's
  existence: a disposed fault is cleared by its disposition record (the
  clearing evidence replay checks) and must NEVER keep a later boundary
  unclean; faults are never re-minted by post-disposition re-observation
  (per NDR-h identity). The class-B row's exclusions and the O row's
  per-disposition results are exactly the enumerations of NDR-l — the
  rows state predicates plus citations; a rule body in either cell is a
  defect (register doctrine 3). Obligations carry into the next window
  (deferral) or stay episode-global (escape, fault); a closed UNCLEAN
  boundary is NEVER retroactively re-cleaned. *Applies:* §14.12.2 steps
  and B/O rows. *Expansion:* §14.12.2 O row (predicate text). *Cited
  at:* B row, verdict table, §14.12.3.
- **NDR-n — Correction lineage: total edge fold.** The fold over
  correction AND duplicate/superseded edges is the TOTAL four-ordered-
  step algorithm to a fixed point: (1) correction pass — target
  validity (only `rejected-refuted` closures may be corrected —
  `correction-bad-target`), linearity (at most ONE correction per
  target — `correction-ambiguity`; chains legal; cycles malformed ⇒
  needs-owner), severity/route violations REFUSED AT INTAKE as
  `correction-severity-decrease` / `correction-route-mismatch` (never
  graph-then-unclean); (2) link effectivization — raw intermediate
  links REPLACED, not composed; each member judged only by its OWN
  effective link vs the effective survivor; intermediate raw failure
  never propagates (the member whose own link fails is itself UNCLEAN);
  traversal is transitive and explicit over BOTH edge kinds (visit-once;
  a repeat = the step-4 cycle case ⇒ needs-owner); (3) per-member rows
  applied in ascending closed-member ULID order via the §14.12.2 r4
  chain table; (4) fixed point + cycle rules. LIVE TIP = the unique
  member NOT closed by `rejected-refuted` — the SAME definition as the
  §14.10.2 lineage rules (v23 R5-C16-3: v22's register row said "not
  closed by `rejected-duplicate`/`superseded`", contradicting the body;
  these are DISTINCT roles). EFFECTIVE LIVE TIP (v24 R5-C17-1 — the
  live tip may ITSELF be terminalized: A refuted, B = correctionOf:A,
  B closed `rejected-duplicate`/`superseded` onto C ⇒ B is the live tip
  by definition but holds no row of its own): consumers resolve a
  terminalized live tip FORWARD along its own duplicate/superseded
  edge to its EFFECTIVE SURVIVOR (transitively, VISIT-ONCE: the walk
  shares the step-4 fold's cycle machinery — a repeat visit IS the
  step-4 cycle case ⇒ NO effective tip is returned and the consumer
  takes the needs-owner path, the same result as the fold itself;
  v25 R5-C18-4: v24 asserted "chains are acyclic so the walk
  terminates", but the fold ADMITS malformed cyclic prefixes (A→B→A),
  and an assertion is not an algorithm — termination is now DERIVED
  from the visit-once rule, with the cyclic case routed, not
  assumed away); the EFFECTIVE LIVE TIP is that survivor. EVERY
  consumer (duplicate resolution, r4 rows, no-live-tip branch trigger)
  binds the EFFECTIVE live tip, never the raw one; a member
  terminalized by duplicate/superseded is never itself an effective
  tip and always delegates its row outcome via step-2 link
  effectivization. Duplicates resolve to the effective live tip's row
  outcome. TOTAL no-live-tip branch:
  resolution runs through the TIP-MOST member T — a valid T refutation
  AND D's link machine-checked against **T's** repro (earlier-member
  digests never check against the corrected tip); owner-authorized
  links ⇒ UNCLEAN; fail-closed default. *Applies:* duplicate/
  supersession accounting, r4 chain-closure table. *Expansion:*
  §14.10.2 lineage-fold paragraph. *Cited at:* r4 chain table rows,
  vectors (b)/(c)/(d).
- **NDR-o — Drift-resolution op (binds the refusal, not just the
  act).** `{refusedActId, refusalRecordId, outcome:"refiled"|
  "withdrawn", newActId|null}` — `refusalRecordId` is REQUIRED: it names
  the LOG RECORD ID of the refusal being resolved; MUST resolve in-log
  to a refusal record of `refusedActId` whose condition is CURRENTLY
  LIVE (a VALID, terminal-by-refusal refusal — replay checks its
  class-validated re-derivation stands), and MUST NOT name a refusal
  already cleared by an earlier resolution or superseded as
  fault-INVALID (those are excluded from the resolution target by
  definition). The live terminal-by-refusal refusal of an act, if any,
  is UNIQUE at every prefix (a re-adjudication replaces the act's
  terminality), so liveness is deterministic. Dedup key:
  `(refusedActId, refusalRecordId)` — a post-R2 resolution is
  admissible; R1's resolution never binds R2. `refiled` requires
  newActId naming a LATER `audit-filing` act whose filing SUCCEEDED
  (replay-derived `effectApplied == true`) AND whose filed header
  `claim` equals the refused act's payload `claim` (equality per NDR-c);
  `withdrawn` closes the need with no filing. *Applies:*
  `filing-drift-resolution` op, both disposition copies. *Expansion:*
  §14.10.3 op entry. *Cited at:* effect fold, §14.12.2 O row, R2
  terminality clause.
- **NDR-p — Reopening edges: exactly two, jointly exhaustive.** Closed
  finding states admit exactly TWO named reopening edges: (1) the minor
  owner-exception `accepted-fix` (per NDR-b) over a `rejected-duplicate`
  **OR `superseded`** closure (v23 R5-C16-2: the canonical text said
  `rejected-duplicate` ONLY — contradicting its OWN registered expansion
  (§14.10.2, v11 R5-C5-4) and the ratified v10/v11 behavior: `superseded`
  members reach the same held state when their link fails revalidation,
  so a `rejected-duplicate`-only cure stranded them with no exit; the
  register restates the ratified rule, it adds none); (2) the
  strand cure — an OWNER act appending
  `closed-residual` (owner authority, severity-agnostic, no repro
  operand) over a finding closed `rejected-duplicate`/`superseded` IFF
  its §14.12.2 r4 chain-closure evaluation CURRENTLY fires
  UNCLEAN+needs-owner for one of exactly TWO survivor-side strands
  (v24 R5-C17-3 folded further by v25 R5-C18-1: the v24 text kept the
  v15 withdrawal-only IFF inline AND appended a closed two-strand list
  contradicting it — this canonical sentence now states the predicate
  over the closed list, adding no behavior the v24 list did not):
  **(a)** its survivor was owner-retired-by-withdrawal (the original
  v15 case) — evidence MUST cite the disposition record AND the
  survivor's finding id; **(b)** its survivor was closed
  `rejected-refuted` with a VALID refutation (per NDR-s) while the
  member's own link is owner-authorized (non-machine-checkable), so
  the r4 refuted row fires UNCLEAN for the member and NO minor
  exception applies (non-minor member — the minor case keeps edge (1))
  — evidence MUST cite the survivor's finding id AND the survivor's
  `reproRunRef`; validation fails closed per strand (no live strand
  proof ⇒ edge refused, closure untouched). Any other UNCLEAN cause —
  e.g. a damaged survivor with an OPEN fault — does NOT take this edge
  (it clears with its fault).** Both edges are FORWARD-ONLY (verdicts
  frozen). EVERY OTHER transition over ANY closed state remains
  invalid — no third edge (v12's one-edge wording was superseded by
  this two-edge set, not contradicted). *Applies:* `audit-finding-update`
  over closed findings, r4 chain table. *Expansion:* §14.10.2
  closed-state paragraph. *Cited at:* §14.10.2 update-intake rule, r4
  rows.
- **NDR-q — needs-owner clearing: no orphan holds.** Every uncleanness
  / needs-owner condition named anywhere in §14.10/§14.12.2 names its
  CLOSING act or transition and its clearing evidence: unresolved
  filing-refusal conditions close via a conforming `filing-drift-
  resolution` naming the live refusal (per NDR-o); integrity faults
  close via `filing-integrity-disposition` (the disposition record IS
  the clearing evidence, per NDR-m); `quiesce-stall` closes when the
  stalled condition drains; a hold closes via its named disposition.
  A hold with no expressible closing route must itself be made
  expressible or fail closed — an enumeration that leaves a hold with
  no exit is a contract defect (this is the invariant every round-4
  cycle-2 fix class enforced: no state may be both permanent and
  owed-with-no-route). **Per-condition closing inventory (v23
  R5-C16-8 — totality is now SUPPLIED, not asserted; every reachable
  §14.10/§14.12.2 needs-owner/unclean condition, its closing act,
  validation operands, clearing evidence, and forward effect):**
  | condition | closing act | validation operands | clearing evidence | forward effect |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | filing refusal unresolved (`owner-filing-draft-drift` / `owner-filing-mapping`) | `filing-drift-resolution` (per NDR-o) | `refusedActId` = the live refusal's act; refiled binds a later APPLIED `audit-filing` | the conforming resolution record | act terminal; refiled ⇒ new finding, withdrawn ⇒ none |
  | integrity fault, any `failingCheck` kind (per NDR-g/h) | `filing-integrity-disposition` (per NDR-m) | `faultId`; `outcome:"refiled"→newActId` binds equal-claim APPLIED filing; `"withdrawn"` always admissible | the disposition record IS the clearing evidence | fault disposed; damaged bytes stay invalid |
  | r4 chain UNCLEAN — survivor retired by withdrawal | NDR-p edge (2) strand (a): owner `closed-residual` | live strand proof: survivor id + disposition record cite | both citations in the update's authority | finding closed residual, verdicts frozen |
  | r4 chain UNCLEAN — owner-authorized link that cannot machine-check (vector (d)) | minor: owner minor-exception `accepted-fix` (per NDR-b, over `rejected-duplicate` OR `superseded` per NDR-p edge (1)); non-minor: owner `closed-residual` per NDR-p edge (2) strand (b) (v24 R5-C17-3 — the edge's strand proof is the survivor's valid refutation + the member's owner-authorized link; v23's bare "authority REQUIRED" prescribed a transition NDR-p refused) | NDR-b predicate / edge-(2) strand (b) proof: survivor id + its `reproRunRef` | the owner act itself (act-bound, not run-bound) + the two strand citations | finding closed forward-only; chain row re-derives |
  | `residual-inherited` chain member (any severity, v24 R5-C17-7 — the closed member inherits an owner-accepted `closed-residual` survivor; §14.12.2: the round carrying it is unclean until settlement, forward-only) | TWO-PHASE residual-cure protocol per NDR-u (canonical, v27 R5-C19-1 — the protocol body now has a register owner; NDR-q maps, restates nothing; §14.10.3 is its declared expansion. v25 R5-C18-3: act `residual-cure` binds `{findingId, survivorId, route, commitment}`, then the supervisor settles with `residual-cure-settlement` once the evidence exists — the v24 row's single-record form demanded evidence at confirmation time and was unexecutable) | act operands `findingId` + `survivorId` naming the SURVIVOR's owner-accepted residual disposition (refused if never owner-accepted; a second unsettled cure on the same pair refused — no forked cure); commitment `{digest,preimage}` re-digest + evidence check (§14.10.3) at settlement | the `residual-cure-settlement` record (green repro-run or filed finding passing the §14.10.3 single evidence check against the commitment preimage) | member clears for boundaries AFTER the settlement; earlier boundaries keep their state; current round unclean until settled |
  | **locked-pair: confirmed cure whose commitment can never be satisfied (v27 R5-C19-5 — the immutable commitment + no-forked-cure rule left NO exit: a corrected cure was refused while the broken one stood unsettled forever)** | `residual-cure-cancel {cureActId}` (owner op per NDR-u (4): REQUIRED target CONFIRMED + UNSETTLED + not already cancelled; refused `cure-already-settled`/`cure-unknown-act`/`cure-already-cancelled`) | the cancellation record (act-bound, supervisor-stamped authority) | the cancelled cure becomes terminal-by-cancellation (per NDR-l), its derived settlement id permanently vacated; the pair becomes RE-ELIGIBLE for a fresh `residual-cure` once no un-cancelled unsettled cure remains | owner re-confirms with a corrected commitment; the pair's uncleanliness persists UNCLEAN + needs-owner across the gap exactly as before any cure existed |
  | `quiesce-stall` | no act — drains when the stalled condition clears | stall condition re-check at next boundary | drain record appended | boundary proceeds |
  | `finding-hold` | `finding-hold-lift` (owner record, §14.12.4) | `findingId` of the held finding | the lift record | hold stops counting as sign-off holder |
  A recorded uncleanness on a CLOSED cycle is historical (verdict
  evidence), NOT a hold: only OPEN-cycle conditions above are holds
  requiring a route. An unlisted reachable hold is a contract defect →
  fail closed and register the missing row (this row-set is re-checked
  by every cycle audit against the condition sites it cites).
  *Applies:* all of §14.10/§14.12.2. *Expansion:*
  (none — self-contained; each listed condition's ACT body lives at
  its own NDR's expansion — the inventory maps, it restates nothing.
  v27 R5-C19-1: the cure rows map to **NDR-u** (protocol canonical)
  with its §14.10.3 expansion, and the cure act's class membership to
  **NDR-v**; the v26 claim that these bodies lived at "their own NDR's
  expansion" was FALSE for the cure protocol — no entry declared it —
  and is now made true by NDR-u/NDR-v.)
  *Cited at:* register doctrine 2
  (completeness check), cycle-16 audit prompt.
- **NDR-r — Filing identity, replay, and re-filing over identical bytes.**
  Three distinct cases, never collapsed: (1) REDELIVERY of the same act
  (same act id AND effect id) is idempotent — replay recognizes the
  already-applied effect, consumes nothing new, appends nothing new
  (general single-consumption rule applied to filings). (2) A NEW
  confirmed act over identical draft bytes is a NEW filing ATTEMPT with
  a NEW effect id: it is NEVER refused as duplicate INTENT — duplicate
  intent is not a validation concept — but is FULLY subject to every
  ordinary intake rule on its own content (success ⇒ a SEPARATE
  `audit-finding` record, conditional on intake per NDR-l; failure ⇒
  refusal record + terminal-by-refusal per NDR-d/l; e.g. a resubmitted
  correction draft is refused `correction-ambiguity` by lineage
  linearity per NDR-n). (3) Same act id with DIVERGENT bytes is
  refused (replay-integrity — THIS entry is the rule's owner: a
  confirmed act's bytes are pinned by its `draftSha256` payload and
  re-digest-checked on every redelivery; NDR-i governs only the
  WITHDRAWAL stage of an `intake-refusal` fault and is NOT the
  authority here — v24 R5-C17-2). Spool dedup is
  STORAGE dedup and has no disposition meaning; two successful filings
  of identical bytes are distinct findings dispositioned as such (any
  `rejected-duplicate` link is the normal path). *Applies:*
  `audit-filing` replay, intake, spool. *Expansion:* §14.10.3
  "Identical bytes ≠ identical filing" paragraph. *Cited at:*
  filing-replay paragraph, spool paragraphs, §14.12.2 effect fold.
- **NDR-s — Refutation evidence rule.** CLOSED THREE-VALUE RESULT
  SEMANTICS (v25 R5-C18-2: v24's §14.12.2 demotion cited this entry
  for semantics it did not state — the definitions live HERE now;
  §14.12.4's field list is the registered expansion): `green` = the
  repro command completed and `postFixExpected` was OBSERVED (supports
  `accepted-fix`); `red` = the repro command completed and
  `postFixExpected` was NOT observed (supports NOTHING — evidence of
  a failed fix, recorded for the trail); `not-reproduced` = the repro
  command ran to COMPLETION against the finding's PRE-FIX
  BASELINE and the behavior `preFixObserved` claims did NOT occur
  (supports `rejected-refuted` ONLY). `rejected-refuted` NEVER
  consumes `green`/`red`; `accepted-fix` NEVER consumes
  `not-reproduced`/`red`. `rejected-refuted` requires a named re-run
  with `result:"not-reproduced"` (§14.12.4 amendment: the PRE-FIX
  BASELINE is the round manifest's `targetDigest` for the finding's
  cycle where one exists, else the episode policy `baseCommit`), with
  `executedArtifactDigest` equal to that baseline, and the standard
  `findingId`+`reproRunRef` binding. A run on a tree already containing
  the fix tests the fix, NOT the claim: REFUTATION-INVALID. A run that
  did not complete (crash/timeout/harness error/environment mismatch)
  is NO RECORD and no evidence of anything. Refutation is owner-grade:
  orchestrator-originated refutation is valid ONLY via a
  trusted-gate/supervisor-authored run meeting ALL of the above; it is
  the ONLY disposition closing a finding without acceptance or fix, so
  its evidence bar is the highest in the enum; a refuted run's evidence never
  discharges a duplicate of a corrected claim (no-cross-lineage
  discharge — OWNED HERE, v27 R5-C19-3: the v26 text cited NDR-n for
  this clause but NDR-n does not state it; the rule now lives in THIS
  entry); refutation
  is repro-gated exactly like filing, and a wrong refutation is
  corrected only via the `correctionOf` lineage (per NDR-n), never by
  touching the closed record. *Applies:* `rejected-refuted` updates,
  repro-run records, r4 refuted row. *Expansion:* §14.10.2
  "What counts as a refuting run" paragraph AND the §14.12.4
  `repro-run` record field list (v25 R5-C18-2: the three-value
  result definitions are owned HERE; §14.12.2's result-semantics
  site is a citation). *Cited at:* §14.10.2
  rejected-refuted bullet, r4 chain table refuted row, §14.12.2 r4
  rule.
- **NDR-t — Field validity and artifact immutability.** (1) Closed
  vocabularies: any unknown value in a wire field makes the record
  INVALID — the receiver refuses the line and surfaces it, never
  silently drops it. (2) `route` is the ONLY routing field
  (`code-fix` → implementation loop, `human-review` → owner ledger);
  `surface:"spec"` with `route:"code-fix"` is INVALID at intake (a fix
  whose subject is the spec edits the spec); a `code-fix` record
  failing a G2 norm check is refused at intake with the `refusal-code`
  journaled as an S5 decision-log record naming the refused line's
  content hash (the line never becomes an `audit-finding`; a corrected
  resubmission is a NEW record next cycle). (3) The `findingRef`
  artifact is **append-only after filing**: `claimDigest` is
  supervisor-computed at intake over the artifact bytes (plain sha256 —
  evidence, not policy); consumers re-hash at check time and refuse a
  mismatch (`finding-artifact-drift`); an edit (correction, retraction)
  is a NEW findingRef + NEW `audit-finding` with the old record
  `superseded` — legal ONLY while the old record is OPEN (a transition
  onto a CLOSED finding is refused; v24 R5-C17-9 qualification: the
  named closed-record route `correctionOf` per NDR-n serves a wrong
  REFUTATION and admits ONLY targets closed by `rejected-refuted`
  (target predicate `correction-bad-target`) — it is NOT a general
  correction route for closed records; every other closed record is
  untouchable except via NDR-p's two named reopening edges). *Applies:* intake validation, artifact
  lifecycle. *Expansion:* §14.10.1 field-rules block (`route`×`surface`
  bullet + `claimDigest`/artifact bullet). *Cited at:* §14.10.1 wire
  comments, intake paragraphs, G2 gate description.
- **NDR-u — Two-phase residual cure: canonical protocol.** The COMPLETE
  lifecycle of curing a `residual-inherited` chain member is canonical
  HERE (v27 R5-C19-1 — v26 stated the protocol only at §14.10.3,
  unregistered, while NDR-q's inventory pointed at it claiming each
  listed act body lives at "its own NDR's expansion" — none did):
  (1) CONFIRMATION — the owner act `residual-cure` binds
  `{findingId, survivorId, route, commitment}` where `commitment` is
  the RE-CHECKABLE PAIR `{digest, preimage}` (per-route CLOSED preimage
  shape, §14.10.3 expansion; confirmation validates
  `sha256(preimage) == digest` AND the shape parse — a violation is
  `cure-commitment-malformed`, refused — and resolves
  `reproDigestOrNull` by the deterministic rule over the survivor's
  closure); the commitment is IMMUTABLE.
  (2) UNIQUENESS — at most ONE unsettled, UN-cancelled cure per
  `(findingId, survivorId)` pair; a second on the pair is refused
  (no forked cure).
  (3) SETTLEMENT — the supervisor appends `residual-cure-settlement`
  under the deterministic id `cure-settlement-<cureActId>` (the
  id-collision refusal IS the one-settlement-per-act guarantee); the
  SOLE clearing condition is the SINGLE EVIDENCE CHECK (v28 R5-C20-1
  — this paragraph OWNS the complete predicate; the §14.10.3 expansion
  supplies clause-level detail and may not weaken it). `accepted-fix`
  = a green `repro-run` whose definition re-digests to the committed
  `reproDigest` AND the THREE-CONJUNCT ORDERING WITNESS: (b1) the
  durable git ancestry walk (ancestor-of-connected from
  `expectedFixBaseline`, ≠ baseline, walked ONCE at settlement-append
  against the pinned gated lineage; missing/pruned/unverifiable closure
  FAILS CLOSED), recorded as the settlement's `ancestryWitness` field;
  REPRO DIGEST (v29 R5-C21-8, from the cycle-4 audit — one operation for
  every site: the committed `reproDigest`/`reproDigestOrNull`, the
  finding-side digest, and the run-side digest): `reproDigest(F)` =
  `"sha256:" + hex( SHA-256( tre-canonical-json/1 bytes of F.repro ) )`,
  where `F.repro` is the finding's `repro` object exactly as stored
  (the closed key set `{kind, command, preFixObserved, postFixExpected}`;
  bookkeeping fields excluded; `repro.kind:"none"` has NO digest). A
  `repro-run` names its DEFINITION by `findingId`: the run's `reproDigest`
  must equal `reproDigest(F)` of THAT finding — for EVERY run that names
  a finding with a non-`none` repro (ordinary history and refutation
  included). The SETTLEMENT commitment equality is scoped separately
  (v30 cycle-9 audit, finding 2): it applies ONLY where a cure
  settlement cites the run as its `evidenceRef` (accepted-fix), where
  the run's digest must also equal the cure's committed `reproDigest`;
  a run no settlement cites has no settlement commitment to satisfy,
  and none is required. Fresh-finding-cycle settlements compare the
  finding's committed `reproDigestOrNull` instead. One operation,
  `reproDigest(F)`, governs every site; key order and whitespace are
  not operands (the canonicalizer fixes them).
  (b2) the run record's S5-log position is AFTER the cure act; (b3)
  the run's DURABLE CURE BINDING (v28 R5-C20-2 — the run must be the
  post-confirmation execution the cure authorized; the mechanism is
  the pre-execution gate defined in §14.10.3 and the binding field
  `cureGateId` on `repro-run`). Ancestry alone and log position alone
  are each NOT a temporal proof (v27 R5-C19-4). `fresh-finding-cycle`
  = APPLIED filing whose `claimDigest` re-digests to the committed
  `claimDigest` AND whose `cureActRef` names the cure act (identity
  checked at intake, state checked here) AND — when the committed
  `reproDigestOrNull` is non-null — whose repro re-digests to it (a
  null commits no digest and none may be invented). Replay recomputes
  ONLY durable operands and consumes the stored `ancestryWitness`; a
  replay NEVER re-walks a git graph.
  (4) CANCELLATION — the owner op `residual-cure-cancel {cureActId}`
  on a cure that is confirmed, UNSETTLED and NOT ALREADY CANCELLED
  (refused otherwise: `cure-already-settled` / `cure-unknown-act` /
  `cure-already-cancelled`); the cancelled act becomes
  TERMINAL-BY-CANCELLATION (per NDR-l), its derived settlement id is
  PERMANENTLY VACATED (any later settlement record bearing it is
  malformed, refused — cancellation beats evidence, fail-closed), and
  the pair becomes RE-ELIGIBLE for a fresh cure. Conformance vector
  (v28 R5-C20P-3 — stranded-queue exit: cure drains, owner cancels
  before evidence, finalization must quiesce): a drained
  `residual-cure` act followed by its validated cancel record passes
  P3 on the cancellation record's account (no owed settlement), the
  boundary is the residual's own UNCLEAN + needs-owner boundary, and
  the later fresh cure on the pair settles the pair normally.
  (5) NO-HOLD / NEVER-CLEAN — an unsettled cure adds NO hold beyond
  the residual-inherited uncleanliness it exists to clear, and while
  unsettled NEVER YIELDS A CLEAN boundary (v29 G1-V29-C6-2, from the
  cycle-6 audit: v28 said "NEVER finalizes its round", which a literal
  reader read as blocking the boundary APPEND — contradicted by NDR-v
  and the §14.12.2 O row, which both prescribe that the round's
  boundary while unsettled is APPENDED as UNCLEAN + needs-owner; the
  exclusion bars only the CLEAN verdict, never the append); settlement
  is owed by EVIDENCE ARRIVAL, never by supervisor effort — class
  membership of the unsettled act (and of the owed `cure-gate`
  completion): NDR-v.
  *Applies:* every cure site, NDR-q inventory, §14.12.2 chain rule,
  envelope record-kind inventory. *Expansion:* §14.10.3
  `residual-cure` / `residual-cure-settlement` / `residual-cure-cancel`
  entries (clause-level detail: preimage shapes, the full evidence
  check text, refusal operands) and the §14.10.1 `cureActRef`
  field-rule block (v27 R5-C19-3: wire operand + intake validation
  of the settlement route's lineage check); v28 R5-C20-2/3: the
  `cure-gate` record (`{id, cureActId, nonce}`), the `repro-run`
  `cureGateId` field with its nullability rule, and the settlement's
  `ancestryWitness` closed shape — the three-conjunct accepted-fix
  ordering witness is OWNED by this entry's paragraph (3); the
  expansion supplies the record shapes AND their append, recovery,
  and binding clauses (dispatch gating, one-per-act, owed-completion
  complete-the-pair, cancelled/settled extinguishment) and may not
  weaken the ordering-witness predicate that paragraph (3) owns (v29
  R5-C21-3: the v28 text said "shapes only", contradicting the manifest
  row, which assigns the clauses to the expansion). *Cited at:* NDR-q inventory rows (residual-inherited +
  locked-pair), NDR-v, §14.12.2, statement-site manifest.
- **NDR-v — Effect-binding exceptions: CLOSED set + caller sweep.**
  An act may LEGALLY hold `effectApplied:false` without being class B
  ONLY in the named CLOSED exception set: (1) a filing-class act whose
  intake appends a PERMANENT refusal (per NDR-d/NDR-l — the refusal IS
  the effect appended, terminal-by-refusal; its unresolved refusal
  CONDITION is the class-O item, per NDR-m/NDR-o); (2) a confirmed,
  UNSETTLED, UN-cancelled `residual-cure` act per NDR-u — its effect
  is the derived id `cure-settlement-<cureActId>`, absent until
  evidence arrival: NEITHER `effectApplied:true` NOR class B NOR a
  quiescence item NOR a quiesce-stall candidate, and the
  boundary the round gets while it is unsettled is the
  residual-inherited UNCLEAN + needs-owner boundary UNCHANGED.
  The exclusion covers the act IN EVERY UNSETTLED STATE — including
  the crash-window state whose `cure-gate` is still OWED (§14.10.3
  recovery): the owed gate completion shares its parent act's
  classification and is NEVER ITSELF a B item, quiescence item, or
  stall candidate (v29 G1-V29-C6-1, from the cycle-6 audit — v28
  justified the exclusion with "no supervisor-owed work exists", which
  the owed-completion clause contradicts; the correct statement is
  that the owed gate completion is recovery-pass work, not drain
  work: the restarted supervisor runs the recovery pass BEFORE
  evaluating any boundary or accepting any new append, so no boundary
  is ever evaluated against a prefix with an unrestored owed gate,
  while the settlement effect remains owed by evidence arrival, not
  supervisor effort).
  **CALLER SWEEP (v27 R5-C19-2):** the exclusion governs EVERY
  consumer of the effect fold — the general effect fold, the §14.12.2
  B row, the queue P3 predicate, the drain act→effect same-section
  rule, and the quiesce-stall rule — each carrying the exclusion by
  named citation to THIS entry; a consumer that classifies an
  exception act as class B from its own text is a DEFECT, corrected to
  a citation (v26 stated the exception at the effect-binding paragraph
  only and four callers contradicted it — one prefix, two
  classifications). The set is disjoint from the integrity-fault
  exclusion (terminal-by-damage, per NDR-h/NDR-l) and from
  terminal-by-cancellation (per NDR-l, reached via NDR-u).
  *Applies:* effect fold, §14.12.2 B/O rows, queue protocol
  predicates, stall rule. *Expansion:* §14.10.3 effect-binding
  paragraph (exception list + sweep text) and the consumer-site
  exclusion clauses (§14.12.2 B row, queue P3 predicate, drain
  NAMED DEFERRED-EFFECT EXCUSE, authorized-effect-stall paragraph).
  *Cited at:* B row, P3, drain, stall rule, NDR-u, statement-site
  manifest.
