**Trust assumptions (v28 R5-C20F-5 — declared basis, owner-adopted;
narrowing any TA is owner territory. A finding that an enforcement
rests on TA-n is ANSWERED HERE, not re-found; every enforcement site
cites its TA).**
- **TA-1 Ledger integrity:** every cited record ref resolves to a
  durable append-only log entry; appended entries are never removed
  or reordered.
- **TA-2 Runner trust:** the gate/run runner (`trusted-gate`, or the
  supervisor where this section allows supervisor-authored runs)
  executes the repro against the intended candidate and records
  `runEvidenceRef` content honestly — including the honest echo of
  the gate nonce (the nonce itself is MINTED by the supervisor — at
  confirmation, or at owed-completion recovery per §14.10.3 — never by
  the runner; the runner's trust obligation is the echo). The
  ledger provides durability and after-the-fact verifiability (the
  nonce-containment check works against the durable gate record);
  it does NOT authenticate an untrusted producer, and no claim in
  this section depends on doing so.
- **TA-3 Git-object honesty:** the object store reachable from
  `expectedFixBaseline` and the candidate contains the objects the
  run actually tested; a forged object store is outside the git
  witness's scope (b1, §14.10.3).
- **TA-4 Preimage availability:** the cure `commitment`'s
  `{digest, preimage}` pair (§14.10.3) and every digest re-checked
  against a stored preimage remain re-checkable for the ledger's
  retention horizon.
- **TA-5 Log-atomicity scope:** S5 is single-writer, ordered, and
  append-only, but NOT transactional across (log append, external
  dispatch) or across multi-record pairs: a crash can tear a pair.
  Any mechanism relying on a pair MUST declare its recovery
  direction (example: §14.10.3 cure-gate complete-the-pair,
  D1=A) and MUST NOT claim "same critical section" atomicity the
  log cannot deliver.

#### 14.10.1 `audit-finding` — wire shape

One JSONL line per finding. Common envelope
`{schema:"tre-supervisor/1", id, ts, episodeId}` (taskId optional — a
finding may name the contract, not a task). `id` is **supervisor-minted
at intake: fresh conforming ULID (F55/F56 precedent), collision-
refused; caller-suggested ids are test-only** (R7). A finding record is
immutable and starts `open` — **it carries no disposition field**; all
state changes flow through `audit-finding-update` (§14.10.2).

```jsonc
{ "kind":"audit-finding", "id":"01J…ULID", "ts":1730231300000,
  "schema":"tre-supervisor/1", "episodeId":"…", "taskId":"t2",   // taskId optional
  "cycle":4,                          // episode-wide round that produced it (v5 R2-5: numbering is G3's, post-close audits are later cycles)
  "origin":"auditor | owner",         // v5 R2-2: who produced the finding (see below)
  "producer":{ "endpoint":"…", "model":"gpt-6.1-terra", "sessionId":"…" },  // v5: renamed from `auditor` — it names whichever session produced the finding, owner audit included
  "ownerActRef":null,                 // v7 R4-C1-2: nullability per ENTRY MODE (see the entry-mode table in 14.10.1): REQUIRED non-null in owner-act mode, null in auditor-intake AND supervisor-derived modes
  "originRef":null,                   // v7 R4-C1-2: REQUIRED {origin:"intake",receiptId} in auditor-intake mode (14.12.4 c4-B2 binding); REQUIRED {origin:"supervisor-derived",fromRefusalId} in supervisor-derived mode; null in owner-act mode (ownerActRef is that record's entry proof)
  "correctionOf":null,                // v6 F1: REQUIRED non-null findingId only for the owner re-filing that corrects a WRONG refutation (rule in 14.10.2); REQUIRED null otherwise
  "route":"code-fix | human-review",               // THE routing field (R1-B)
  "surface":"code | test | doc | spec",            // artifact domain (R1-B)
  "severity":"blocker | major | minor",
  "verdictBasis":"repro | evidence-only | opinion",
  "claim":"…",                        // bounded summary, ≤2000 chars, single line
  "claimDigest":"sha256:…",           // v5 R2-4: supervisor-computed at intake over the findingRef artifact's bytes (binding rule below)
  "findingRef":"findings/f-0061.md",  // REQUIRED: full-prose artifact in the episode dir (R5-A)
  "scopeRefs":["src/runner/attempt.ts"],  // G5 (§14.14.1): repo-relative paths/#anchors; [] = unscoped, serial
  "repro":{ "kind":"probe|fixture|session-log|none", "command":"…",
            "preFixObserved":"…", "postFixExpected":"…" },
  "evidenceRefs":["sessions/t2.jsonl#<entryId>"],  // ≥1 required
  "cureActRef":null,                  // v27 R5-C19-3 REQUIRED PRESENT (may be null; source: draft header, via act payload in owner-act mode — v28 R5-C20P-2) — the DURABLE lineage operand for the `fresh-finding-cycle` cure settlement route (NDR-u (3)): a filed finding curing a residual names the `residual-cure` ACT's record id here (intake checks IDENTITY only over the intake-validation prefix — resolves to a `residual-cure` act record, v28; confirmed/unsettled/not-cancelled is a SETTLEMENT-prefix check, F5); null = the finding is no cure evidence; a settlement citing a finding whose `cureActRef` is null or names a different or non-evidence-eligible (settled/cancelled) act is REFUSED (counterexample: a claim-matching finding with a purported prose citation and null `cureActRef` cannot settle a cure)
  "affectedNorm":{ "doc":"docs/21-p9-m3-…", "anchor":"§1.1 (c) step (2)",
                   "sha256":null }                 // or null (R6)
}
```

Field rules (closed vocabularies; an unknown value makes the record
invalid — the receiver refuses the line and surfaces it, never silently
drops it):

- **`cureActRef` (v27 R5-C19-3; intake/settlement split v28 R5-C20P-5: the v27 wire comment demanded confirmed+unsettled at intake
  while the field rule deferred that state to settlement).**
  REQUIRED to be PRESENT (value may be
  null): the durable lineage operand of the `fresh-finding-cycle` cure
  settlement route (per NDR-u (3)) — a finding filed as cure evidence
  names the `residual-cure` act's record id; a non-null value is
  validated at INTAKE for identity only — it must resolve in-log
  over the intake-validation prefix to a `residual-cure` act record
  (unknown id or non-cure act ⇒ the line is refused,
  `cure-unknown-act`); CONFIRMED + UNSETTLED + NOT-CANCELLED is a
  SETTLEMENT-prefix check (the target act's state at settlement
  time), not an intake check. A finding naming an already-settled
  or already-cancelled cure is a conforming finding that settles
  nothing — a settlement citing it is refused. This is the ONLY
  encoding of cure lineage — a prose or evidenceRefs citation
  settles nothing.
- **`route` × `surface` (R1-B).** `route` is the ONLY field the
  orchestrator routes on: `code-fix` re-enters the implementation loop;
  `human-review` goes to the owner ledger (G2's norm state — out of
  scope here). G2 (v2) does NOT re-route records — it gates intake: a
  `code-fix` record failing a G2 norm check is **refused at intake**
  (`refusal-code` journaled as an S5 decision-log record naming the
  refused line's content hash — the line never becomes an
  `audit-finding`, so the auditor's immutability rule is untouched;
  a corrected resubmission is a NEW record in the next cycle), and any
  G2 blocker or
  stale-norm situation is filed by the SUPERVISOR as its own
  `human-review` record. One mutable record never overrides another's
  route. `surface` (the R5 round's proven vocabulary) records
  where the defect lives: `code | test | doc | spec`. Intake rule:
  `surface:"spec"` with `route:"code-fix"` is **invalid** — a fix whose
  substance is changing ratified norm text cannot self-route into a
  code cycle; everything else may pair freely (a TEST-major is
  normally `route:code-fix, surface:test`).
- `severity` — the repo's blocker/major/minor audit vocabulary.
  **Minors never hold a sign-off by themselves; the owner decides
  whether any given minor holds** — escalation is a recorded
  `finding-hold` record (14.12.4, `dispositionBy:"owner"`,
  TTY-confirmed; v4 — supersedes v1's "audit-finding-update" wording,
  which predated the hold record kind; R4).
- `verdictBasis` — records that a finding reproduced against pre-fix
  behavior outranks one argued from reading. Whether an `opinion`-basis
  finding may hold a sign-off open is a **convergence** question:
  §14.10 supplies the basis, **G3 owns enforcement** (R8).
- `claim` — bounded single-line summary (S5 record discipline); the
  full finding (location, scenario, fix direction — real findings run
  to several hundred words) lives in `findingRef` (R5-A). The episode
  layout (S4) gains `findings/` accordingly; this section amends S4 by
  adding that directory — file naming within it is open, log-line
  machine-checkability is not.
- `repro` — required (`kind` ≠ `none`) when `route:"code-fix"` AND
  `severity` ≠ minor: an unfalsifiable blocker/major is refused at
  intake (`finding-intake-invalid`). Lesson of record: a claim the next
  cycle cannot re-run wastes a full cycle (p9m3 findings fresh every
  cycle through 4). **Acceptance contract (R4; qualified v9 R4-C3-7 —
  v8's unconditional sentence refused what §14.10.2/§14.12.2's minor
  owner exception declares valid): a transition to `accepted-fix` is
  only meaningful if the finding's repro was re-run against
  `postFixExpected` and observed green — EXCEPT the minor owner
  exception (minor + dispositionBy:owner + riding a
  finding-disposition act + non-empty matching reason + **`reproRunRef
  == null` — v12 R5-C6-4, predicate completed here too: the exception
  applies ONLY where no run reference is attached; a NON-null
  reference must pass the ordinary green-run validation regardless of
  owner reason (the consumer rule §14.12.2 refuses an invalid
  non-null run identically — the exception excuses the ABSENCE of a
  run, never a bad one)**), where the
  binding evidence is the owner act itself (act-bound, not
  run-bound). No other null-evidence accepted-fix exists.**
  Enforcement of that
  check belongs to the consumer (G2/G3); this section pins its
  semantics.
- `evidenceRefs` — ≥1 session-log or decision-log entry id. Forensics
  rule (D-round): the orchestrator's own echoes are not evidence.
- `origin` + `producer` (v5 R2-2; `producer` is the additive rename of
  v4's `auditor` — the field names whichever session produced the
  finding, and the trio cannot honestly name an owner audit).
  **The two rules below describe the auditor-intake and owner-act
  modes respectively; supervisor-derived records are governed by the
  entry-mode table ALONE (v9 R4-C3-3 — re-lands C2-5a, dropped by the
  same crashed script: the v7 table permits either origin with a
  derived originRef and a supervisor producer, so unconditional prose
  here read the same record as legal and malformed depending on which
  paragraph a validator applied first).**
  Auditor-intake mode: `origin:"auditor"`: produced by an auditor
  worker via supervisor intake (`producer` = that session);
  `ownerActRef` REQUIRED null. Owner-act mode:
  `origin:"owner"`: produced by an owner-run audit (practice produced
  these on both ends of AUD56 — the AUD55 owner pre-audit findings
  folded at round OPEN, and AUD56's post-close owner audit found
  791b6c3) — it rides the owner-act
  channel (D2/P17, 14.10.3): a TTY owner-act (`op:"audit-filing"`,
  payload below) is appended FIRST, the finding record carries its id
  in `ownerActRef` (the same append-API provenance binding as every
  privileged kind), and `producer` names the owner session where
  known (nullable trio fields when the owner audited outside tre.).
  Without an owning owner-act an `origin:"owner"` line IS MALFORMED —
  **for the owner-act entry mode only (v7 R4-C1-2); the
  supervisor-derived mode (below) is the sole carrier of owner-observed
  findings WITHOUT an owner-act, and that is exactly what its proof
  field attests.** This closes v4's contradiction: §14.10.2's
  reopening rule assumed the owner files findings while v4's emission
  authority let only auditors append them.
- **Entry-mode table (v7 R4-C1-2, supersedes the v6 F3 prose; closes
  v6 F3's residual contradiction — the v6 wire comments and owner rule
  read `origin:"owner"` ⇒ ownerActRef REQUIRED / originRef null
  UNCONDITIONALLY, which made the third mode both permitted and
  malformed in the same section). Nullability is driven by the ENTRY
  MODE, never by `origin` alone. Exactly three modes; a validator
  refuses every other field combination:**
  | mode | origin | originRef | ownerActRef | producer trio |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | auditor intake | `"auditor"` | REQUIRED `{origin:"intake", receiptId}` (§14.12.4 c4-B2 binding) | null | auditor session |
  | owner act | `"owner"` | null | REQUIRED non-null (the `audit-filing` act) | owner audit session, nullable trio for out-of-tre filings |
  | supervisor-derived | `"auditor"` OR `"owner"` (who OBSERVED the defect) | REQUIRED `{origin:"supervisor-derived", fromRefusalId}` | **null (v7: no owner act exists in this mode — v6 said the mode was legal while its prose demanded the act)** | supervisor session (the appender) |
  An owner-act filing is NOT a receipt outcome, so it can never
  violate "every receipt resolves to exactly one outcome", and it is
  absent from `submissionAccounting` by construction (it never entered
  the round queue; quiescence, 14.12.2 step 3, is unaffected — same
  accounting exclusion for supervisor-derived, v7 stated: neither
  non-intake mode enters submissionAccounting; only mode-1 records
  have a receipt and are counted there). The wire-block comments on
  `originRef`/`ownerActRef` defer to THIS table (single normative
  statement; the comments are signposts).
  **Supervisor-derived filings (G2 blockers, human-review records a
  refusal produces, 14.12.4)** are a mode, not a value of `origin`;
  `correctionOf` may only be non-null in the owner-act mode (F1). An owner filing
  whose draft names a defect a receipt already produced is the NORMAL
  duplicate path (new finding + `rejected-duplicate`, owner-act
  channel) — never a re-resolution of a closed receipt.
- `claimDigest` (v5 R2-4) — computed by the SUPERVISOR at intake over
  the `findingRef` artifact's bytes (plain sha256 over the file — the
  artifact is evidence, not policy, so no canonicalizer: re-hashing
  bytes at check time is the check). This binds the machine-checkable
  record to the prose the loop actually adjudicates; without it the
  contract content is mutable after filing and the record attests to
  nothing — demonstrated live in the AUD56 trail fold: finding prose
  rewritten post-commit (the fabricated fourth-pass narrative removed
  before the record stood) — under git that is auditable history,
  under a plain `findings/` dir it would be nothing).
  Companion rule: the artifact is **append-only after filing** — an
  edit (correction, retraction) is a NEW findingRef + a NEW
  `audit-finding` record, the old one `superseded` — legal ONLY while
  the old record is still OPEN (v6: a transition onto a CLOSED finding
  is refused by the 14.10.2 intake rule; the closed-record correction
  route is `correctionOf`, F1); consumers re-hash at check time and
  refuse a mismatch (`finding-artifact-drift`).
- `affectedNorm` (R6) — an OBJECT `{doc, anchor, sha256}` or null
  (null = pure-code finding, no norm implicated). `anchor` is
  free-text locant; `sha256` (digest of the anchored text at reference
  time) is **optional until G2 rules** whether digests are mandatory —
  reserved now while amendment is free. A finding binds AT MOST ONE
  norm; a finding touching several splits into several records (a
  primary `claim` may name the others in prose).

#### 14.10.2 `audit-finding-update` — disposition transitions (R2-A)

The second kind — fully specified here so no lifecycle is ever inferred
from two encodings:

```jsonc
{ "kind":"audit-finding-update", "id":"01J…ULID", "ts":1730231300001,
  "schema":"tre-supervisor/1", "episodeId":"…",
  "findingId":"01J…ULID",             // MUST reference an existing audit-finding id
  "to":"accepted-fix | rejected-refuted | rejected-duplicate | closed-residual | superseded",
  "dispositionBy":"orchestrator | owner",
  "authority":null,                    // REQUIRED non-null for closed-residual (see below)
  "reproRunRef":null,                  // v5 R2-3: REQUIRED non-null for accepted-fix when the finding's severity ≠ minor, and ALWAYS for rejected-refuted (see below)
  "supersedes":null,                   // REQUIRED non-null findingId for rejected-duplicate AND superseded
  "reason":"…" }                       // bounded single line, advisory
```

- No `from` field: current state is derivable by log order (single-
  writer flock discipline, S5). Intake rule: a transition applied to an
  already-closed finding is **invalid** (refused) — reopening requires
  the owner filing or re-filing, never an update chain resurrection.
  **FIRST named exception (v10 R5-C4-7, extended v11 R5-C5-4; the
  TWO-edge set is completed by the strand cure edge below (renamed
  v25 R5-C18-1 — its strand set is a closed list, not withdrawal-only;
  v16 R5-C10-4):** an
  OWNER act (not the orchestrator) may append a minor-owner-exception
  `accepted-fix` (§14.12.2) over a finding closed as
  `rejected-duplicate` OR `superseded` — the chain row's cure for a
  member a machine-checked run cannot reach (e.g. a non-falsifiable
  repro). **v11: `superseded` members reach exactly the same held
  state as `rejected-duplicate` members when their link fails
  revalidation against a refuted/exception-accepted survivor, so the
  cure must name both closures — a v10 exception limited to
  `rejected-duplicate` stranded superseded members with no exit.**
  Validation: the target's current state IS `rejected-duplicate` or
  `superseded`, severity minor, the exception's
  owner-act conditions hold, and the effect is FORWARD-ONLY — it
  re-evaluates LATER boundaries only (survivor-change rule, verdicts
  frozen). **TWO NAMED EDGES JOINTLY EXHAUSTIVE (v12 R5-C6-5 rule
  restated v16 R5-C10-4 over the v15 edge set — v12's "the named
  exception is the ONLY reopening edge" was written when exactly
  one edge existed and is SUPERSEDED by this sentence, not
  contradicting it: v15 added a second named edge below, so the
  exhaustive set is exactly the two named edges — the minor-owner-
  exception `accepted-fix` above and the strand-cure
  `closed-residual` below): EVERY OTHER TRANSITION OVER ANY CLOSED
  STATE REMAINS INVALID — a closed finding accepts no further
  transition of any kind except by one of the two named edges
  (validation of each is local to its own paragraph; an act naming
  neither condition over a closed target is refused), and no third
  edge exists.**
  **SECOND NAMED REOPENING EDGE (v15 R5-C9-1 — stranded-cure;
  strand list extended v24 R5-C17-3 per NDR-p): an OWNER act may
  append `closed-residual` (owner authority REQUIRED — the same
  authority field as any residual acceptance, no repro-run operand,
  severity-agnostic) over a finding closed as
  `rejected-duplicate` OR `superseded` when and only when that
  member's §14.12.2 r4 chain-closure evaluation currently fires
  UNCLEAN + needs-owner because its survivor hit one of the TWO
  closed-list strand kinds: **(a)** owner-retired-by-withdrawal
  (§14.10.3's `filing-integrity-disposition` outcome `withdrawn`) —
  the record MUST cite that disposition record AND the survivor's
  finding id; **(b)** survivor `rejected-refuted` with a VALID
  refutation while the member's OWN link is owner-authorized (per
  NDR-p; the minor case is cured by edge (1) instead) — the record
  MUST cite the survivor's `reproRunRef` AND the survivor's finding
  id; validation fails closed otherwise (no live strand of either
  kind ⇒ the edge is refused, the closure is untouched); Effect: FORWARD-ONLY (verdicts frozen; LATER
  boundaries evaluate the member as owner-`closed-residual` —
  resolved as residual, surfaced at P13, per the r4 residual row —
  never as "closed by any other route" and never UNCLEAN again);
  the two named edges (this one and the v10/v11 minor-exception
  `accepted-fix`) are jointly the COMPLETE reopening edge set —
  no third exists.**
- `closed-residual` records (the old `residual-risk-accepted` class —
  residual acceptance is a DISPOSITION, not a finding class) require
  `authority`: a reference to the accepting owner channel (CLI session,
  ledger line) or a pinned policy clause. An unbacked residual
  transition is invalid.
- `rejected-refuted` (v5 R2-1) records "the claim did not reproduce":
  **`reproRunRef` REQUIRED non-null**, naming the durable `repro-run`
  record whose re-run failed against `preFixObserved`. **What counts
  as a refuting run (v6 F5, G1 review round 3 — v5 said "failed" over
  a `result:"green|red"` enum where neither value names
  non-reproduction, and never said AGAINST WHAT ARTIFACT, so both a
  run on the already-fixed tree and a crashed harness could be read
  as refuting):** the run's `result` MUST be `not-reproduced` (§14.12.4
  record amendment: the repro command ran to COMPLETION against the
  finding's pre-fix baseline and the behavior `preFixObserved` claims
  did NOT occur); `executedArtifactDigest` MUST equal the finding's
  **pre-fix baseline** — the round manifest's `targetDigest` for the
  finding's cycle where one exists, else the episode policy
  `baseCommit` (a refutation run against a tree that already contains
  a fix tests the fix, NOT the claim, and is REFUTATION-INVALID);
  same `findingId` + `reproDigest` binding as every run. A run that
  did not complete (crash, timeout, harness error, environment
  mismatch) is **not evidence of anything** and must never be written
  as a `repro-run` record at all (a plain failure note in the decision
  log; the finding stays open); an inconclusive observation is not a
  refutation. Refutation stays owner-grade evidence: an
  orchestrator-originated refutation is valid ONLY through a
  trusted-gate/supervisor-authored run meeting ALL of the above. It is the ONLY
  disposition that may close a finding without anyone accepting or
  fixing it, so its evidence bar is the highest in the enum. v4's enum
  forced practice into lies: AUD51-c5's owner-refuted M2 fit none of
  the four transitions (`rejected-duplicate` — no surviving twin;
  `closed-residual` — accepting authority for a risk shown not to
  exist; `superseded` — no successor record). A refutation asserted
  without a named re-run is invalid — refutation is repro-gated exactly
  like filing. **A wrong refutation is corrected WITHOUT
  touching the closed record (v6 F1, G1 review round 3):** a
  correction NEVER updates the refuted finding — an update to a closed
  finding is refused by the intake rule above, so v5's "the old one
  `superseded` by it" was an illegal instruction: it demanded an
  update the same section forbids. The route: the owner RE-FILES (new
  `audit-finding`, `origin:"owner"` via the audit-filing act) carrying
  **`correctionOf`** = the refuted finding's id (field in 14.10.1;
  null elsewhere). The old finding stays closed as `rejected-refuted`
  forever — history is never rewritten.
  **Correction-lineage fold (v7 R4-C1-3 — v6 said "the pair is ONE
  lineage" but defined neither chains nor the fold, so a duplicate
  naming the obsolete refuted member could discharge against A while
  the live corrected claim B stayed open):**
  - Target validity: `correctionOf` MUST name an existing finding
    whose current state is CLOSED BY `rejected-refuted`; any other
    target (open, or closed by another route) is refused at intake
    (`correction-bad-target`) — non-refuted closure routes keep their
    own mechanisms.
  - Linearity: at most ONE correction per target (a second is refused,
    `correction-ambiguity`); a correction may itself be refuted and
    corrected (chains are legal); `correctionOf` cycles are malformed
    (same rule as duplicate chains). A **lineage** = the maximal
    correctionOf chain; the **live tip** = the unique member NOT
    closed by `rejected-refuted` (if every member is refuted-closed
    the lineage is fully refuted and has no live member). **The live
    tip may itself be terminalized (v24 R5-C17-1): when it carries a
    `rejected-duplicate`/`superseded` closure, it is NOT its own
    effective tip — consumers resolve it FORWARD along that edge
    (transitively, visit-once per NDR-n; v25 R5-C18-4: a repeat visit
    — malformed cyclic prefix — yields NO effective tip and the r4
    caller applies NO survivor row: the chain evaluates UNCLEAN +
    needs-owner naming the lineage) to its effective survivor (per
    NDR-n's EFFECTIVE LIVE TIP clause); the r4 row of a terminalized
    live tip is its survivor's row outcome.**
  - Duplicate resolution: a `rejected-duplicate` naming ANY member of
    a lineage resolves, at every boundary and in the §14.12.2 r4
    chain table, to the LIVE TIP's row outcome — never the named
    member's. A refuted member's evidence NEVER discharges a
    duplicate: A's failed re-run says nothing about corrected claim
    B. **Total no-live-tip branch (v8 R4-C2-4 — v7 left "no live
    member" without an r4 survivor, so D had no defined row):** when
    the lineage has NO live tip (every member closed by
    rejected-refuted), a duplicate naming member M resolves through
    the **TIP-MOST member T** (the chain's last member), not the
    named member's evidence: D DISCHARGES only if (i) T's own
    refutation is VALID under the r4 refuted row AND (ii) D's link
    is machine-checked against **T's** repro (`reproDigest` equal to
    T's; a link digest-equal to an EARLIER member A never
    machine-checks against T's corrected repro — repros differing
    across the lineage is the normal case, which is why the test
    runs on T). An owner-authorized link (non-falsifiable repro) ⇒
    UNCLEAN, needs its own disposition (r4 refuted row, owner link).
    Fail-closed default: anything not provable through (i)+(ii) ⇒
    UNCLEAN. Vectors: (a) A refuted, B = correctionOf:A open, D
    duplicate-naming-A ⇒ D's outcome = B's row (open, counts rule 3
    at B's severity) — discharge REFUSED; (b) same chain, B later
    validly refuted (T = B), no further correction ⇒ D discharges
    ONLY if D.reproDigest == B.reproDigest (machine-checked against
    the TIP B); digest-equal-to-A-only ⇒ UNCLEAN; (c) a second
    correction C2 of A while C1 stands ⇒ `correction-ambiguity`
    refused; (d) (v9 R4-C3-8 — the v8 vector demanded an impossible
    refutation: `rejected-refuted` ALWAYS requires a conforming
    not-reproduced run, which kind:none can never supply; **FULLY
    SPECIFIED AS A REACHABLE RECORD SEQUENCE v10 R5-C4-8**) lineage
    A→B (B = `correctionOf:"A"`, so B is the TIP) with B (the TIP)
    validly refuted under the r4 refuted row, and duplicate D
    closing to `rejected-duplicate` with `supersedes` = B via an
    OWNER-authorized link rather than a machine-checked one ⇒
    UNCLEAN — a refutation never shares its evidence across a
    non-machine-checked link. The complete sequence: (1) finding A
    (route r, severity minor, repro `kind:"probe"` falsifiable);
    (2) a conforming `repro-run` refuting A — `result:"not-reproduced"`
    on A's pre-fix baseline with `reproDigest` == A's — then A closes
    `rejected-refuted` with that `reproRunRef` (**A MUST be refuted
    and CLOSED before B may name it — target validity above refuses a
    correction of an OPEN finding; the v10 vector omitted this step**);
    (3) finding B with `correctionOf:"A"`, SAME route, severity ≥
    A's, with its OWN falsifiable repro (`kind:"probe"`,
    `reproDigest` dB); (4) a conforming `repro-run` refuting B —
    `result:"not-reproduced"` on B's pre-fix baseline with
    `reproDigest` == dB — then B closes `rejected-refuted` with
    that `reproRunRef` (B's refutation is VALID: B's repro is
    falsifiable); (5) finding D, minor, route r, whose OWN repro
    is `kind:"none"` — **the non-falsifiability is D's LINK-SIDE
    repro: D carries no `reproDigest` comparable to dB, which is
    exactly why its link cannot be machine-checked**; (5) an
    owner-act `finding-disposition` closing D
    `rejected-duplicate` `supersedes:"B"` (an owner-authorized
    link — the only route a kind:none duplicate may take). D does
    NOT discharge: the r4 refuted row requires machine-checking
    against T's (= B's) repro and D's link is owner-authorized ⇒
    UNCLEAN, needs-owner naming D, until D's own disposition cure
    (row rule above). An INVALID or absent tip refutation
    fails closed independently of link authority: condition (i) is
    never excused by (ii).
  - **Edge composition — ONE deterministic fold (v9 R4-C3-4 — v8
    defined the correction branch and the r4 duplicate/supersede
    table separately, so mixed graphs had no defined outcome and
    correction-resolved survivors escaped the severity/route
    revalidation; ALGORITHM MADE TOTAL v10 R5-C4-6 — v9 declared
    "an undefined composition IS a contract defect" without
    pinning traversal, per-step effective edges, or intermediate-
    failure propagation):** the fold is a pure function of the log
    prefix, computed at every boundary in FOUR ordered steps:
    **(1) CORRECTION PASS:** resolve every `correctionOf` edge per
    the correction-lineage rules — a target refuted and corrected
    leaves the survivor set; the live tip (or, with no live tip,
    T for the no-live-tip test) takes its place. A correction
    violating severity non-decrease or same-route is **REFUSED AT
    INTAKE** (append-time validation, like `correction-bad-target`
    / `correction-ambiguity` — the new kind name is
    `correction-severity-decrease` / `correction-route-mismatch`;
    it is NEVER accepted into a graph that then folds UNCLEAN at
    the boundary: intake rules decide graph legality, the fold
    only ever sees legal graphs). **(2) LINK EFFECTIVIZATION:**
    every duplicate/superseded edge is rewritten to its EFFECTIVE
    SURVIVOR — the target resolved by TRANSSHIPMENT (v11 R5-C5-2:
    follow the target's OWN effective edge — duplicate/superseded
    edges AND correction edges alike — repeatedly, visiting each
    node at most once (a repeat visit is the step-4 cycle case,
    malformed ⇒ needs-owner), until reaching the member with no
    outgoing effective edge; so when E duplicate-of D and D
    duplicate-of a CLOSED member D', E's traversal passes through
    D to the effective survivor; the correction pass of step (1)
    has already settled correction chains, so the traversal is
    TOTAL over every legal mixed graph and terminates) —
    ONCE; the effective link is then revalidated for severity,
    route, and equivalence using **the source finding's own
    link-side repro versus the effective survivor's repro**
    (machine-checked vs owner-authorized) as if the link named the
    survivor directly. **Intermediate raw links are REPLACED, not
    composed: a raw link's own failure does NOT propagate along
    the chain — each member is judged only by ITS effective link
    against the effective survivor.** This answers the pinned
    counterexample (v10): E duplicate-of D, D duplicate-of A,
    B = correctionOf A ⇒ E's and D's effective links BOTH name B;
    E's reproDigest equals B's ⇒ E machine-checks against B's row
    outcome; D's does not equal B's ⇒ D is UNCLEAN even though
    D digest-equals A; one member's outcome never changes
    another's. "E folds through D's row outcome for B in one
    pass" (v9) MEANS: the pass resolves E's link target to B and
    evaluates E's OWN link — it never means E inherits D's
    outcome. **(3) PER-MEMBER ROW APPLICATION:** members are
    applied to the §14.12.2 chain table in ASCENDING record-id
    (ULID) order of the CLOSED member — a fixed total order, so
    two implementations produce identical results; each row's
    inputs are the effective survivor's current disposition and
    THAT member's revalidated effective link, nothing else.
    **(4) FIXED POINT & CYCLES:** steps (1)–(3) re-run until no
    member's outcome changes; the correction pass is idempotent
    (graph legality was decided at intake), so the iteration
    terminates in at most one pass — any claimed non-termination
    means a cycle: same-kind cycles AND mixed-edge cycles (a
    cycle visiting BOTH edge kinds) are malformed ⇒ needs-owner
    (same rule as same-kind cycles), never silently folded.
    Owner-supersede onto a lineage member relinks to that
    lineage's effective survivor with full revalidation (same
    effective-link rule as step 2). Both lineage branches feed
    r4 explicitly: live-tip branch ⇒ the TIP's row outcome with
    the effective-link revalidation above; no-live-tip branch ⇒
    the T-based test of (i)+(ii) above; each feeds fail-closed
    (anything not provable ⇒ UNCLEAN), so the table has a row for
    every composition (v9: no composition of legal graphs lands
    undefined; an undefined composition IS a contract defect —
    v10: the four ordered steps above are the total algorithm
    that discharges the claim). `superseded`
    keeps its own meaning — a closed record never gains fields
    post-hoc). AUD51:
  c5 REFUTED an M2 claim — both mutant shapes red — and c6 showed the
  refutation was WRONG about the double-failure shape, which survived
  the whole suite; the finding was re-raised as that cycle's finding,
  accepted, and pinned as F98 — traveling exactly this path). Who may
  originate it (round 2 decision R2-D1, owner-adopted):
  `dispositionBy` ∈ {orchestrator, owner} both legal — the orchestrator
  may refute directly given a conforming gate-runner `repro-run`
  record, because the evidence (not the rank) carries the claim; owner
  dispositions ride the same owner-act channel as other transitions.
- `reproRunRef` (v5 R2-3) — the acceptance binding the section's own
  R4 contract demands: for `accepted-fix` where the finding's
  `severity` ≠ minor, REQUIRED non-null, naming the durable `repro-run`
  record re-run against `postFixExpected` and observed GREEN (the
  record is written by the gate runner through the append API, 14.10.3
  — the same channel as dispositions, so the green re-run is bound
  where an auditor cannot strike it). Required for BOTH
  `dispositionBy` values: an orchestrator-originated accepted-fix has
  no owner act at all, and v4 left its green re-run bound nowhere.
  Minor-severity accepted-fix may carry null —
  the single carve-out (v6 F4, pinned jointly with §14.12.2 rule 4 so
  the two sections can never diverge again): valid ONLY for
  `dispositionBy:"owner"` riding a `finding-disposition` owner-act
  with a non-empty `reason` echoed verbatim in the act's canonical
  payload (validation checks the record's reason equals the act's —
  the act IS the authority and its payload is the binding; minors are
  owner-judgment by the severity rule, and the reason is what that
  judgment leaves behind). An orchestrator-originated minor
  accepted-fix with null ref is malformed — refused; §14.12.2 rule 4
  is the consumer enforcement and states the same three conditions. This field existed in the v4
  owner payload (`finding-disposition.reproRunRef`) with no record
  field to receive it — c7-B1's named-field-absent defect class,
  closed pre-implementation.
- `rejected-duplicate` and `superseded` require `supersedes` naming the
  surviving finding — the old "companion record" half-mechanism is
  gone; one encoding, here.

#### 14.10.3 Emission authority (R3)

A shared flock-guarded log has no cryptographic signer; authority is
structural, same posture as F53 (mint, don't trust):

- **Auditor workers append `audit-finding` records only** — via
  supervisor intake (which validates and mints the id), and only with
  `origin:"auditor"`. They never append updates, and they cannot
  originate an `origin:"owner"` line by ANY route — the owner-act
  route requires an owning owner-act (14.10.1) and the derived mode
  is the SUPERVISOR's filing privilege, never a worker's (v9
  R4-C3-3: the v8 rationale named only the act while the entry-mode
  table admits owner-origin records without one — via the supervisor
  alone). **Owner-origin findings (v5 R2-2) enter through the owner-act
  channel (`op:"audit-filing"`) — or, when supervisor-derived,
  through the derived mode of the entry-mode table WITHOUT an act
  (v8 R4-C2-5 — v7's unconditional "rides the act" contradicted the
  table) — the owner never appends to the log directly.** Payload + binding rules (v6 F2, G1
  review round 3): v5's payload `{findingDraftRef, claim, cycle}`
  bound a PATH, not bytes — between the owner's TTY confirmation and
  intake, the file at that path could change, so re-digesting at
  intake proved only what the supervisor read, never what the owner
  authorized. The v6 payload is `{ findingDraftRef, draftSha256,
  claim, cycle }` — **HISTORICAL (v14 R5-C8-7): the CURRENT closed
  payload is `{ findingDraftRef, draftSha256, claim, cycle,
  taskId|null }` (op entry below, v10 R5-C4-1); this sentence
  records the F2-era shape only — build the current schema** —
  **`draftSha256` (sha256 over the draft's exact
  bytes) is computed by the CLI at confirmation time from the bytes
  actually displayed to the owner and is part of the digest-bound
  canonical payload.**
  **Confirmed-bytes snapshot (v7 R4-C1-5 — v6 left the confirmed
  bytes unpersisted: intake re-read the LIVE path, so a
  `owner-filing-draft-drift` refusal stranded a durably confirmed act
  with an unapplied effect and NO defined resolution — an outstanding
  owed effect finalization cannot cleanly close).** Ordering,
  CLI side, fsync-enforced: at confirmation the CLI (i) writes the
  exact displayed bytes to the content-addressed spool path
  `drafts/sha256-<draftSha256>` and fsyncs, THEN (ii) the owner-act
  appends (the draft artifact is capped at 16 KiB by the CLI —
  over-cap drafts refused at input — so the act stays self-contained
  per v11 c9-B3). Intake NEVER reads the live `findingDraftRef`
  path: it reads the SPOOL file and re-hashes it; the bytes MUST
  equal `draftSha256` and parse per the header rule. Mismatch or
  missing spool = `owner-filing-draft-drift`, possible only via
  spool corruption or a CLI crash between (i) and (ii) — fail closed.
  **Drift is TERMINAL for the act (v7):** the drift-refusal record is
  the act's terminal outcome (its effect set is empty-by-refusal), so
  it never stands as an outstanding owed effect in finalization; the
  act remains immutable evidence of what was confirmed; the boundary
  is UNCLEAN + needs-owner until an owner `filing-drift-resolution`
  act (new closed op, added to the enum below; **generalized to
  EVERY permanent filing refusal v10 R5-C4-2, made EXHAUSTIVE v11
  R5-C5-5, PERMANENCE PINNED TO THE INTAKE PREFIX v12 R5-C6-2: a
  permanent filing refusal is ANY intake refusal of an
  `audit-filing` — the refusal record, appended at intake, is
  DURABLE, IMMUTABLE, and TERMINAL FOR THE ACT as adjudicated
  against the **intake-validation prefix** (the log prefix that
  existed when intake evaluated the act): **the refusal record
  BINDS the prefix it was adjudicated against (v13 R5-C7-3,
  checkability): a permanent-refusal record carries
  `{ intakePrefixEndId, intakePrefixSha256 }` — the id and running
  digest of the LAST record of the prefix intake read (the refusal
  record's own predecessor — an append-only log's prefixes are
  exactly its record-terminated initial segments, so the binding
  is one field pair; **THE EXHAUSTIVE TWO-CLASS EXCEPTION
  (v16 R5-C10-2, sweep-completed v19 R5-C13-5 — v18 called the
  P(W) case "the ONE exception" while its own cycle-11 gate
  rule made legality-gate refusals bind the predecessor: a
  validator applying the v18 text rejected the conforming gate
  refusal; the exception set is now stated EXHAUSTIVELY and
  consistently at every site): a re-adjudication refusal R2
  (the `refused` outcome of a withdrawal's serialized re-
  adjudication, §14.10.3) is CLASS-DEPENDENT — (i) a PINNED
  refusal (the P(W) adjudication itself refused; its
  diagnostic derives over P(W)) does NOT bind its immediate
  predecessor — recovery may append unrelated records between
  the withdrawal and R2's append, so the predecessor rule would
  make R2 bind a prefix the adjudication never used; it binds
  the withdrawal's FROZEN adjudication prefix P(W), and
  validation establishes its relationship to W and to the
  outcome record by identity (the protocol's cross-binding
  clauses) instead of by adjacency; (ii) an APPEND-LEGALITY-
  GATE refusal (R5-C11-2: the pinned prefix found the effect
  appendable, the gate at append time refused) binds its OWN
  IMMEDIATE PREDECESSOR under the general rule — the gate's
  checks evaluate the APPEND-time prefix, not P(W), so the
  general predecessor binding is exactly the prefix its
  diagnostic re-derives over (no exception applies to it); the
  class is determined by the refusal's own derivation and is
  REPLAY-CHECKABLE from the record + outcome (the
  `pinnedVerdict` pair, R5-C12-4/C13-4 — eligibility ⇒
  predecessor-bound, refusal ⇒ P(W)-bound; a mode inconsistent
  with the re-derived pinned verdict is a malformed candidate,
  never an outcome), never from an asserted label** — the
  general rule and these two exception classes are jointly
  exhaustive: every permanent refusal binds either its own
  predecessor (ordinary AND gate refusals) or a withdrawal's
  frozen prefix named through the protocol (pinned refusals
  only) — and replay VALIDATES the recorded refusal
  by re-deriving its diagnostic code over exactly THAT frozen
  prefix and its named verification source **as defined per check
  class (v14 R5-C8-2, third class ADDED v15 R5-C9-2 — v14's
  two-class split misclassified DRAFT-BYTE-DERIVATIVE checks
  (header parse, invalid enum, header-claim vs payload-claim)
  as "log-derivative over the bound prefix alone": the prefix
  holds the act and its `draftSha256`, NOT the draft bytes, so
  those codes could not re-derive and a legitimate refusal
  looked corrupt — same defect class as the spool problem the
  v14 fold fixed; **v16 R5-C10-3 completes the same fix: the
  FOUR CORRECTION DIAGNOSTICS (`correction-bad-target`,
  `correction-ambiguity`, `correction-severity-decrease`,
  `correction-route-mismatch`) were v15's NEXT misclassification
  — they are NOT computable from log records alone: the target
  id, proposed severity, and proposed route are DRAFT-HEADER
  operands (the prefix holds only the act's digest, so a
  prefix-only validator cannot even know WHICH finding was
  targeted), while the target's current state/lineage is
  log-derived. A validator honoring v15's classification could
  not re-derive a legitimate correction refusal — the same
  defect class, third instance**): LOG-DERIVATIVE
  codes (computable from prefix records alone — the class is
  retained for record-only conditions; as of v16 NO intake
  refusal code is log-only) re-derive over
  the bound log prefix alone; FILESYSTEM-OBSERVATION checks
  (spool absent/mismatch — the `owner-filing-draft-drift`
  codes) are evidenced ONLY by the refusal
  record's own self-contained fields (`spoolObserved:"absent"|
  "mismatch", observedSha256|null` — a `mismatch` is
  self-evidenced by `observedSha256 != draftSha256`, a record-only
  comparison; a recorded `absent` is NOT refuted by the spool
  existing later — restoration never converts an absence-refusal
  into a forgery); **DRAFT-DERIVATIVE codes (mapping/schema
  failures of the header/payload — any refusal whose derivation
  reads the draft bytes) re-derive over the draft bytes EMBEDDED
  IN THE REFUSAL RECORD ITSELF: such a refusal carries
  `adjudicatedDraftBytes` (the exact spooled bytes intake
  adjudicated, ≤ the 16 KiB draft cap, same-domain transport as
  owner-act payload storage per the c9-B3 self-containment rule)
  — replay verifies the embedded bytes re-digest to the ACT's
  `draftSha256` (the act is in the bound prefix) and re-derives
  the code from the embedded bytes; required non-null exactly
  when the diagnostic is draft-derivative **or MIXED (fourth
  class, v16 R5-C10-3 — diagnostics whose derivation reads BOTH
  bound-prefix records AND draft bytes: exactly the four
  correction codes) — MIXED refusals re-derive JOINTLY over the
  bound prefix AND the digest-verified embedded bytes TOGETHER:
  the header operands (`correctionOf` target id, proposed
  severity, proposed route) come from the verified bytes, the
  target's current state and lineage from the bound prefix, and
  the code re-derives only from the combination — prefix-only
  or bytes-only re-derivation is INCOMPLETE for this class and
  validation that runs either alone has not validated anything;
  the `adjudicatedDraftBytes` requirement is the same (≤16 KiB,
  MUST re-digest to the act's `draftSha256` from the bound
  prefix) and totality is the same (intake ordering makes
  this total: absent/mismatch spool routes to drift BEFORE any
  draft-parsing code can fire — a correction refusal proves the
  header parsed, so readable bytes existed to embed); a
  draft-derivative OR
  MIXED refusal missing the field, or whose embedded bytes fail
  the digest, is a malformed record → integrity fault (never
  silently honored)** before the refusal is honored: a refusal
  whose code does NOT re-derive over its bound prefix (plus
  embedded bytes where its class requires them), or a
  permanent refusal missing the binding, is itself a forgery/
  corruption case — fail closed to `owner-filing-integrity-fault`
  class O naming the refusal record (never silently honored, never
  silently dropped), and replay NEVER evaluates the refusal's
  conditions against any later state**. Later replay RECOGNIZES
  the recorded refusal (validated against its bound prefix) and
  never re-adjudicates its target/lineage/
  schema conditions against the evolved prefix (a target closed
  AFTER the refusal, or a new diagnostic that a later prefix would
  yield, changes NOTHING — the recorded code stands; without this
  pin, `correction-bad-target` would flip to admissible when the
  target later closes, leaving terminality undefined), so the
  refusal re-derives identically on every replay of the same act
  over the same verification source — `owner-filing-draft-
  drift`, `owner-filing-mapping`, AND the §14.10.2 intake refusals
  (`correction-bad-target`, `correction-ambiguity`,
  `correction-severity-decrease`, `correction-route-mismatch`) AND
  any finding-schema intake failure of the header/payload (a field
  outside its closed enum, a missing required field, a malformed
  repro): the refusal record names its diagnostic code, and EVERY
  such refusal is terminal-by-refusal (the act's effect set is
  empty-by-refusal — a never-created finding is NOT an owed class-B
  effect) and is cleared ONLY by a conforming `filing-drift-
  resolution` naming the refused act. A refusal that could NOT
  re-derive on replay (transient I/O) is retried, never
  terminalized; a code outside this rule means the implementation
  invented a refusal — contract defect**):
  `{ refusedActId, refusalRecordId, outcome:"refiled"|"withdrawn",
  newActId|null }` —
  **`refusedActId` names the permanent-refused act (drift OR
  mapping, v10 R5-C4-2; renamed from `driftedActId` — DRAFT, no
  migration); `refusalRecordId` REQUIRED (v15 R5-C9-3 — an act's
  history can hold MORE THAN ONE durable refusal after the
  intake-refusal lifecycle: R1 (invalid, fault-withdrawn) plus a
  re-adjudication outcome refusal R2 — act-only binding cannot say
  WHICH refusal condition clears): it names the LOG RECORD ID of
  the refusal being resolved, MUST resolve to a refusal record of
  `refusedActId` whose condition is CURRENTLY LIVE (a VALID,
  terminal-by-refusal refusal — replay checks its class-validated
  re-derivation stands), and MUST NOT name a refusal already
  cleared by an earlier resolution or superseded as an INVALID
  (fault-adjudicated) refusal — those are excluded from the
  resolution target by definition; the live terminal-by-refusal
  refusal of an act, if any, is UNIQUE at every prefix (a
  re-adjudication replaces the act's terminality), so liveness is
  deterministic)** —
  `refiled` requires newActId naming a LATER `audit-filing` act
  **WHOSE FILING SUCCEEDED (v8 R4-C2-3 — act existence alone lets a
  second drifted/refused act B clear A's hold while nothing was
  filed): newActId's act must have replay-derived `effectApplied ==
  true` (its finding record exists and validates) AND the filed
  finding's header `claim` EQUALS the refused act's payload `claim`
  (the same confirmed statement, re-confirmed and ACCEPTED on
  current bytes)**; `withdrawn` closes the need with no filing. On a
  conforming resolution the refusal condition clears (the resolution
  act names it) and the boundary is no longer held by it. The
  supervisor copies the spool bytes to an immutable `findingRef`
  artifact and the record's `claimDigest` is that same digest:
  confirmed bytes, spool bytes, stored bytes, and attested digest are
  ONE byte-string.
  **Draft→record mapping (v6 F2; header completed v7 R4-C1-4):** the
  draft is a structured artifact: line 1 = the magic line
  `tre://audit-filing-draft/1`; line 2 = ONE single-line JSON object
  (the header) carrying the record's COMPLETE closed-field set —
  `(route, surface, severity, verdictBasis, claim, repro, scopeRefs,
  affectedNorm, correctionOf, evidenceRefs, cureActRef)` — free prose below.
  **`cureActRef` (v28 R5-C20P-2 — cure-lineage source: the v27 wire
  field had no source in this map, so no owner filing could carry it
  and the mapping's own any-unsourced-field defect fired on the
  settlement route's key operand): the header carries `cureActRef`
  REQUIRED-PRESENT (explicit null allowed — a null header value
  files an ordinary non-cure finding); the record copies it verbatim
  at intake and mapping replay compares it exactly (same
  verbatim-compare rule as `taskId`, v10 R5-C4-1); a header omitting
  the field is malformed (`owner-filing-mapping`, refused).
  Non-null semantics are split by prefix (v28 R5-C20P-5 intake/
  settlement split: the v27 texts demanded confirmed+unsettled at
  intake in one place and at settlement in another): at INTAKE over
  the intake-validation prefix the validator checks IDENTITY only —
  the value resolves in-log to a `residual-cure` act record
  (unknown id or non-cure act ⇒ `cure-unknown-act`, refused; ref
  resolution over the durable append-only log is the declared basis
  §14.10.0 TA-1); the
  CONFIRMED + UNSETTLED + NOT-CANCELLED state is a SETTLEMENT-time
  check over the settlement prefix (a finding naming a settled or
  cancelled cure is a conforming finding — it simply settles
  nothing, and a settlement citing it is refused).
  **`correctionOf` and `evidenceRefs` were absent from the v6 header
  enumeration while both are authority-relevant record fields
  (`correctionOf` drives lineage/convergence; `evidenceRefs` is
  ≥1-REQUIRED on every finding): two records differing only in those
  fields could both "re-derive" from the same confirmed bytes (round-4
  finding 4) — now EVERY non-envelope record field has exactly one
  source: the header (classified fields), the act payload
  (`draftSha256`, `claim`, `cycle`, `taskId|null` — v10 R5-C4-1),
  or the entry-mode envelope (mode,
  origin, proof refs — entry-mode table above; `ownerActRef` on the
  record is an envelope proof ref, and in owner-act mode the act
  payload's `cureActRef` — v28 R5-C20P-2 — is the header-carried value
  above, so its chain is header → payload → record, never a
  payload-only invention).** `draftSha256`
  covers the WHOLE artifact bytes. **`cycle` (v9 R4-C3-1 — re-lands
  C2-1, which a crashed fold script dropped from the body while the
  changelog claimed it): the header carries NO cycle; cycle's SOLE
  source is the act payload; the header↔payload MUST-EQUAL comparisons
  are exactly TWO (v28 R5-C20-4 — finding 4: the v9 rule named `claim`
  only while v28 requires `cureActRef` too): `claim` (byte-equal after
  NFC, NDR-c) and `cureActRef` (null=null or identical in-log act id).
  `cycle` is NOT compared — it has no header source and comes from the
  act payload alone.** Envelope-field sources, exhaustively (v9): `kind`
  /`schema` fixed; `id`/`ts`/`episodeId`/`findingRef` path/
  `claimDigest` supervisor-minted at intake; `producer` trio = the
  session recorded on the CLI channel (owner-act mode; nullable trio
  out-of-tre; supervisor session in derived mode); `taskId` = act
  payload or null; mode/origin/proof refs per the entry-mode table.
  Any record field with no listed source is a contract defect.
  **`taskId` vectors (v10 R5-C4-1):** (a) owner files a
  task-specific finding: act payload carries `taskId:"t2"` (a real
  task id in the episode), the record's `taskId` copies it, and
  mapping replay re-derives `taskId` from the act and compares — a
  record with `taskId:null` under an act carrying `"t2"` (or the
  reverse) is `owner-filing-mapping`, refused at intake; (b)
  contract-only owner filing: act payload carries EXPLICIT
  `taskId:null`, record `taskId` is null, replay compares null to
  null — conforming; an act payload OMITTING `taskId` is malformed
  at the closed-schema check (explicit-null is required — absence
  is not a third state).
  **Claim-equality encoding (v9 R4-C3-5; operands AND normalization
  stage RE-PINNED v10 R5-C4-3 — v9's "byte equality in their
  canonical payloads, no normalization" contradicted
  `tre-canonical-json/1`'s mandatory NFC (the act payload passes
  through the canonicalizer, so its stored claim is already NFC) and
  left the draft header (a single-line JSON object, NOT a canonical
  payload) without a defined comparison operand):** the operands are
  the DECODED JSON string VALUES — parse the header JSON per its
  pinned single-line-JSON serialization (v7 R4-C1-4), take `claim`;
  decode the act's canonical payload bytes, take `claim`. The two
  strings are EQUAL iff their **NFC forms are equal by code-point
  sequence** — the SAME normalization stage the canonicalizer
  applies, run on BOTH operands before comparison (correcting v9's
  "no normalization": comparing raw decoded strings against a
  canonicalized operand was order-dependent and made legitimate
  decomposed owner text unfilable; comparing NFC(both) is one rule
  consistent with the canonicalizer). Vectors: (a) header `claim`
  uses decomposed `e`+U+0301, act canonical payload carries composed
  U+00E9 ⇒ NFC on both sides ⇒ EQUAL ⇒ conforming (v9's raw-byte
  reading failed this mapping for a claim the owner literally
  confirmed); (b) header `"\u00e9"` escape vs act `"é"` raw ⇒ decode
  to the same string, NFC identity ⇒ EQUAL ⇒ conforming; (c) header
  claim "foo" vs act claim "Foo" ⇒ NFC preserves case ⇒ NOT EQUAL ⇒
  `owner-filing-mapping`, refused. No normalization beyond NFC at
  comparison time (no case folding, no compatibility decomposition).
  (Correcting v9's cross-reference: this rule is pinned HERE in
  §14.10.3, not in §14.10.1 as the replay text cited.) Validation
  parses the header
  from the confirmed bytes and **re-derives every authority-relevant
  record field from it**; the act payload's `claim` MUST EQUAL the
  header's re-derived `claim` (one confirmed statement, not two) — a
  record field differing from the confirmed draft, a header failing
  the §14.10.1 schema, or a payload/header claim disagreement is
  `owner-filing-mapping`, refused at intake; the supervisor
  transcribes an owner-origin record's classified fields, never
  authors them.
- **The supervisor is the sole appender of `audit-finding-update`.**
  `dispositionBy:"owner"` requires a recorded owner channel behind it:
  owner dispositions originate ONLY from the TTY-confirmed operator CLI
  act (the D2 human-gate precedent, docs/21 §4) and carry its
  reference in `authority` (or the pinned policy clause for residuals).
  The attack this closes: an implementer (or an eager orchestrator)
  downgrading its own blocker to `closed-residual` — the field alone
  could not stop it; the emitter rule can.
- **Enforced provenance boundary (v6, c4-M11):** the threat model is
  the shared machine — any process with filesystem access to S5 can
  forge any string, so an `authority`/`runner` field is NEVER proof of
  origin on its own. The enforcing layer is the **append API**: S5
  direct file access is restricted (0600, supervisor-owned) and there
  is NO general-purpose writer — privileged kinds
  (`policy-revision`, `repro-run`, `spend-reconciliation`,
  `finding-hold`/`-lift`, owner dispositions, `scope-escape-resolution`)
  are appendable ONLY through supervisor entrypoints that are
  themselves reachable only from (i) the trusted-gate/supervisor
  process path (repro-run: the gate runner is a supervisor-executed
  child; its record is written BY the supervisor from the child's
  evidence and bound to `runEvidenceRef`), or (ii) the TTY-confirmed
  operator CLI (the P17 activation precedent): a TTY act appends a
  durable **owner-act record**
  `{ kind:"owner-act", id, ts, episodeId, op:"<exact operation>",
  payload, payloadDigest:"sha256:<canonical payload>", channel:"tty:<dev>",
  sessionRef }` FIRST, and every privileged record's `authority` field
  names that owner-act id; validation replays the owner-act, re-digests
  the payload it bound, and refuses on ANY mismatch (op, digest,
  channel) — channel-to-payload binding is the check, not the string.
  **Payload IN the record (v11, c9-B3): the record stores the FULL
  canonical payload bytes, not a digest alone** — a digest-only act
  is unrecoverable exactly when recovery needs it most: if the queue
  file that carried the act is gone, a digest cannot reconstruct the
  missing effect, so authorized authority would silently lapse. The
  act is therefore self-contained: `payload` (canonical bytes,
  ≤ 16 KiB — payloads are closed per-op schemas, none is larger)
  AND `payloadDigest` over those bytes; validation checks the two
  agree, and that the queue entry (while it exists) matches both.
  A worker-originated privileged record (no valid owning owner-act, or
  digest mismatch) is malformed ⇒ refused at intake AND ignored by
  replay; finding the string "tty:…" in a payload proves nothing.
  **Trust-boundary limits, stated honestly (v7, c5-M1):** this is a
  same-OS-user threat model and its residual limits are part of the
  contract, not hidden by it: (i) a process running as the supervisor's
  OS user that bypasses the append API CAN in principle open the 0600
  file — the enforcement holds against every process that goes through
  the API (the only supported write path) and against separate-user
  attackers by file permissions; closing the same-user bypass would
  require OS-level isolation (separate uid / sandbox) for the CLI and
  worker processes — an OWNER DEPLOYMENT choice, recorded here as a
  declared limit, not claimed enforcement; (ii) a compromised supervisor
  process can mint both owner-acts and privileged records — the
  contract's guarantees assume an uncompromised supervisor and name it
  (Tcb-1 style: the trusted computing base IS the supervisor; nothing
  in the log self-certifies against a corrupted writer). `channel:
  "tty:<dev>"` plus `sessionRef` record WHERE the confirmation was
  collected (the interactive TTY the operator typed at, per the P17
  activation precedent); the human binding is the interactive
  confirmation step in the CLI process, and its forensic trail is the
  owner-act — again with the same limit: an OS-level impersonator is a
  deployment concern (uid separation), not a log-level one.
  **Owner-act payload canonicalization (v7, c5-M1; closed per-op
  schemas v8, c6-M7):** `payloadDigest` is computed over the CANONICAL
  payload of the one operation the act authorizes, using the SAME
  pinned canonicalizer as policy bytes (`tre-canonical-json/1`, §14.12
  v8 pins incl. Unicode NFC and the numeric domain — ONE
  canonicalizer for the whole contract, not two dialects), domain-
  separated by prefixing the bytes `"tre-owner-act/1\n" + op + "\n"`.
  The payload field set is a CLOSED SCHEMA per operation (v8 — a
  validator may NEVER omit an authority-relevant field; omitted
  optional fields are represented as explicit `null` so their absence
  is digest-visible):
  - `finding-disposition`: `{ findingId, fromStatus, toStatus,
    basisRef|null, reproRunRef|null, reason:string|null }` —
    **`reason` added v7 (R4-C1-1; the v6 minor accepted-fix carve-out
    demanded the reason be "echoed verbatim in the act's canonical
    payload" while this CLOSED payload had no reason field — the
    exception was not expressible: adding the field ad hoc would
    violate the closed schema, omitting it failed the exception).**
    Nullability: for an `accepted-fix` toStatus on a minor with
    `reproRunRef:null` (the §14.10.2/§14.12.2 carve-out) `reason` is
    REQUIRED non-empty; for every other disposition it is an advisory
    string or null (explicit null keeps absence digest-visible).
    Validation: the `audit-finding-update` record's `reason` must
    EQUAL the act payload's `reason` (both single-line, ≤1000 chars);
    mismatch ⇒ the update is refused (`disposition-reason-mismatch`).
    Vectors: minor accepted-fix, act reason "docs-only, owner accepted"
    + record reason equal ⇒ VALID; same with record reason "" ⇒
    refused; record reason differing by one char ⇒ refused.
  - `audit-filing` (v5 R2-2 — §14.10.1's owner-origin findings need an
    op or the closed-schema rule itself would refuse the channel that
    files them; the c7-B1 defect class, closed at the same time as the
    field that consumes it; **v6 F2**: `draftSha256` added and the
    draft→record mapping rule stated in the 14.10.1/14.10.3 owner-
    filing text above — the pre-F2 payload bound a path whose bytes
    could change after confirmation): `{ findingDraftRef, draftSha256,
    claim, cycle, taskId|null, cureActRef|null }` — **`cureActRef|null`
    added v28 R5-C20P-2 (the v27 settlement route's key lineage
    operand had no act-payload carrier — a cure-evidence filing could
    not be expressed on the owner channel without violating the
    mapping's source rule; the payload carries the header's value
    EXPLICIT-NULL closed, same nullability contract as `taskId|null`:
    the CLI copies the confirmed header's `cureActRef` into the act
    payload before the act is appended, intake compares
    payload-to-header (`owner-filing-mapping` on mismatch), and the
    resulting record copies it verbatim as above)** — **`taskId|null` added v10 R5-C4-1:
    the envelope map claimed `taskId` came from the act payload while
    the closed payload had no such field, making a task-specific owner
    filing inexpressible and a null-task filing unsourceable; the
    field is EXPLICIT-NULL closed (a null-task filing digests its
    `null`, so absence is never digest-invisible), the record's
    optional `taskId` copies it verbatim at intake, and mapping
    re-derivation compares it** — the CLI hashes the draft's displayed
    bytes into
    `draftSha256` BEFORE the act is appended, intake re-hashes the
    **spooled bytes at the content-addressed path `drafts/sha256-<
    draftSha256>` (v14 R5-C8-7 — the source is the SPOOL only; the
    live `findingDraftRef` path is NEVER read at intake, per the
    confirmed-bytes-snapshot rule above** and refuses a mismatch (`owner-filing-draft-drift`),
    and the resulting `audit-finding`'s `claimDigest` equals
    `draftSha256`; validation replays the act, re-digests the draft,
    and re-derives the record's classified fields from the confirmed
    header (a conforming validator MUST be able to reconstruct every
    authority-relevant field from the act's own payload + bytes —
    c7-B1's reconstructibility standard applied here)
  - `finding-hold` / `finding-hold-lift`: `{ findingId }` — the
    resulting record's `dispositionBy`/`authority` are supervisor-
    stamped, not act-bound; the act binds the finding it escalates

    refused by the closed-schema rule itself)
  - `norm-transition`: `{ normId, from, to, expectedRevision,
    sha256|null, anchorTextRef|null, supersedes|null }` — exactly
    reconstructible from the resulting §14.11.2 transition record
    (v9, c7-B1: ratify/reject/supersede ARE owner acts under §14.7;

  - `policy-revision`: `{ revision, digest, policyRef, canonicalizer }`
    — the §14.12.3 record's authority-relevant fields (v9, c7-B1)
  - `scope-escape-resolution`: `{ escapeId, taskId, decision, authId,
    noteDigest|null }` — field-for-field with the §14.14.4 resolution
    record (`noteDigest` = canonical sha256 of the record's `note`, so
    the note's bytes are bound; v9, c7-B1: the v8 payload
    `{escapeEventId, scopeDigest, resolutionTextDigest}` named fields
    the record does not HAVE — no supervisor could reconstruct it from
    the record's own fields, so every such act refused or bypassed

  - `scope-escape-waiver`: `{ escapeId }` (record fields `{escapeId,
    authority}`; v9, c7-B1 alignment — v8 folded it into the
    resolution schema it does not share)
  - `remote-terminal-disposition`: `{ unprovenRecordId, cycleId,
    dispatchIds[] (sorted), disposition, evidenceRefs[] (sorted),
    residualCapUsd|null (required non-null iff
    disposition:"accept-residual-risk"),
    acknowledgment|null (v12 audit fix — §14.13.4a's
    sustained-unreachability class (iii) REQUIRES the disposition to
    carry `acknowledgment:"unreachable-is-not-non-support"` but the
    closed payload did not have the field, so a conforming validator
    refused the very disposition the rule demanded — same defect
    class as c8-M15's `outcome`): REQUIRED non-null
    `"unreachable-is-not-non-support"` exactly when the
    terminality-inability evidence for this disposition is class
    (iii) sustained-unreachability, REQUIRED null otherwise; a class
    (iii) disposition without it, or a non-(iii) disposition
    carrying it, is refused at validation)`
    (`unprovenRecordId` added
    v9 per c7-B4 below — one source of truth; `residualCapUsd` v9
    c7-B4 binds the bounded-unknown charge into the same act)
  - `history-integrity-disposition`: `{ faultId, decision, explanationDigest|null, voidedQueueIds|null }` — `decision` ∈ {accept-recomputed, external-explanation, retire-duplicate-channel} (v18, cycle-11 self-audit finding 5); `retire-duplicate-channel` (valid only on a `channel-id-collision` fault) REQUIRES `voidedQueueIds` = the sorted queueIds of EXACTLY the undrained entries whose `channelOpenRecordId` equals the fault's affectedRecordId at disposition (any other set refused) and `explanationDigest` null; every other decision REQUIRES `voidedQueueIds:null`. Retirement (v19, cycle-12 audit finding 5): the disposition records the channelOpenRecordId as RETIRED under the S5 flock; every later queue append carrying it is REFUSED; a listed entry is VOIDED — it is EXCLUDED from pair formation in the pre-drain duplicate scan, from drift checks, and from P1–P3 (v20, cycle-13 finding 5 — v19 excluded voided entries from P1–P3 but the separate every-entry duplicate scan still formed pairs from them), is never drained, and the list is complete because no later append for the retired channel can land. **Drained entries of a retired channel (v21, cycle-14 finding 3; closure predicate and residual mechanism corrected v22, cycle-15 findings 2–3):** a DRAINED entry is consumed fact and is NEVER voided or un-run (same invariant as an accepted ledger entry). Fault closure at retirement is THREE-WAY, and the three cases are exclusive and total for the retired channel's faults:
  (a) a `queue-receipt-divergence` fault whose affected entries ALL belong to the retired channel (drained or voided) — the SAME predicate as §14.12.3 (v21's weaker "affectedRecordId is an entry of" text is WITHDRAWN: it closed mixed-channel faults here but not there, letting replays disagree) — is closed BY the retirement disposition itself (the disposition names the retired channelOpenRecordId, and closing scope follows from the record, never from an owner assertion); a fault already closed is never re-closed (idempotent per fault identity; the retirement whose predicate first holds owns the closure);
  (b) every OTHER outstanding fault arising from the retired channel's duplicate triples — a mixed-channel divergence fault (an affected entry drained on another channel; §14.12.3 invariant), or an execution-side-effect fault from a drained act (a duplicate-act dispatch or receipt) — is NOT closed by the retirement. Such a fault is dispositioned INDIVIDUALLY, by its own ordinary `history-integrity-disposition` appended BEFORE the retirement disposition: the retirement's append-time validation REFUSES (prefix stays clean, nothing retires) while any fault in class (b) touching the channel is still open. Validation order is therefore deterministic on replay: run the §14.12.3 DETECTION BARRIER first — every scan of the pinned pre-append prefix durably appends its still-missing fault records before the retirement may append (v25, cycle-18 finding 5; validation enumerating a stale durable fault set while a detectable fault is unrecorded is NOT equivalent) — then enumerate the channel's faults from the durable fault set → class (b) must all be closed already, else refuse → close class (a) with the retirement record. (v21 said the retirement disposition itself "must name each such fault and disposition it individually" — the closed payload `{ faultId, decision, explanationDigest|null, voidedQueueIds|null }` has NO field able to carry a fault list or per-fault decisions, so the requirement was inexpressible; the individual-disposition route needs no new field and binds each residual to the fault-identity and decision rules that already govern single-fault dispositions.)
  (c) where a residual effect cannot be ESTABLISHED at all — an executed (drained) act whose side effects cannot be enumerated from the durable record set — retirement is REFUSED for the channel and the case escalates `needs-owner`: fail closed; the v18 invariant "a disposition never claims what it cannot establish" governs the channel case (v19 retired unconditionally and left drained-entry faults undisposed).
A queue-receipt-divergence fault whose drifting entries are all voided is disposed by the retirement itself (v20, finding 5; drained-only entries disposed by clause (a), v21); a retire-then-restart scan therefore yields no new fault. An empty list is valid
  - `budget-extension`: `{ supersedesRevision, newMaxCycles|null,

    and legal ONLY as null when `component:"elapsed"` (elapsed has

    non-attributable to any provider stream; a null where required,
