    closed per-route shape, keys in the order shown) and `digest` =
    sha256 of those exact bytes. Confirmation validation (fail-closed,
    BOTH required): `sha256(preimage) == digest` (the pair remains
    re-checkable for the ledger's retention horizon per §14.10.0 TA-4)
    and the preimage
    parses to the CLOSED shape for the payload's `route` (extra or
    missing member ⇒ `cure-commitment-malformed`, refused).
    `reproDigestOrNull` is resolved AT CONFIRMATION by a deterministic
    rule over records that already exist: if the survivor's closure
    carries a machine-checkable `reproDigest` (§14.10.2 effective
    link), the owner MUST bind that digest (validator-required);
    if the survivor's closure is non-falsifiable (no machine-checkable
    digest exists — e.g. an opinion route), the owner binds `null`.
    The preimage is IMMUTABLE (append-only — never rewritten; a
    changed intent is a NEW cure act, and the second-unsettled-cure
    refusal on the same pair (§14.10.0 route row — no forked cure)
    still applies). REQUIRED non-null.
    CURE GATE (v28 R5-C20-2 — finding 2: the v27 "post-confirmation"
    claim had no mechanism; a run recorded after confirmation could
    still be a pre-confirmation result). At CONFIRMATION the supervisor appends
    (a SEPARATE append immediately after the confirmation record —
    NOT "the same critical section as the act": the log is
    append-then-act and cannot promise an atomic multi-record pair,
    v28 R5-C20F-4 / owner decision D1=A; a crash tearing the pair is
    recovered by the OWED-COMPLETION clause below),
    `cure-gate { id, cureActId, nonce }` — `id` is a fresh conforming
    ULID minted by the supervisor, `nonce` is 32 random bytes hex
    minted by the supervisor, and the record is the only place the
    nonce is durable before settlement. The supervisor hands the gate id + nonce to
    the trusted gate runner for that cure only. DISPATCH GATING
    (v28 R5-C20F-4): the repro is dispatched ONLY AFTER the gate
    record's append is DURABLE (append-then-dispatch); a dispatch
    issued while the gate append is not durable is a contract
    violation, and every run such a dispatch produces is
    unverifiable forever (§14.10.0 TA-5).
    A `repro-run` admitted as cure
    evidence MUST carry `cureGateId` (the gate's id) and its
    `runEvidenceRef` MUST contain the nonce verbatim — the
    verification predicate PINNED (v28 R5-C20F-2; the predicate is
    NAMED `cureGateOk` — recovery and settlement clauses cite it by
    that name): the gate `nonce`
    string occurs as a SUBSTRING of the durable content named by
    `runEvidenceRef` (the gate's command log echoes it); the
    `cure-gate` RECORD is the ONLY durable nonce source — a nonce
    quoted from memory or re-minted after a lost record verifies
    NOTHING (the checked run predates the re-minted value). A run
    citing a `cureGateId` with NO durable `cure-gate` record is
    REFUSED as an unsourced citation (lost-gate refusal,
    v28 R5-C20F-2: no gate record, no cure evidence, ever). Settlement-time
    validation refuses: a run without `cureGateId`, a `cureGateId`
    naming another cure's gate or an unknown gate, or a
    `runEvidenceRef` lacking the nonce. STATED TRUST RESIDUAL (not
    closed by the record):
    a runner that fabricates the echoed nonce from a cached result
    is outside the record's protection; the gate runner is a trusted
    component (§14.10.0 TA-2) and the nonce echo is the checkable artifact the
    supervisor verifies at append. Replay checks the stored
    `cureGateId`/nonce operands only; it never re-runs the gate.
    Because the `{id, nonce}` pair is minted at confirmation (or —
    for an owed completion recovered under R5-C20F-4 / D1=A — by the
    recovery append), a run recorded before the mint cannot carry
    them, and any dispatch issued before the gate append was durable
    is itself the TA-5 contract violation whose runs are
    unverifiable forever, so a pre-confirmation green result can
    never be retro-claimed.
    PARTIAL-PAIR RECOVERY (v28 R5-C20F-4 — owner decision D1=A,
    complete-the-pair): a CONFIRMED cure act with no durable gate
    record (crash between the confirmation append and the gate
    append) is an OWED COMPLETION, not a dead end: the supervisor's
    recovery pass MUST append the derived `cure-gate` record (its
    `nonce` freshly minted at recovery) BEFORE dispatching any
    gated repro for that act, and — ordering pinned v29 G1-V29-C6-1
    (cycle-6 audit), mirroring the pre-drain full scan of §14.12.2 —
    on EVERY startup, before evaluating any boundary and before
    accepting any new append, the recovery pass restores EVERY owed
    gate completion in log order; no boundary is ever evaluated
    against a prefix with an unrestored owed gate (the alternative —
    letting a pending fresh-route settlement extinguish the gate
    first — is FORBIDDEN: recovery sees the pre-recovery log state,
    so only a settlement already durable at restart extinguishes the
    obligation). FAILURE PATH (v30 cycle-9 audit finding 1; REVISED v30 C9-1 — the
    v30 first draft routed the stuck gate through `quiesce-stall`,
    which contradicted NDR-v: an owed gate is NEVER a B item, quiescence
    item, or stall candidate). The owed gate is a RECOVERY-BARRIER item,
    not a drain item, and its failure exit is a FAIL-STOP, defined as
    follows and nothing else:
    (a) SINGLE ATTEMPT PER OWED GATE PER PROCESS (C11-3 — scoped from
    per-process): each owed `cure-gate` is appended AT MOST ONCE per
    supervisor process; recovery may still restore OTHER owed gates in
    the same pass (the barrier requires every owed gate restored) —
    QUALIFIED v33 audit-of-8c5d987 C1-2: ONLY while NO gate-append has
    failed in this pass; after ANY gate-append failure (definite or
    indeterminate) this process attempts NO further appends of ANY
    kind — the pass stops at the failure and (b) fires — gates not yet
    restored stay owed for the next process's pass (V-g9). A
    DEFINITE failure (an error that POSITIVELY ESTABLISHES NO WRITE —
    e.g. the append call fails before transferring any bytes, so this
    process knows the file is byte-unchanged; v31 C1-1: an error alone
    is NOT definite — if the process cannot POSITIVELY establish that
    no bytes were written, the outcome is INDETERMINATE) and an
    INDETERMINATE outcome (bytes may have reached the file — readable,
    but with sync-before-ack UNPROVEN and durability across storage
    failure unestablished (v32 rationale restatement); or fsync's
    result is unknown)
    are both fail-stops (b): the process never
    re-appends after any failure, because a second append could duplicate
    a gate whose first copy is durable. After an INDETERMINATE outcome the
    process CANNOT determine whether the gate is durable and therefore
    never dispatches under it or appends further (C11-2). Duplicate-gate
    safety therefore never rests on a read in the same process. Cross-process safety rests on (c): the next process opens the
    file fresh under exclusive ownership, and its recovery pass finds the gate if it is in the log — and under (c1) treats it as durable only after its own establishing sync (QUALIFIED v33 cycle-18 fold C18-3: the sync is demanded only when the gate's ORIGINATING FSYNC OUTCOME IS UNKNOWN — a gate known-successful by its originating append is established with no sync demanded, per E-7's outcome-equivalent provenances).
    The one-gate-per-act refusal (below) is the backstop: a second
    `cure-gate` for the act is refused as malformed, so a duplicate that
    slipped through would be classified, not silently counted.
    (b) FAIL-STOP: any gate-append failure (definite or indeterminate)
    refuses ALL further appends for the episode and exits the process
    with a nonzero status, reporting the fault on the operator channel.
    This is deliberately NOT a log record: a log that cannot durably
    accept the gate cannot be trusted to accept a stall record either,
    so no record of the fault is attempted. On a DEFINITE failure (the
    positively-established-no-write class of (a), v31 C1-1) the
    on-disk state is unchanged: the act is UNSETTLED and the gate OWED.
    On an INDETERMINATE failure the gate may or may not be durable
    (readable bytes do not PROVE the sync-before-ack policy was met,
    V-g5; v32 rationale restatement); that
    is unknown to this process and is resolved only by (c).
    (c) RESTART (C11-2; REVISED v31 audit-of-7a83bc6, findings A1+A2;
    STEPS REORDERED v32 audit-of-dfb6cf8 — the v31 phrase "repair the
    tail BEFORE any classification" collided with §13.1's rule that a
    LOAD ERROR (bad header, mid-file corruption) throws BEFORE THE
    FILE IS TOUCHED: an unqualified repair-first would MUTATE a file
    validation rejects. The restart's steps run in STRICT order —
    validate, repair, classify, establish:
    (c0) OWNERSHIP → VALIDATION WITHOUT MUTATION → REPAIR. The next
    supervisor start takes EXCLUSIVE OWNERSHIP of the log (§13.2 I1),
    then validates WITHOUT WRITING anything: the header, every
    TERMINATED record in the file, and a read-only classification of
    the final tail (terminated line / complete record missing only its
    newline / partial fragment). A prohibited fault — bad header or a
    corrupt TERMINATED record anywhere (mid-file corruption) — throws
    at this step and the file is NOT TOUCHED: not even an
    independently repairable final fragment is truncated or terminated
    behind a rejected load (vector V-g8); the fail-stop (b) recurs.
    ONLY a file that passed validation is repaired, per §13.1 alone: a
    partial gate fragment is the partial-tail class (truncate it
    away); a COMPLETE gate record that lost only its terminating
    newline is KEPT and terminated (its content counts — truncating it
    would desync the replayed state). No recovery append may be issued
    behind an unrepaired tail.
    (c1) CLASSIFICATION runs over the VALIDATED and (if needed)
    REPAIRED prefix IN THIS ORDER (v33 audit-of-8c5d987 cycle-3 fold
    C3-1 — the semantic checks are REPLAYED BEFORE any establishing
    sync, because a malformed prefix must never be synced (v33 C3-1;
    NOTE v33 C4-1: an UNESTABLISHED terminal record DOES demand its
    own establishing fsync before it may extinguish — that sync
    happens at (c1b), after the checks): (c1a) SEMANTIC CHECKS OVER
    THE REPAIRED PREFIX — the ORDERING checks O1/O2/O3, one-gate-per-
    act, and the terminal-combination check (a cancellation+settlement
    for one act is forbidden) are replayed over EVERY record (gates
    and terminal records alike); any violation refuses the prefix —
    fail-stop (b) recurs, NO sync is issued, nothing is cleared or
    appended. (c1b) TERMINAL-FIRST CLASSIFICATION per (d) — an act
    with an ESTABLISHED-DURABLE cancellation or settlement is
    EXTINGUISHED and its
    gate (which passed O3, so it precedes the terminal record) is
    INERT HISTORY: NO establishing sync is needed or performed FOR THE GATE
    (the obligation extinguished via the terminal record, not the
    gate). TERMINAL RECORDS THEMSELVES MUST BE ESTABLISHED BEFORE
    RELIED ON (v33 cycle-4 fold C4-1 — the SAME rationale as (c1c):
    a cancellation and a settlement are decision records under the
    sync-before-ack policy, so a readable terminal record whose
    originating append's fsync outcome is UNKNOWN has not been
    PROVEN durable and may NOT extinguish the obligation): recovery
    issues its OWN establishing fsync for such a terminal record
    (one file-level fsync establishes every readable record's bytes
    at once — it also covers an inert preceding gate, which needs no
    sync for its own sake); a FAILING establishing fsync for a
    terminal record is its own case: fail-stop (b) recurs, the act
    is NEITHER extinguished nor classified owed (the terminal
    disposition stands on disk with durability unestablished), and
    the next restart re-runs (c) until a sync succeeds or an
    operator intervenes.
    (c1c) ESTABLISHING SYNC for a present gate of an
    otherwise-live act ONLY (v31 A1;
    THE SYNC IS THE SAME SINGLE FILE-LEVEL FSYNC (v33 cycle-6 fold
    C6-1): establishment is per-FILE, not per-record — ONE
    successful fsync of the log file issued at recovery (whether
    first demanded by a terminal record at (c1b) or by a live gate
    here) establishes the durability of EVERY readable record's
    bytes in the file at once, gates of other acts included. A
    pass performs AT MOST ONE establishing fsync after (c1a):
    if it succeeded for any reason (e.g. a terminal record needed
    it at (c1b)), every present gate is ESTABLISHED and no second
    fsync is issued or required — the scenario "the (c1b) file
    sync succeeded but the (c1c) gate sync fails" CANNOT occur;
    if it failed, that single failure is the case below (no act
    gets a second attempt in this pass).
    RATIONALE RESTATED v32 audit-of-dfb6cf8 — this is NOT a
    process-death claim: under §13.1 R3 page-cache bytes DO survive
    process death, and R3 explicitly disclaims power-failure
    guarantees. The obligation is narrower and POLICY-based:
    `cure-gate` is a decision-log record, and decision records are
    SYNC-BEFORE-ACK (§13.1 R3 fsync policy: "steer receipts and
    decisions: sync before ack"); a readable gate whose originating
    append's fsync outcome is UNKNOWN has not been PROVEN to satisfy
    that policy, and the window restart guards is storage failure —
    exactly the window in which readable ≠ durable): recovery issues
    its OWN successful fsync of the log file, and only a sync that
    returns success establishes the found gate durable (the restart's
    own sync is the establishment — no earlier process's success is
    assumed).
    A FAILING ESTABLISHING SYNC IS ITS OWN CASE, NOT AN (a) "DEFINITE
    FAILURE" (v31 C1-1 — the (a) definite-failure clause asserts the
    file is byte-UNCHANGED; that assertion does not transfer here: the
    bytes, and possibly the newline added by repair, ARE present, and
    a "unchanged ⇒ gate absent" reading would misclassify a present
    gate): fail-stop (b) recurs, the repaired prefix stands on disk
    UNTOUCHED FURTHER but its durability is UNESTABLISHED, the gate
    is neither cleared nor trusted for dispatch, and nothing
    dispatches. The next restart runs this same (c) again — (c0)
    validate, repair, (c1) classify, establish — until a sync succeeds
    or an operator intervenes. The semantic checks of (c1a) ran
    BEFORE this sync (v33 C3-1 fold): a prefix failing O1/O2/O3,
    one-per-act, or the terminal-combination check is refused at
    (c1a) and never reaches a sync.
    (c2) applies only to an act SURVIVING (c1a)/(c1b) with no
    ESTABLISHED cancellation or settlement and none whose establishing
    sync is pending or failed (a terminal record awaiting or failing
    establishment fail-stops before (c2) per (c1b)/V-g12; an act
    extinguished at (c1b) is not owed): for such an otherwise-live
    act, an absent gate leaves the obligation owed, and recovery
    appends it under (a).
    Failure of storage at ANY step of (c) recurs the same fail-stop;
    the episode does not advance. This is the ONLY exit, and it
    introduces no new record kind, no stall classification, and no
    boundary: NDR-v and the stall rule are unchanged, and no boundary
    may be evaluated with the gate owed.
    (c1-M) OUTCOME MATRIX (v33 structural fold, post-round-3 audit of
    650abe1 — finding PR-3 and the finding CLASS behind it: since the
    cycle-8 fold, every finding (PR-1, C10-1, PR-2, PR-3) was a
    narrative SENTENCE scoping wider than its rule — a stray
    "proceeds normally" / "either way" / "independently" /
    "already established" — not a misclassified state. The state
    space itself passed three consecutive full-matrix audits CLEAN;
    the residual defect lives in prose. This matrix REPLACES the
    outcome narratives of V-g8's ordered classification, V-g11(i),
    V-g12, and V-g12b as the NORMATIVE outcome source: every
    outcome claim attaches to exactly one row, provenance facts
    (WHY a state holds) live only in section 0 where each is true
    by construction, and the audit question becomes table
    completeness — a reachable combination with no row, or two rows
    classifying one combination differently — not stray-quantifier
    hunt. Where any retained narrative conflicts with this matrix,
    THE MATRIX IS NORMATIVE.
    SCOPE: one row per (act, cell) for every `residual-cure` act
    carrying a recovery (owed-completion) question at (c1),
    evaluated over the prefix that PASSED (c1a), with the pass's
    single establishing-fsync outcome (§0 mechanics, §1 pass-level
    outcome) applied.
    AXES (closed): TERMINAL — none (live act) | readable cancellation
    or settlement with originating fsync KNOWN SUCCESSFUL | readable
    with fsync UNKNOWN, demanded establishing fsync SUCCEEDED |
    UNKNOWN, establishing fsync FAILED | UNKNOWN, no establishing
    fsync demanded or completed yet (pass aborted elsewhere). GATE —
    absent | present readable, established (own successful append,
    own-demanding establishing fsync, or another act's demanding
    establishing fsync — establishment is per-file (C6-1): the
    outcome depends on the sync's RESULT alone, never on WHICH
    record demanded it) | present not yet synced (reached only via
    an aborted pass — no row attaches) | present-but-ineligible
    (O3-violating etc.) — a pass-level REFUSAL at §1, never a row.
    0. MECHANICS (the only place causation is stated): a pass
    performs AT MOST ONE establishing fsync after (c1a) (C6-1); it
    is DEMANDED by every act in state TERMINAL=UNKNOWN or
    GATE=present-unsynced OF AN OTHERWISE-LIVE ACT (v33 cycle-18
    fold C18-1: an inert gate — the gate of an act with an
    ESTABLISHED terminal record — demands no sync, per (c1b)/E-2,
    so its unknown originating fsync never demands a pass fsync
    and cannot introduce a fail-stop the source rules do not
    require); if it is never demanded, no fsync is
    issued and no act's outcome depends on an fsync result; one
    successful fsync establishes EVERY readable record's bytes at
    once (per-file, not per-record); a failing fsync fail-stops
    the whole pass per (b) and attaches NO classification to any
    record whose durability DEPENDS on it — every UNKNOWN-fsync
    act and gate in the pass (C10-1 generalized to the pass: an
    unestablished remainder classifies nothing), while records
    established INDEPENDENTLY of that fsync (durable by
    originating sync, or own-append success earlier in the pass)
    keep their classification; an act's own successful
    append makes ITS OWN gate established (durable-by-this-process)
    with no fsync request of the establishing kind — an (a)
    append's own sync-before-ack belongs to the append's write
    path and is NOT what the "at most one establishing fsync per
    pass" cap counts; the cap covers only syncs ISSUED AT RECOVERY
    for records already in the file, and by the (c1b)/(c1c)
    ordering the single establishing fsync (if demanded at all)
    resolves BEFORE any (a) append begins, so at the moment of any
    append failure every present-record classification is already
    attached; a failure for another act — append or
    sync — NEVER retroactively changes a classification THIS act
    already holds (classifications attach at their own
    establishment and never detach within a pass — the per-file
    sync, once successful, cannot be un-succeeded, and an act
    already durable by origin or by its own append is established
    regardless of any later failure elsewhere in the pass).
    1. PASS-LEVEL OUTCOMES (all passes): (P-REFUSE) (c0) validation
    fault or (c1a) semantic violation (O1/O2/O3, one-per-act,
    terminal-combination) ⇒ prefix refused or file untouched, fail-
    stop (b), NO sync issued, nothing cleared, established, or
    appended (C3-1; the matrix is never consulted for a refused
    prefix). (P-SYNCFAIL) establishing fsync demanded and failed ⇒
    fail-stop (b): NO classification attaches to any record whose
    durability DEPENDS on that fsync — every record with UNKNOWN
    originating fsync is neither extinguished nor cleared nor
    owed-appended, gates included (C10-1). Records ALREADY
    ESTABLISHED independently of it (durable by originating sync,
    or by this pass's own earlier successful append) KEEP their
    classification — establishment once held is never retaken by a
    later failure (§0), and the next restart rederives the same
    classification from the durable log anyway; the fail-stop
    governs PROCESS PROGRESSION (exit nonzero, no boundary
    evaluated, no append attempted), not the erasure of
    independently established state. Next restart re-runs (c) for
    the unestablished remainder. (P-APPENDFAIL) an owed-gate append (a) fails
    (definite or indeterminate) ⇒ fail-stop (b), no further appends
    of any kind attempted this pass (C1-2); the failing act's own
    outcome is E-11; other acts keep the rows already attached.
    (P-COMPLETE) no failure anywhere ⇒ every act classified per
    §2, no owed gate remains, recovery proceeds to the normal
    recovery steps. ONLY P-COMPLETE is a normal pass completion.
    2. PER-ACT ROWS (one operative classification each; EXCEPT
    E-6/E-9, which are NON-OPERATIVE EXPLANATORY ENTRIES (v33
    cycle-17 fold C17-5): the combinations they name are classified
    SOLELY by §1 P-REFUSE — the matrix is never consulted for a
    refused prefix — and they stand here only to record that the
    axes leave those combinations with no operative row; they
    assign nothing):
    E-1 TERMINAL known-successful, GATE absent ⇒ EXTINGUISHED per
    (d)(ii)/(iii), nothing owed (V-g11(i) durable-by-origin case;
    no sync demanded by this act).
    E-2 TERMINAL known-successful, GATE present ⇒ EXTINGUISHED per
    (d)(ii)/(iii) — operative; GATE INERT HISTORY (V-g10(i); no
    sync demanded by this act; inertness attaches because the
    TERMINAL record is established, independent of any pass fsync).
    E-3 TERMINAL UNKNOWN + establishing fsync SUCCEEDED (demanded
    by this act), GATE absent ⇒ EXTINGUISHED (V-g12(i)); no append
    owed.
    E-4 TERMINAL UNKNOWN + establishing fsync SUCCEEDED, GATE
    present ⇒ EXTINGUISHED operative + GATE INERT HISTORY
    (V-g12(iii)/V-g12b success halves).
    E-5 TERMINAL UNKNOWN + establishing fsync FAILED ⇒ NEITHER
    extinguished NOR owed (V-g12(ii)); pass outcome is P-SYNCFAIL
    (other acts in the pass: everything depending on that fsync
    classifies nothing; independently established acts keep their
    rows — §0/P-SYNCFAIL).
    E-6 TERMINAL UNKNOWN + no establishing fsync issued (the pass
    was REFUSED at §1 before the fsync the act demands could run —
    since a present UNKNOWN record DEMANDS the fsync, the only
    way to hold this act with no fsync result is a (c1a) refusal
    elsewhere in the prefix) ⇒ UNCLASSIFIED (V-g12b pending case;
    pass outcome P-REFUSE — a refused prefix classifies nothing).
    E-7 GATE live (TERMINAL=none), present + ESTABLISHED, or
    appended successfully under (a) ⇒ CLEARED per (d)(i) — the
    three establishment provenances (own append / own-demanding
    sync / another act's demanding sync) are OUTCOME-EQUIVALENT
    (V-g13); no append owed.
    E-8 GATE live, present + UNSYNCED, establishing fsync DEMANDED
    and FAILED ⇒ UNDER THE BARRIER — neither cleared nor trusted
    for dispatch (V-g3/V-g6); pass outcome P-SYNCFAIL. (A present
    unsynced gate DEMANDS the fsync: if it succeeds the gate is
    established and the row is E-7; if the pass is refused before
    the sync, no row stands — E-9.)
    E-9 GATE live, present, no establishing-fsync result because the
    pass was REFUSED at §1 before the sync ran ⇒ no row stands
    (P-REFUSE precedes — a refused prefix classifies nothing).
    E-10 GATE live, absent, THIS ACT'S APPEND ATTEMPT REACHED (no
    earlier pass abort) ⇒ OWED, appended once under (a);
    append SUCCEEDS ⇒ E-7; append attempt fails ⇒ E-11; any other
    act's establishing fsync result (success or failure) does not
    change this act's owed-ness (an owed append is not an fsync
    demand; V-g11(i) multi-act composition, PR-2 scoped to this
    act): an absent gate demands no establishing fsync, so the
    pass's single establishing fsync — if any — resolves BEFORE
    the (a) append loop begins (§0), and its result neither
    creates nor removes this act's owed-ness; owed-ness changes
    only via this act's own append. An act at E-10 whose append is
    NEVER ATTEMPTED (the pass aborted on another act's failure)
    is E-12, not E-10 (v33 cycle-17 fold C17-1: E-10/E-12 are
    mutually exclusive by attempt-reached).
    E-11 own gate-append FAILED (definite or indeterminate) ⇒
    pass outcome P-APPENDFAIL; definite: act UNSETTLED, gate OWED
    for the next process; indeterminate: bytes may stand (readable
    ≠ proven), resolved only by the next process's (c) (V-g9's
    second gate; V-g5).
    E-12 GATE live, absent, but another act's failure aborts the
    pass before this act's append is attempted ⇒ remains OWED
    (the (a) qualification, C1-2: gates not yet restored stay owed
    for the next process's pass; V-g9's first gate is the
    counter-case — its own append succeeded, so it stands at E-7).
    CONSISTENCE CLAUSES: every reachable (act, pass) combination
    lands in EXACTLY ONE row (or a §1 pass-level outcome that
    classifies nothing); no pair of rows assigns two operative
    classifications to one combination; an act with an ESTABLISHED
    terminal record NEVER clears via (d)(i) (C7-1 — E-2 extinguishes
    rather than clears) and an act with NO established terminal
    record NEVER extinguishes; (c2)'s owed rule is E-10 restated;
    (d)(i)/(ii)/(iii) are the row mechanics for E-7/E-1/E-3.
    Vectors (v31 A2) (v33 cycle-17 fold C17-3: V-g1/V-g2's stated
    outcomes are scoped to a pass reaching that act — a prefix
    refused at (c1a), an establishing sync that fails, or another
    act's failure aborting the pass BEFORE this act's append is
    attempted routes to P-REFUSE / P-SYNCFAIL / E-12 instead — the
    vectors illustrate the single-act success path):
    V-g1 — the log ends in a PARTIAL gate line
    (`{"kind":"cure-gate","id":…` truncated): repair truncates the
    fragment, classification sees NO gate, the act stays owed, and (a)
    appends the gate once. V-g2 — the log ends in a COMPLETE gate line
    missing only its terminating newline: repair KEEPS the record and
    terminates the line; classification sees a valid gate; the (c1)
    establishing sync clears the obligation. V-g3 — a valid gate sits
    in the prefix but the restart's establishing sync FAILS: fail-stop
    (b) recurs; the gate is not dispatched under and not cleared.
    V-g4 — a mid-file corrupt line before the gate: (c0) VALIDATION
    rejects the file (`loadSession`-class) and throws BEFORE the file
    is touched (§13.1), the fail-stop recurs, and the episode advances
    nothing.
    V-g5 (v31 C1-1) — the gate append returns an error AFTER bytes were
    transferred (readable in the cache, fsync outcome unknown): that is
    INDETERMINATE, never definite — this process neither re-appends nor
    dispatches; a full-line readable copy may exist, and only (c)
    resolves it (repair keeps a complete line, (c1) sync establishes or
    fails). V-g6 (v31 C1-1) — repair terminated a complete gate line
    (V-g2 state) and the establishing sync then FAILS: the terminated

    cleared, nothing dispatches; the next restart re-runs (c) from

    V-g7 (v31 cycle-2 fold C2-1) — a validly shaped `cure-gate` sits at
    log position 1 and its `residual-cure` act at position 2, with no

    (1) TERMINAL RECORDS FIRST PER (d): a `residual-cure-cancel` or a

    the obligation per (d)(ii)/(iii) REGARDLESS of gate presence —

    stated); A GATE AT A LOG POSITION STRICTLY AFTER ITS OWN act's
    cancellation or settlement is FORBIDDEN (the act was terminal

    BEFORE any establishing sync) as
    ORDERING and one-per-act, fail-stop (b) recurs, NO inert-history

    (2) THEN THE GATE BRANCHES for that otherwise-live act: NO GATE

    SYNC PER (c1) — a gate whose establishing sync FAILS neither

    COMBINATION FAULT (v33 C1-1): a prefix showing BOTH a
    cancellation AND a settlement for the same act is a FORBIDDEN

    v32 cycle-1 fold C1-1 stands: a disposition that restores

    V-g9 (v33 audit-of-8c5d987 C1-2 — the two-gate partial-pass

    succeeded — cleared under (d)(i) with no establishing sync
    needed, the sync-before-ack was this process's own successful
    append); the second gate is owed (definite: byte-unchanged,

    V-g10 (v33 audit-of-8c5d987 C2-1 — the both-orderings vector) —

    stands as INERT history: no establishing sync demanded FOR THE

    V-g11 (v33 audit-of-8c5d987 C3-1 — the no-live-gate and O3-invalid

    OUTCOMES SPLIT (v33 post-round audit of 6c004b9, PR-1 — the
    no-append-owed half applies ONLY when the terminal record IS
    established): (success — already durable or the establishing
    fsync SUCCEEDS) THIS act extinguishes, no sync is issued FOR
    THE GATE and no gate append is owed for it (the barrier has no

    acts under their own rules, and PASS-LEVEL SUCCESS IS NOT
    IMPLIED HERE (v33 post-round-2 audit of 2c085c8, PR-2) — the
    pass completes normally only if EVERY other act in it also
    completes: another act's establishing-sync or gate-append
    failure fail-stops the whole pass per (a)/(b). THIS act's
    extinguishment STANDS across another act's failure — by EITHER
    establishment provenance, stated separately (v33 post-round-3
    audit of 650abe1, PR-3: the earlier single-provenance "the
    establishing fsync already established them" was FALSE for the
    already-durable path): a terminal record ALREADY DURABLE by its
    originating sync is established regardless of any pass fsync,
    and another act's later failure cannot un-establish it; a
    record established by the PASS's establishing fsync stands
    because that fsync SUCCEEDED and, per (c1c) (C6-1), NO SECOND
    ESTABLISHING FSYNC IS ISSUED in this pass — a later
    establishing-sync failure is UNREACHABLE; only an
    APPEND failure for another act can occur, and appends do not
    un-establish anything; (failure — the establishing fsync FAILS)
    the pass FAIL-STOPS per (b): nothing proceeds, no append is
    owed or made for this act, no boundary is evaluated, and the
    episode advances nothing until the next restart re-runs (c). (ii) an O3-INVALID prefix (V-g10 (ii)
    or its settlement variant, or the forbidden cancellation+settlement
    combination): (c1a) REFUSES the prefix BEFORE any establishing
    sync — there is no state in which a sync precedes the check that
    decides whether any sync is needed; fail-stop (b) recurs and
    nothing is cleared, synced, or appended.
    V-g12 (v33 audit-of-8c5d987 C4-1 — the unestablished terminal
    record vectors) — a supervisor appends a cancellation (or a
    fresh-route settlement) and its fsync outcome is UNKNOWN when the
    process exits; on restart the complete terminal record is
    readable, passes validation and (c1a). Four cases: (i) NO
    preceding gate, establishing fsync SUCCEEDS ⇒ the terminal record
    is established durable ⇒ extinguishment per (d)(ii)/(iii). (ii)
    NO preceding gate, establishing fsync FAILS ⇒ fail-stop (b): the
    act is NEITHER extinguished (the record is not proven durable)
    NOR classified owed; the bytes stand on disk unestablished and
    the next restart re-runs (c). (iii) WITH a preceding valid gate
    (act < gate < cancel/settle) — OUTCOMES SPLIT (v33 cycle-10
    fold C10-1: the inert classification is part of the terminal-
    first classification and attaches ONLY on success): establishing
    fsync SUCCEEDS ⇒ the act extinguishes and the gate is INERT
    HISTORY (it never demanded a sync of its own; the SAME single
    file-level fsync established the terminal record); establishing
    fsync FAILS ⇒ NO TERMINAL-FIRST CLASSIFICATION ATTACHES TO THIS
    ACT OR ITS GATE (v33 cycle-17 fold C17-4: the claim is
    act-scoped — per P-SYNCFAIL/§0, records established
    INDEPENDENTLY of the failed fsync, e.g. another act's terminal
    record durable by its originating sync, keep their
    classification) — the act is neither
    extinguished nor owed AND the gate is neither inert-classified,
    cleared, nor trusted for dispatch — fail-stop (b) as in case
    (ii), the next restart re-runs (c). (iv) the record's originating fsync is known
    SUCCESSFUL (e.g., the appending process is still the same
    process) ⇒ already durable, no re-sync demanded. The rule is the
    gate rule generalized: EVERY decision record relied on at
    recovery — gate, cancellation, or settlement — must be
    established durable (own fsync) before it clears, extinguishes,
    or is trusted.
    V-g12b (v33 audit-of-8c5d987 C5-1 — V-g8's own branch list now
    covers the terminal-establishment cases): a dispositioned
    restart whose validated prefix holds act → cancellation (or
    settlement) with UNKNOWN originating fsync and no gate: (1)
    terminal-first applies only if the establishing fsync SUCCEEDS
    (extinguishment); if it FAILS the act is NEITHER extinguished
    NOR owed — fail-stop (b), the next restart re-runs (c); the
    live-act gate branches (2) are reached only for an act with no
    ESTABLISHED terminal record. Same with a valid preceding gate —
    OUTCOMES SPLIT (v33 cycle-10 fold C10-1): on SUCCESS the act
    extinguishes and the gate is inert history; on FAILURE neither
    the extinguishment nor the inert classification attaches — the
    gate is neither cleared nor trusted — fail-stop (b); the
    outcome turns on the terminal
    record's establishment alone.
    V-g13 (v33 audit-of-8c5d987 C6-1 — the one-fsync-for-all-records
    vector) — one pass over a prefix with TWO acts: act A has a
    readable cancellation with UNKNOWN originating fsync; act B is
    live with a readable gate (unknown fsync). (c1a) passes. The
    pass issues ONE file-level establishing fsync (demanded by A at
    (c1b)): it SUCCEEDS ⇒ A extinguishes AND B's gate is ESTABLISHED
    in the same operation — no second fsync is issued or required
    for B, B's obligation clears, and the "A's sync succeeded but
    B's gate sync failed" combination is UNREACHABLE. If the single
    fsync FAILS, the whole pass fails per (b): A is neither
    extinguished nor owed and B's gate is neither cleared nor
    trusted; the next restart retries. Establishment is per-file:
    there is no per-record durability state after one successful
    post-(c1a) fsync.
    (d) CLEARING (C10-2, C11-1 — three cases, all already-durable or
    durable-by-restore; "durable" throughout means ESTABLISHED
    DURABLE — a readable record with unknown originating fsync is
    established by the restart's own fsync per (c1b)/(c1c), v33
    C4-1) AND classified per (c1a)/(c1b) first (v33 cycle-7 fold
    C7-1 — the three cases apply only AFTER the semantic checks and
    terminal-first classification): (i) a valid gate is durable (found on restart
    per (c1), establishing sync included, or appended successfully
    under (a)) ⇒ the obligation clears, PROVIDED the act has no
    ESTABLISHED cancellation or settlement — an act extinguished at
    (c1b) is NOT cleared by (d)(i); its gate is inert history and
    the extinguishment (d)(ii)/(iii) is the operative classification
    (cross-reference (c1b)). (ii) a
    `residual-cure-cancel` ALREADY DURABLE at recovery (established
    per (c1b) if its fsync outcome was unknown) ⇒ extinguished
    (`cure-already-cancelled`). (iii) a settlement ALREADY DURABLE at
    recovery (established per (c1b) likewise) ⇒ extinguished (`cure-already-settled`; the fresh-route
    settlement that landed without a gate, as stated above). A NEW
    cancellation or NEW settlement is NOT a way through the barrier: the
    barrier refuses every append until the gate is restored, so neither
    can be appended ahead of an owed gate to clear it.
    AT MOST ONE `cure-gate` record per
    `cureActId` — a second gate for the same act is refused (the
    id-uniqueness rule inherited from settlement; otherwise nonce
    binding would be nondeterministic). If the act is already
    CANCELLED — OR ALREADY SETTLED (v29 R5-C21-1 — audit of 2cca082:
    the fresh-finding route settles WITHOUT a gate, so a confirmed cure
    can be settled while its gate is still owed) — at recovery time,
    the owed completion is EXTINGUISHED (v28 R5-C20P-6: cancellation is
    terminal-by-cancellation per NDR-l and nothing may dispatch under a
    cancelled act; v29: a settled act is closed history and no gated
    repro for it can be dispatched any longer). A `cure-gate` appended
    for a cancelled OR settled act is malformed, refused — the cancelled
    code is `cure-already-cancelled` (shared with the cancel op's
    refusal) and the settled code is `cure-already-settled`; the two
    acts can never both demand it. A settlement that lands BEFORE the
    gate is an accepted, closed fresh-route outcome; no gate is owed for
    it, and an accepted-fix settlement cannot precede its gate (its
    evidence requires the gate, see (b3)).
    ORDERING (v29 R5-C21-2 — replay-checked, not merely declared;
    v29 R5-C21-9: the qualification "if a gated run exists" governs
    the gate-to-run edge — every gate follows its act; an UNUSED gate,
    e.g. a crash after gate append and before dispatch, is valid history
    PROVIDED it passes the other applicable checks (v33 C3-2 alignment);
    v31 cycle-2 fold C2-1: the gate-to-act edge is checked on EVERY
    gate, run or no run — the run-conditional phrasing left an unused
    gate that precedes its act with no stated refusal; v33 cycle-2
    fold C2-1 adds the third edge (O3) below; v33 cycle-3 fold C3-1:
    all THREE run at (c1a) — over the repaired prefix, BEFORE any
    establishing sync, so a malformed prefix is never synced): replay
    runs THREE
    independent checks. (O1) EVERY `cure-gate` record, whether or not
    any run exists: its `cureActId` MUST resolve in-log to a
    `residual-cure` act at a STRICTLY EARLIER durable position — an
    unresolvable act or a gate at/before its act is malformed, refused
    (vector V-g7: a validly shaped gate at position 1, its act at
    position 2, no run — refused by O1, not "valid unused history").
    (O2) for every GATED run (a `repro-run` with non-null `cureGateId`)
    the durable log positions are STRICTLY `residual-cure` act <
    `cure-gate` < `repro-run` — replay refuses a gated run whose gate
    is not after the act or not before the run. (O3 — v33 audit-of-8c5d987
    C2-1) for every `cure-gate`, its durable log position is STRICTLY
    EARLIER than every TERMINAL record for the same act
    (`residual-cure-cancel` or settlement): a gate at or after its own
    act's cancellation or settlement is malformed, refused — the act was
    terminal when that gate would have been appended and a gate for a
    terminal act is refused (`cure-already-cancelled`/
    `cure-already-settled`); O1 and O2 do NOT catch this (such a gate
    still follows its act). The valid orderings are act < gate <
    cancel/settle (the gate was legal at append; the later terminal
    record extinguishes and the gate is inert history per (d)) and,
    for a fresh-route settlement, act < settle with no gate at all. O2's
    run < settlement edge is required
    ONLY where a settlement cites that run as its `evidenceRef` (v29
    R5-C21-5, from the cycle-1 audit: a red or abandoned gated run has no
    settlement and must still be classifiable, not refused). A gated run
    never cited by any settlement is ordinary gated-but-unevidential
    history: it contributes no clearing and is not an error. What the log cannot show is the wall-clock
    dispatch instant; that the dispatch followed the gate's DURABLE
    append is the TA-5 supervisor-discipline obligation, declared
    trust, not replay-verified.
    Recovery NEVER fabricates
    evidence: any run dispatched before the gate existed cannot
    contain a nonce that did not exist at its execution time and
    fails `cureGateOk` forever; recovery only makes the
    RE-dispatch correctly gated. The cancel-only alternative
    (D1=B) was rejected by the owner 2026-11-22 — it strands an
    executable cure as permanent owner work; complete-the-pair is
    the log's universal recovery direction (owed record before owed
    effect).
    PHASE 2: the supervisor appends a distinct durable settlement
    record `residual-cure-settlement { id, cureActId, evidenceRef, ts,
    route, ancestryWitness|null }` — `ancestryWitness` is the closed
    §14.10.3 accepted-fix shape (REQUIRED non-null exactly when
    `route:"accepted-fix"`, null exactly when `route:"fresh-finding-cycle"`;
    a value under the wrong route or null under accepted-fix is malformed)
    (v28 R5-C20-3 — one shape, defined here and mirrored only by
    reference in the inventory) in the S5 decision log (this kind JOINS the envelope
    record-kind inventory alongside `finding-hold`/`-lift` and the
    §14.10 kinds — v25 R5-C18-3; `route` is copied verbatim from the
    act at append; a settlement whose route differs from its act's
    is malformed, refused; `id` is the deterministic
    `cure-settlement-<cureActId>` — v26 R5-C18F-2, the id is fully
    derivable from the act BEFORE the settlement exists, which is what
    makes the act's effect binding re-checkable (see the effect-binding
    paragraph), and the id-collision refusal IS the one-settlement-
    per-act uniqueness guarantee).
    The settlement is appended ONCE THE EVIDENCE EXISTS AND PASSES THE
    SINGLE EVIDENCE CHECK (v26 R5-C18F-1/F-3 — one predicate,
    machine-checkable at settlement time from durable records only,
    recomputed identically by every replay — v27 R5-C19-4 names the
    replay authority for each operand):
    `accepted-fix` — `evidenceRef` names a `repro-run` record
    `result:"green"` AND (a) its repro definition re-digests to the
    preimage's `reproDigest` against `expectedFixBaseline` AND (b) the
    THREE-CONJUNCT ORDERING WITNESS (v28 R5-C20-3 — replaces v27's
    two-conjunct witness, which proved only record order):
    (b1) ANCESTRY — the settlement's `ancestryWitness` field is the
    closed shape `{ "executedArtifactDigest":"<sha>",
    "expectedFixBaseline":"<sha>", "result":"ancestor-proper" }`
    (the ONLY admissible `result` value; a failed walk appends NO
    settlement, so no false witness is ever durable). Producer: the
    supervisor, at settlement-append, by a git walk against the
    gated candidate lineage pinned in the artifact store (missing,
    pruned, or unverifiable closure FAILS CLOSED; the honesty of the
    object store itself is the declared basis §14.10.0 TA-3).
    Validation: the
    two sha operands EQUAL the run record's `executedArtifactDigest`
    and the preimage's `expectedFixBaseline`, and the digests differ
    (a fix IS a change over the baseline). Replay checks the operands
    and consumes the stored `result`; it never re-walks git.
    (b2) LOG ORDER — the `repro-run` record's S5-log position is
    after the cure act's record.
    (b3) POST-CONFIRMATION CURE GATE (v28 R5-C20-2 — the mechanism
    that makes the run post-confirmation testimony, see §14.10.3
    `cure-gate`): confirmation of the cure act appends a
    supervisor-minted `cure-gate` record
    `{ id, cureActId, nonce }` (separate append, torn-pair-safe via
    the §14.10.3 complete-the-pair recovery, v28 R5-C20F-4). The `repro-run` MUST carry
    `cureGateId` equal to that gate's id, and its `runEvidenceRef` MUST contain the gate
    `nonce` verbatim — substring containment over the durable
    evidence content, predicate pinned in §14.10.3 (v28
    R5-C20F-2). Because the gate id is minted at confirmation
    (or, for an owed completion, at recovery — see the
    complete-the-pair clause), no run recorded before the mint can
    name it; a run whose
    `cureGateId` is absent or names another cure's gate is refused.
    The runner-side obligation to execute the post-confirmation
    candidate and not a cached result is a stated trust residual
    (see §14.10.3 `cure-gate`), checked by the supervisor's append-
    time verification of the echoed nonce.
    `fresh-finding-cycle` — `evidenceRef` names a filed finding (an
    APPLIED `audit-filing` act) whose `claimDigest` re-digests to the
    preimage's `claimDigest` AND whose `cureActRef` field (v27
    R5-C19-3: the DURABLE lineage operand — the wire field added to
    `audit-finding` in §14.10.1; "its lineage cites the cure act" had
    no schema-valid encoding, so replay had no record field to check)
    names the cure act's record id AND (v27 R5-C19-3, split v28 R5-C20P-5: intake checks identity, settlement checks state) if the
    preimage's `reproDigestOrNull` is NON-NULL, the filed finding's
    repro definition re-digests (same digest operation as
    `accepted-fix` (a)) to that committed `reproDigestOrNull` — a
    committed digest is checked on BOTH routes, a mismatch refuses
    settlement (counterexample closed: claim-matching finding with
    unrelated repro E settling a cure that committed D); where
    `reproDigestOrNull` is null (non-falsifiable survivor closure)
    no digest operand applies and none may be invented.
    NO FURTHER CONJUNCT (v26 R5-C18F-3 — the replay text's trailing
    "or the fresh finding itself disposed" is WITHDRAWN: settlement
    requires no disposition on the evidence beyond the check itself —
    a fresh finding enters its own round as ordinary open work and is
    disposed by the ordinary rules on its own record; the cure closes
    the OLD chain's residual question, it does not pre-dispose the
    new finding). ONE settlement per cure act (a second is
    malformed, refused); the settlement's route is the act's
    (never re-litigated); missing evidence OR a failed check ⇒ no
    settlement (the pair stays unsettled — an unsettled cure adds NO
    hold beyond the residual-inherited uncleanliness it exists to
    clear; settlement is owed by EVIDENCE ARRIVAL, never by supervisor
    effort — see the effect-binding paragraph, v26 R5-C18F-2).
    CANCELLATION (v27 R5-C19-5 — closes the LOCKED-PAIR STATE the
    v26 protocol could reach: a confirmed cure whose commitment can
    never be satisfied — e.g. a wrong baseline or claim digest —
    stays unsettled forever AND its immutability blocked every
    corrected cure on the pair, with no exit) is the separate OWNER
    op `residual-cure-cancel` — its own item below.
    One act cures ONE (`findingId`, `survivorId`) pair; the

    `withdrawn` carries

  **Filing replay is an explicit exception to from-record
  reconstruction (v8 R4-C2-7; composition made EXPLICIT v9 R4-C3-5 —
  v8's "the three checks are the check" read as waiving the general
  authority checks, which it never intended: the exception replaces
  ONLY the reconstruction STEP, nothing else):** validation of an
  `audit-filing` act proceeds in four stages, ALL required —
  **(0) ordinary act provenance, unwaived:** the act's channel is a
  valid TTY-confirmed owner-act channel per the general rules, its
  op is in the closed enum, its signature/authority stamps validate,
  its `effectRecordIds` bind exactly one effect record, and the act
  carries no second effect: **`consumed` is a replay-DERIVED state
  named by the bound effect, not a stage-0 precondition (v10
  R5-C4-4 — v9's stage-0 "not already consumed" literally refused
  the redelivery that rule (a) below declares idempotent: on replay
  of an already-applied filing the act IS consumed, and stages
  (1)–(3) re-running against the existing record is exactly the
  recognition intended). FIRST APPLICATION vs REPLAY: stage (0)
  passes when the act's uniquely-bound effect record does not yet
  exist (fresh application — the single-consumption refusal targets
  a SECOND record naming an act whose named effect already exists
  and validates under DIFFERENT bytes or a different effect id,
  which stays refused) or, on replay, when it exists, is the record
  the act names (identity, not coincidence — **stage (0) checks
  EXISTENCE + IDENTITY + single-consumption ONLY, never the
  CONTENT-VALIDATION RESULT (v13 R5-C7-2: "validates under the
  act's op schema" as a stage-(0) gate made the post-effect
  integrity-fault branch unreachable — a validator walking stages
  in order failed at (0) before the stage-(2)/(3) routing existed
  to run)**: a post-effect effect record whose bytes FAIL the
  op-schema/mapping checks is NOT a stage-(0) refusal — it routes
  to its named closed outcome below (damaged record/artifact ⇒
  `owner-filing-integrity-fault`; a record that fails identity or
  a second record naming a consumed act ⇒ the general
  single-consumption refusal), and the four stages are read as:
  (0) provenance + identity, (1) payload re-digest, (2) spool/
  post-success source, (3) full mapping — stages (1)–(3) run over
  the post-effect source and EVERY failure there routes to its
  named closed outcome (drift, mapping, integrity-fault, or
  terminal-by-refusal), none to a silent stage-(0) reject; ordering
  relative to `effectApplied`: `effectApplied` is computed AFTER
  this four-stage replay, from its outcome, never read as an input
  to stage (0);**
  **(1) act digest:** the stored canonical payload re-digests to
  `payloadDigest`; **(2) spool identity / post-success authority
  (v10 R5-C4-5 — v9 made a missing spool unconditionally drift, so
  losing the spool AFTER a successful filing left the effect state
  undefined — terminal-by-refusal describes a never-created finding
  while the finding here exists):** re-hash the durable bytes
  against the payload's `draftSha256`. The verification source
  depends on the act's effect state, **selected by EXISTENCE AND
  IDENTITY of the act-bound effect record, never by a validation
  result (v11 R5-C5-3 — v10 said "exists AND validates", which is
  circular: validation is what the four stages produce, so the mode
  selector must be evaluable BEFORE them):** **(a) PRE-EFFECT (no
  effect record in the log names this act as its bound effect):**
  the source is the SPOOL — missing
  or mismatching spool = `owner-filing-draft-drift` exactly as the
  entry rule states (terminal-by-refusal, drift condition). **(b)
  POST-EFFECT (the act-bound effect record EXISTS — mode selected
  by existence+identity, per above; a record that later FAILS the
  stage-(3) checks routes to the integrity-fault branch below):**
  the durable authority is the IMMUTABLE `findingRef` ARTIFACT,
  not the spool — the intake invariant "confirmed bytes, spool
  bytes, stored bytes, and attested digest are ONE byte-string"
  means re-hashing the stored `findingRef` bytes against
  `draftSha256` is the SAME test on equal-strength bytes; a
  missing/corrupt spool with a validating `findingRef` is NOT
  drift, NOT an outstanding effect, NOT terminal-by-refusal — the
  act remains APPLIED. The supervisor appends a `spool-loss-
  post-filing` ADVISORY record (supervisor-authored, envelope-
  carried; fields `{ lossTs, actId, findingId, verifiedBy:
  "findingRef" }`): the finding is NEVER retracted, re-filed, or
  duplicated by it (append-only; the record's existence or absence
  never changes the effect state), it carries NO needs-owner
  condition — the evidence chain is intact through `findingRef` —
  and it exists so the operator sees spool GC damage; re-filing
  the identical bytes is permitted (new act, new finding, chain
  table governs) but NEVER required to clear anything; **if the
  bound effect record or its `findingRef` artifact FAILS the
  stage-(3) checks post-effect (corrupt record, artifact whose
  bytes fail the mapping): the act is NEITHER silently APPLIED
  NOR silently drift — fail closed to a durable `owner-filing-
  integrity-fault` needs-owner condition naming the act and the
  failing check (a third named condition, distinct from drift and
  mapping: post-hoc artifact damage is an integrity fault, not an
  intake refusal); it is class O (owner-only) in the §14.12.2
  finalization table, **the fault record itself is
  supervisor-authored and envelope-carried with fields `{ faultTs,
  actId, failingCheck:"effect-record"|"findingRef-artifact"|
  "intake-refusal"|"act-payload"|
  "readjudication-group"(v17 R5-C11-3 — corrupted withdrawal

  self-contradictory record field,**
  evidenceRefs[] }` — **dedup identity is PER-CHECK KIND (v14

  re-adjudication outcome record lands. **SERIALIZED ADJUDICATION
