  on the outcome" while the outcome shape had NO field to record
  it in, so the observation was claimed-durable but durable
  nowhere): `bytesSource` REQUIRED — **CANONICAL LABELS (v19
  R5-C13-3 — v18 attributed digest-matching bytes to
  `"embedded-R1"` "or" byte-identical fresh-spool content with
  replay accepting either: two validators on the same durable
  prefix could pick different labels, and `"embedded-R1"`
  described bytes that might not exist in R1 at all; the
  physical source is UNOBSERVABLE from durable records, so the
  label must be a function of content only. `"embedded-R1"` is
  DELETED from the closed enum; the closed set is
  `"content-addressed"|"fresh-spool"|"none"`):**
  `"content-addressed"` exactly when the bytes the adjudication
  consumed RE-DIGEST to the act's `draftSha256` (any outcome
  kind, any physical source — embed, MIXED bytes, or a fresh
  spool read whose content happens to match: the digest match
  against the act IS the provenance; `observedSha256:null` —
  the digest is already durable on the act, recording it again
  is new noise, not new information); `"fresh-spool"` only when
  NO EMBEDDED BYTES EXIST (a draft-derivative condition judged
  over observed bytes the record names by `observedSha256` —
  `observedSha256` non-null = sha256 of the bytes actually
  used; a MIXED refusal's `adjudicatedDraftBytes` NEVER take
  this label — a MIXED R2 whose bytes fail the act-digest
  re-check is MALFORMED, never a canonical `fresh-spool`
  outcome, v20 R5-C14-4 — see the admission rule below); under
  the current admission rules no refusal class admits embedded-
  bytes-absent content (draft-derivative and MIXED refusals
  always embed their digest-verified bytes; spool-mismatch/
  absent routes to the drift `"none"` class), so
  `"fresh-spool"` is a RESERVED label with no current domain:
  the validator NEVER fabricates it, and one appearing on an
  outcome without a durable non-embedded-bytes basis is a
  malformed outcome (fail closed);
  `"none"` only
  for FILESYSTEM-OBSERVATION (drift) refusals where no draft
  bytes exist to consume (v18 R5-C12-2 correction: v17's
  example — "the append-legality gate refused before any
  byte-reading check" — was FALSE: the gate's checks read the
  verified bytes (MIXED class), so its R2 is never `"none"`);
  `observedSha256` non-null EXACTLY when `bytesSource ==
  "fresh-spool"` (the digest of the bytes actually used;
  replay cross-validates: a `refused` outcome with
  `bytesSource:"fresh-spool"` requires
  `observedSha256 == sha256(bytes R2 adjudicated)` — under the
  v20 reserved-label rule this cross-check is VACUOUS (no
  current refusal class fills `"fresh-spool"`; if a future
  class does, it names its durable byte authority there); a
  mismatch is a malformed outcome, never appended; an `applied`
  outcome's digest stands as the observed-once provenance record
  (the finding's own effect validation is its check; the spool
  need not persist)) — **RECOVERY-RECONSTRUCTIBILITY AMENDMENT
  (v18 R5-C12-2 — v17's crash-recovery rule requires recording a
  LANDED effect "WITHOUT re-running the adjudication", but a
  finding effect carries NO field distinguishing whether its
  bytes came from R1's embed or a fresh spool read (finding
  admission is content-addressed: it records the digest only),
  so recovery could not fill `bytesSource` from durable evidence
  — it would have to GUESS or re-run, contradicting the rule;
  and a re-run's spool read would attribute provenance to an
  observation the crash-time adjudication actually performed; the
  label vocabulary and single-label rule are per NDR-e, the
  recovery-duty totality per NDR-k — this clause is a DECLARED
  BOUNDED EXPANSION of NDR-e (v25 R5-C18-6: superseding v24
  R5-C17-6's "application site" classification — the case-level
  assignment algorithm below is normative rule content, so it is
  declared in NDR-e's *Expansion:* set; a fold that changes it must
  sweep NDR-e in the same commit; recovery-duty totality remains
  per NDR-k):
  `bytesSource`/`observedSha256` are DETERMINISTIC FUNCTIONS OF
  DURABLE RECORDS ONLY — replay-computable for any landed
  effect, so recovery always fills them without re-running:
  (i) `outcome:"refused"` — from R2's own durable fields, ONE
  label per content state (v19 R5-C13-3 — the v18 dual-label
  choice for digest-matching MIXED bytes is DELETED; there is
  no "OR" left anywhere in this rule): a DRAFT-DERIVATIVE R2
  (its condition is about the bytes themselves — parse/enum/
  claim — and those bytes re-digest to `draftSha256` by the
  refusal condition's own construction) ⇒
  `bytesSource:"content-addressed"`, `observedSha256:null`; a
  MIXED R2: its `adjudicatedDraftBytes` MUST re-digest to the
  act's `draftSha256` (the general refusal-validation admission
  rule, mixed class: the header operands come from the verified
  bytes — the digest check is CONSTITUTIVE of a MIXED refusal,
  never waivable by a provenance label, v20 R5-C14-4) — match ⇒
  `bytesSource:"content-addressed"`,
  `observedSha256:null` (the digest match against the act is
  content-only and durable — no attribution to embed vs
  byte-identical spool is made or needed); MISMATCH ⇒ the R2 is
  NOT a valid refusal candidate at all (embedded bytes failing
  the digest → the general malformed-record integrity-fault
  route; at recovery it fails re-validation ⇒ group-fault path,
  never a recorded outcome) — the v19 `!=` ⇒ `"fresh-spool"`
  branch is DELETED (it labeled a record the admission rule had
  already refused, letting an outcome label waive the act-byte
  binding);
  legality-gate R2 is MIXED (it embeds the bytes the gate
  consumed, R5-C12-3) ⇒ computed exactly as the MIXED case
  above; `"none"` REMAINS for the FILESYSTEM-OBSERVATION
  refusals (spool-absent/mismatch drift — no draft bytes exist
  to consume; self-evidenced by R2's own `spoolObserved`
  fields, null `observedSha256` here is REQUIRED: those
  refusals carry their observation in their own fields, not in
  the outcome); applied effects use "content-addressed";**
  (ii) `outcome:"applied"` —
  the finding effect is SELF-EVIDENCED: its recorded content
  re-digests to the act's `draftSha256` (admission condition),
  so the bytes' identity is proven by the effect record itself
  and the SOURCE question (embed vs byte-identical spool) can
  only ever have had byte-identical answers — `bytesSource:
  "content-addressed"`, `observedSha256:null` (provenance is
  the effect record's own digest match; no observation field is
  needed or meaningful — the same canonical label as the
  digest-matching refused case, v19 R5-C13-3: ONE rule for
  digest-matching bytes regardless of outcome kind); the cross-
  validation rule is unchanged where applicable. Determinism
  clause (2) (all replays agree) holds LITERALLY (v19
  R5-C13-3 — v18 needed a "content-vacuous exception" because
  its rule admitted two labels; with the canonical content-only
  labels every value is a strict function of durable records,
  one answer per prefix, no exception needed).**
  **OUTCOME DEPENDENCE AND SAME-ACT
  BINDING (v16 R5-C10-6 — the nullable ids were outcome-free, so
  `applied` naming an unrelated finding, or `refused` naming
  another act's refusal, validated vacuously):**
  `outcome:"applied"` ⇒ `findingId` REQUIRED (the log record id
  of the finding the adjudication minted — it MUST resolve in-log
  to an `audit-finding` record whose originating act is the
  fault's act A, appended in the same critical section) and
  `refusalRecordId` MUST be null; `outcome:"refused"` ⇒
  `refusalRecordId` REQUIRED (MUST resolve in-log to an
  intake-refusal record of act A — `refusedActId == A` —
  appended in the same critical section, bound per NDR-d
  (class-dependent binding — PINNED refusals to P(W), legality-gate
  refusals to their own append-time prefix; mode determined by the
  refusal's own derivation and replay-checkable either way per NDR-d,
  not restated here), carrying its class-required
  `adjudicatedDraftBytes` so R2 is independently validatable)
  and `findingId` MUST be null; any violation is a malformed
  outcome, never appended. **PINNED-VERDICT RECORDING (v18
  R5-C12-4 — v17's legality-gate paragraph asserted "the P(W)
  verdict stands recorded on the outcome regardless" while the
  outcome shape had NO field for it (claimed-durable, durable
  nowhere — the same defect class R5-C11-4 fixed for the byte
  provenance): the outcome now RECORDS the pinned adjudication's
  own verdict separately from the final landed outcome.
  `pinnedVerdict` REQUIRED: the P(W) adjudication's verdict —
  `"eligible"` (the pinned-prefix verdict found the effect
  appendable; the legality gate then decided the landing) or
  `"refused"` (the pinned-prefix verdict itself refused — the
  landed refusal R2 derives from P(W) and binds P(W) per the
  PINNED class of the two-class exception, v19 R5-C13-5). `pinnedVerdictCode` REQUIRED null when
  `pinnedVerdict:"eligible"`, REQUIRED non-null (the refusal
  diagnostic code the P(W) adjudication derived) when
  `"refused"`. Replay binding: (1) `outcome:"refused"` with R2
  bound to P(W) ⇒ `pinnedVerdict:"refused"` and
  `pinnedVerdictCode == R2.diagnosticCode` (MIXED codes
  re-derived jointly over P(W) + R2's embedded bytes per
  R5-C10-3 must equal it); (2) `outcome:"refused"` with R2 bound
  under the GENERAL rule (a legality-gate refusal, R5-C11-2) ⇒
  `pinnedVerdict:"eligible"` and `pinnedVerdictCode:null` — R2's
  code comes from the append-time prefix, NOT the pinned one,
  and this pair is exactly what distinguishes the two refusal
  kinds a plain `outcome:"refused"` cannot; (3)
  `outcome:"applied"` ⇒ `pinnedVerdict:"eligible"`
  (`pinnedVerdictCode:null`) — a pinned refusal cannot mint an
  effect; a mismatch on any clause is a malformed outcome,
  never appended (and determinism clause (3) re-checks the
  pinned re-derivation against these fields, fail closed).**
  **APPEND ORDER within the critical
  section: W → effect (the minted finding record OR refusal R2)
  → outcome LAST (the outcome's required id is what closes the
  group — it names the effect that actually landed).**
  **CRASH RECOVERY, REFINED (v16 R5-C10-6, enumeration made
  EXHAUSTIVE v17 R5-C11-3 — v16 defined one-valid / no-candidate
  / two-same-kind but one candidate of EACH kind satisfied the
  per-kind cardinality and matched no defined outcome, and an
  invalid candidate matched none either):** W durable, outcome
  absent — recovery enumerates ALL candidates over the UNION of
  both kinds (any `audit-finding` record with originating act A
  appended after W; any refusal of A bound to P(W) or per the
  legality-gate binding appended after W), and every candidate
  MUST re-validate (schema + same-act
  clauses above); **EXACTLY ONE valid candidate (of either kind)
  ⇒ recovery appends the
  matching outcome RECORDING that effect WITHOUT re-running the
  adjudication (no second effect is possible — any further
  effect for A is refused: a second applied effect collides with
  the finding's intake state, a second R2 collides with R2's
  terminal-by-refusal standing). **PINNED-VERDICT RECONSTRUCTION
  AT RECOVERY (v19 R5-C13-4 — "without re-running the
  adjudication" is LITERALLY TRUE only for the effect's own
  fields; `pinnedVerdict` is about P(W), which R2's record does
  not carry, so recovery is granted ONE replay-only duty:
  deterministically RE-DERIVE the pinned verdict over P(W)
  (durable) + the candidate's embedded/re-digesting bytes —
  validation, not adjudication: the re-derivation APPENDS
  NOTHING and mints no effect, exactly the replay operation
  §14.10.3 validation already performs on every load — so the
  no-re-run rule prohibits re-ADJUDICATING (choosing an outcome
  and appending it), not verifying a landed record; a second
  effect remains impossible regardless).** THE DUTY SPLIT BY
  CANDIDATE KIND (v20 R5-C14-3 — v19 wrote the duty as if every
  single candidate were a refusal with draft bytes to consume;
  it is not, and the v19 text could not produce the applied
  outcome nor handle byte-free drift refusals): recovery first
  classifies the ONE candidate, then runs the matching check —
  (a) APPLIED finding (no refusal): its own effect validation
  (finding bytes vs act payload vs append-time legality) IS the
  verification it owes; the pinned-verdict check re-derives the
  P(W) verdict over P(W) + the finding's durable bytes and
  requires `eligible` — a re-derived REFUSAL code contradicts
  the landed applied effect (pinned-input violation) ⇒ invalid
  candidate ⇒ group-fault path, never an outcome; conforming ⇒
  outcome records `outcome:"applied"`,
  `pinnedVerdict:"eligible"`, `pinnedVerdictCode:null`.
  **DURABLE BYTE AUTHORITY for this re-derivation (v21
  R5-C15-2 — "the finding's durable/re-digesting bytes" named
  no artifact: the `audit-finding` record carries `claim`,
  `claimDigest` and `findingRef`, and a digest does not
  reconstruct parseable bytes):** the authority is the
  finding's IMMUTABLE `findingRef` ARTIFACT — written at
  intake when the supervisor copied the adjudicated spool bytes
  there (§14.10.3 intake: "confirmed bytes, spool bytes, stored
  bytes, and attested digest are ONE byte-string"), and bound
  TWO-WAYS: `sha256(findingRef bytes) ==` the record's
  `claimDigest` AND `==` the act's `draftSha256`; the
  re-derivation PARSES that artifact (header + body) exactly
  as intake parsed the spool draft, over P(W). Missing
  artifact / transient read failure ⇒ retry (same route as a
  transient spool failure); deterministic digest mismatch
  against either bound ⇒ the artifact is damaged — NOT a
  replay contradiction to paper over: this is exactly the
  post-effect `findingRef-artifact` damage the ordinary
  intake/replay path already routes to
  `owner-filing-integrity-fault` — recovery takes the SAME
  route through the group-fault path (a damaged candidate
  fails re-validation ⇒ R5-C11-3 group fault), never records
  an outcome.
  (b) PINNED refusal (P(W)-bound): re-derive over P(W) + its
  embedded/re-digesting bytes; the re-derived code MUST equal
  `diagnosticCode` (else forged ⇒ group-fault path); conforming
  ⇒ `pinnedVerdict:"refused"`, `pinnedVerdictCode ==` the
  re-derived code. (c) GATE refusal (predecessor-bound,
  R5-C11-2): its collision diagnostic is verified over its
  APPEND-TIME prefix by the ordinary refusal-validation rule;
  the pinned duty re-derives the P(W) verdict (the gate consumed
  P(W)-pinned inputs + append-time state) and requires
  `eligible` — a re-derived REFUSAL code means the gate refusal
  asserts `eligible` against a pinned-REFUSED prefix ⇒ forged,
  group-fault path; the assertion is PROVEN by the re-derivation,
  not trusted from the binding mode; conforming ⇒
  `pinnedVerdict:"eligible"`, `pinnedVerdictCode:null`.
  (d) BYTE-FREE drift refusal (`bytesSource:"none"` —
  filesystem-observation refusal, e.g. absent spool; permitted
  R5-C12-2): NO draft bytes exist to consume, so the duty runs
  over the refusal record's OWN RECORDED filesystem observation
  (`spoolObserved` fields — the durable historical observation;
  current filesystem state NEVER substitutes, same rule as
  intake), re-deriving the drift verdict over P(W) + that
  recorded observation; mismatch ⇒ invalid candidate ⇒
  group-fault path; conforming ⇒ `pinnedVerdict:"refused"`,
  `pinnedVerdictCode ==` the re-derived drift diagnostic ==
  R2's own `diagnosticCode` (v21 R5-C15-1 — v20 said "set to
  the re-derived verdict (eligibility-shaped drift refusals
  record `eligible`/null...)", but a drift refusal is a
  terminal refusal BOUND TO P(W) (the first exception class),
  and replay binding clause (1) requires EVERY P(W)-bound
  refused outcome to carry `pinnedVerdict:"refused"` + code ==
  R2's diagnostic: an `eligible`/null pair on a P(W)-bound
  refusal is malformed, so NO drift case is ever
  "eligibility-shaped" — the pinned re-derivation of a drift
  candidate can only ever return the drift refusal itself (the
  `spoolObserved` evidence is what P(W)'s drift check
  consumed); a re-derivation returning `eligible` contradicts
  the landed refusal ⇒ forged candidate ⇒ group-fault path.
  Replay vector, byte-free drift (closing the vector-list
  gap): W → drift refusal R2 bound to P(W)
  (`bytesSource:"none"`, `spoolObserved` set, null
  `observedSha256`) → outcome `refused` + `"none"`/null
  provenance + `pinnedVerdict:"refused"` + code ==
  R2.diagnosticCode, re-derived over P(W) + `spoolObserved` ⇒
  the unique valid group; any other pair on a P(W)-bound drift
  refusal ⇒ malformed, never appended).
  Failure route, all kinds: re-derivation FAILS transiently ⇒
  retry; fails deterministically ⇒ the prefix contradicts the
  pinned-input guarantee ⇒ group-fault path; candidate/check
  mismatch ⇒ group fault, never an outcome); NO candidate effect ⇒ recovery
  re-runs the adjudication over P(W) (with the append-legality
  gate); TWO OR MORE candidates of ANY combination, or a
  candidate failing re-validation ⇒ a nonconforming-writer /
  damaged-history state: recovery NEVER picks a winner, appends
  an `owner-filing-integrity-fault` of the NEW failingCheck kind
  `"readjudication-group"` (v17 R5-C11-3 — the closed enum had
  no kind for a corrupted withdrawal group, so the mandated fail
  closed was unrepresentable: identity is a DAMAGE kind,
  `(actId, failingCheck)` — one physical fact per act, open or
  disposed; `refusalRecordId` REQUIRED NULL per R5-C9-4 (damage
  kind), the corrupted candidates are named in `evidenceRefs[]`;
  boundary UNCLEAN + needs-owner through the fault)** —
  the fault's ONLY exit is `filing-integrity-disposition` with
  outcome `withdrawn` (`refiled` INEXPRESSIBLE — a corrupted
  group establishes no trustworthy result to replace, same rule
  as `act-payload`); withdrawing a `readjudication-group` fault
  RETIRES THE GROUP: no readjudication is owed (re-adjudicating
  would re-enter the corrupted group) and the act is TERMINAL-
  BY-DAMAGE with its claim RETIRED (v19 R5-C13-1/2 — NOT a
  return to terminal-by-refusal: the R1 a group fault names was
  fault-adjudicated INVALID — that adjudication is why the
  withdrawal existed — and an invalid refusal is never restored
  to live standing nor made a resolution target by a later
  disposition; if the audit trail shows R1 was in fact VALID
  when the intake-refusal fault was withdrawn (the group arose
  by candidate corruption, not R1's invalidity — both shapes
  are reachable), the same rule applies unchanged: the group's
  OWN damage, not R1's status, terminalizes the act, so replay
  needs no case split; the disposition record is the clearing
  evidence — no class-B item, no class-O item);
  the group fault never silently discharges and never re-mints.
  (c) adjudication inputs are ONLY
  replay-reconstructible things per check class (v16 R5-C10-3):
  the LOG-DERIVATIVE codes over the
  PINNED prefix; DRAFT-DERIVATIVE codes over R1's embedded
  `adjudicatedDraftBytes` IF they re-digest to the act's
  `draftSha256`, else a fresh spool read AT adjudication time
  (observed-once, recorded on the outcome — a refusal outcome
  carries its own `spoolObserved` fields like any refusal);
  **MIXED codes (the correction diagnostics) over the PINNED
  prefix AND the digest-verified bytes TOGETHER — same byte-
  source rule as the draft-derivative case; R2 (a new refusal
  of a MIXED or draft-derivative code) MUST embed its OWN
  `adjudicatedDraftBytes` (the bytes the adjudication actually
  used — R1's if they re-digested, else the fresh spool read,
  recorded observed-once on the outcome), so R2 is
  independently validatable without the spool.**
  **APPEND-LEGALITY GATE (v17 R5-C11-2 — the frozen prefix pins
  the adjudication's VERDICT INPUTS; it does NOT exempt the
  resulting effect from intake legality at append time: after W
  a distinct owner filing C may validly correct A's target T,
  and appending A's finding unconditionally would produce an
  illegal graph (at most ONE correction per target), while
  re-adjudicating against the current prefix silently moves the
  frozen verdict — v16 specified no valid outcome for either.
  Rule: once the P(W) adjudication finds the effect eligible to
  append (initial run or recovery re-run), the supervisor — in
  the SAME S5 flock critical section — evaluates over the THEN-
  CURRENT prefix the same MIXED-class intake-legality checks a
  fresh append of A's finding would pass (lineage linearity: the
  target carries no other correction; target state; severity/
  route comparisons) together with the verified draft bytes.
  Legal ⇒ the effect + outcome append as specified. A legality
  COLLISION ⇒ the effect is NOT appended; instead a refusal R2
  carrying the ORDINARY diagnostic selected by the CLOSED
  MAPPING OF GATE FAILURES TO DIAGNOSTICS (v18 R5-C12-3 — v17
  named only `correction-ambiguity` ("the same code ordinary
  intake produces for a double correction"), but the gate checks
  MORE than double-correction: a target that CLOSED after W (or
  was never a valid correction target) fails the TARGET-STATE
  check, and a severity/route comparison failure is neither a
  linearity collision nor ambiguity — mandating one code for all
  gate failures produced a refusal that fails its own MIXED
  re-derivation over the append-time prefix (the prefix supports
  the REAL diagnostic, not the mandated one), converting a legal
  gate outcome into a spurious integrity fault. Mapping (first
  failing check in this FIXED PRIORITY wins — deterministic,
  one code per prefix): (1) target carries another standing
  correction ⇒ `correction-ambiguity`; (2) target not in a
  correctable state (open, or closed outside the correctable
  set) ⇒ `correction-bad-target`; (3) proposed severity below
  the target's ⇒ `correction-severity-decrease`; (4) proposed
  route ≠ target's ⇒ `correction-route-mismatch`; the selected
  code is the SAME code ordinary intake would produce for the
  SAME verified bytes over the SAME append-time prefix (no new
  diagnostic; R2 is a MIXED refusal: it embeds the draft bytes
  the gate consumed and binds its APPEND-TIME prefix under the
  GENERAL rule, so its MIXED re-derivation over that prefix +
  those bytes yields exactly the selected code — the refusal
  that the general refusal-validation rule then honors without
  exception).
  R2 appends
  as an ORDINARY permanent refusal bound under the GENERAL rule
  to its own predecessor (the current prefix at append time —
  NOT P(W), because its derivation consumed that prefix; the
  R5-C10-2 P(W) exception covers only refusals whose verdict
  consumed P(W)); the outcome records `outcome:"refused"`
  naming it. What the frozen adjudication guarantees — and what
  determinism clause (3) re-checks — is PINNED VERDICT INPUTS,
  never that a later log cannot change intake legality; every
  append in this contract, including this one, must satisfy the
  legality of the prefix it appends against, so no illegal graph
  is ever produced and no verdict is silently changed (the P(W)
  verdict stands recorded on the outcome regardless; the
  legality refusal is a separate, named, separately validatable
  event).**
  (d)
  CRASH RULE: disposition durable, outcome absent (lock released
  by crash) ⇒ recovery re-runs the SAME adjudication over the
  SAME PINNED prefix (the record, not the wall clock, defines the
  inputs; unrelated appends in between CANNOT change the pinned
  prefix or its verdicts — the log-derivative verdict is fixed;
  only the observed-once filesystem input may differ, and its
  observation belongs to the outcome that actually lands — with
  the landed-effect recovery path above, an effect already on the
  log is never re-adjudicated, only recorded); the
  determinism the contract promises is: (1) exactly one outcome
  record per withdrawal, (2) ALL replays agree with the landed
  outcome forever (no re-adjudication after the outcome exists),
  (3) the pinned-prefix clause is re-checkable (the outcome's
  log-derivative verdicts — and, for MIXED codes, its verdicts
  over the pinned prefix AND R2's embedded
  `adjudicatedDraftBytes`, v16 R5-C10-3 — re-derive over the
  pinned prefix and MUST match the recorded outcome — mismatch
  is a history-
  integrity-fault, fail closed), NOT that a hypothetical earlier
  retry would have chosen identically.
  The outcome is itself terminal by
  the ordinary rules: `applied` (the finding mints,
  `effectApplied:true`) OR `refused` (a NEW bound permanent
  refusal R2 — terminal-by-refusal, class-O condition
  via the refusal-condition row, its own binding pair pointing at
  the PINNED prefix **per the two-class exception, per NDR-d (v22
  citation conversion: class-dependent binding is canonical in the
  register entry; the pre-v22 body text and its v16/v17/v19/v20 fold
  history are preserved verbatim in
  `docs/audits/g1-ndr-conflict-log.md`)**, cleared only by a fresh
  `filing-drift-resolution` naming R2 — v15 R5-C9-3: resolution
  binds R2 by record id, R1's history is excluded); re-adjudication
  NEVER re-runs
  (one outcome per withdrawal — a recorded outcome is final for
  that withdrawal)** —
  is NOT owed while the exclusion holds (nothing the supervisor can complete for damage kinds — the
  bytes are damaged, not missing) and is never class B in those states** —
  **replay vectors (v13 R5-C7-1/5, extended v14 R5-C8-1): (i) PRE-FAULT: effect appended,
  bytes intact ⇒ `effectApplied:true`, no fault. (ii) FAULT-OPEN:
  artifact damaged, no disposition ⇒ fault F appended once, act
  terminal-by-damage (NOT class B), boundary UNCLEAN+needs-owner
  via F. (ii-b) GROUP-TERMINAL (v19 R5-C13-1/2): a
  `readjudication-group` fault G disposed `withdrawn` ⇒ G
  disposed, needs-owner cleared, act TERMINAL-BY-DAMAGE with
  its claim RETIRED (the named R1 is NOT restored to live
  standing and is NOT a resolution target — its invalidity is
  why the withdrawal existed; NEITHER class B nor class O item
  — the claim retirement, not an unresolved-refusal fold, is
  what removes the class-O row; the disposition record is the
  clearing evidence), further replays reference G (never
  re-mint, never re-adjudicate into the corrupted group). (iii) WITHDRAWN (damage kind): owner withdraws F ⇒ F disposed, needs-owner
  cleared, further replays re-observe the damage and reference F
  (never re-mint, never re-raise), act stays terminal-by-damage —
  never class B. (iv) REFILED (damage kind): owner refiles with a successful
  later filing of the same claim ⇒ F disposed; the fresh finding is
  live evidence; the faulted act stays terminal-by-damage — never
  class B, never applied; (v) INTAKE-REFUSAL OPEN: bound refusal R
  of act A fails log-derivative re-derivation ⇒ fault F' (keyed
  `(A, intake-refusal, R)`) appended, boundary UNCLEAN+needs-owner
  via F', A held out of class B while F' is open; (vi) INTAKE-
  REFUSAL WITHDRAWN: owner withdraws F' ⇒ needs-owner cleared;
  until the re-adjudication outcome appends, A is `readjudication-
  owed` = CLASS B (crash here is recoverable: replay re-runs
  adjudication over the PINNED prefix frozen by the withdrawal
  record — v15 R5-C9-5, serialized protocol above); outcome applied ⇒
  `effectApplied:true`; outcome new bound refusal R2 ⇒
  terminal-by-refusal (R2 is independently validatable; a SECOND
  failed re-derivation of R2 is a NEW fault `(A, intake-refusal,
  R2)` — the disposed F' suppresses nothing); (vii) INTAKE-REFUSAL
  REFILED: claim stands via the accepted fresh filing ⇒ A
  terminal-by-disposition, never class B again; (viii) GROUP
  FAULT (v18 R5-C12-1): withdrawal W durable, recovery finds
  ≥2 valid candidates (or a candidate failing re-validation) ⇒
  group fault G appended once (`(A, readjudication-group)`),
  boundary UNCLEAN+needs-owner via G, A excluded from class B
  on G's EXISTENCE, `readjudication-owed` SUSPENDED (no outcome
  is owed while G is open); owner withdraws G ⇒ needs-owner
  cleared, group retired, A TERMINAL-BY-DAMAGE with its claim
  RETIRED (v19 R5-C13-1/2 — NOT terminal-by-refusal: invalid R1
  (named in G's `evidenceRefs[]`) was fault-adjudicated and can
  NEVER stand again or be a resolution target; the disposition
  abandons the re-adjudication route, nothing is owed, and the
  disposition record is the clearing evidence — no class-B item,
  no class-O item); re-observation references G, never re-mints** —
  **cleared by the closed owner act `filing-integrity-disposition`
  (v12 R5-C6-1; joins the closed op enum below) with payload
  `{ faultId, outcome:"refiled"|"withdrawn", newActId|null }`** —
  `faultId` names the durable `owner-filing-integrity-fault` record;
  `refiled` requires newActId naming a LATER `audit-filing` act with
  replay-derived `effectApplied == true` (same outcome-binding as
  `filing-drift-resolution`) whose filed finding satisfies the FULL
  REPLACEMENT BINDING OF THE `filing-integrity-disposition` OP (the
  op-enum entry in this section, above) — header `claim` EQUAL to the faulted act's payload `claim`
  AND severity/route PRESERVED **when the fault kind names a
  faulted FINDING (`effect-record`/`findingRef-artifact`); for
  kind `intake-refusal` the binding is claim-equality-only and
  severity/route come from the fresh filing's own intake — no
  faulted finding exists, no obligation exists to preserve
  (v17 R5-C11-1, reconciled with the op-enum copy)** (v14 R5-C8-4; and for an
  `act-payload` fault `refiled` is INEXPRESSIBLE — the corrupt
  payload establishes none of the compared fields; likewise when
  even the faulted act's `claim` cannot be established from
  durable evidence; all cases fail
  closed to `withdrawn`-only when the fields cannot be established)
  (mismatch ⇒ refused
  `integrity-disposition-mismatch`); `withdrawn` carries
  newActId:null and is ALWAYS admissible. Clearing predicate (objective,
  replay-checked): the named fault record has a conforming disposition
  record naming IT; one disposition per fault (a second is refused,
  already-resolved). **After disposition the faulted act/effect is
  NEVER rewritten and its damaged bytes are never treated as valid
  evidence — the fault record and the damaged finding remain as
  immutable evidence; `refiled` establishes the claim's FRESH filing
  as the live evidence, `withdrawn` retires the claim; **the faulted
  finding's CHAIN obligations resolve through the disposition record
  itself (v13 R5-C7-6 — the chain table gains its machine-checked
  link, no new op): `refiled` — the disposition record is the
  EFFECTIVE-SURVIVOR binding for every chain row whose survivor (or
  member link) names the damaged finding: the refiled finding (the
  claim-equal fresh filing named by newActId) is the effective
  survivor for those rows, traversed exactly like a correction-edge
  transshipment (§14.10.2 fold), forward-only — rows evaluated over
  earlier prefixes are never re-adjudicated; `withdrawn` — the
  claim is OWNER-RETIREMENT (v14 R5-C8-3 — named outcome, defined
  inline; v13 routed members to "retired-survivor rows" that do
  not exist in this table): chain rows consuming the damaged
  finding evaluate it as **owner-retired-by-withdrawal**: the
  damaged survivor never discharges through its own disposition —
  every member whose chain evaluation consumes it is UNCLEAN +
  needs-owner naming that member at EVERY boundary thereafter
  (forward-only; boundaries before the withdrawal keep their
  frozen verdicts), including already-closed major members whose
  link pointed at the damaged survivor; the ONLY cure is each
  member's OWN route (v15 R5-C9-1: an OPEN member takes the r4
  table's ordinary disposition rows as if it stood alone; an
  ALREADY-CLOSED member is cured by §14.10.2's SECOND named
  reopening edge (owner `closed-residual` withdrawal-strand act
  citing this disposition, forward-only, resolved as residual) —
  every strand HAS a reachable cure; withdrawal blocks nothing,
  it waives nothing), and
  withdrawal alone NEVER silently discharges a chain — it routes
  it through this named row. Open and
  already-closed damaged survivors take the SAME disposition path
  (the disposition acts on the fault + finding identity, and §14.10.2's
  closed-state refusal does NOT bar it — it is a `filing-integrity-
  disposition`, not an `audit-finding-update` transition)** (the
  disposition clears the FAULT condition, and the finding's chain
  obligations follow exactly the routes above)** —
  **(3) full
  mapping, unwaived:** EVERY header/act/envelope mapping of the
  entry rule applies — the header parses per §14.10.1, every
  authority-relevant record field re-derives from **the stage-(2)
  verification source (the spool bytes PRE-effect, the `findingRef`
  artifact POST-effect — v11 R5-C5-3: v9/v10 said "from the spool
  bytes" unqualified, which post-success demanded bytes the
  post-effect rule itself declares unnecessary)**,
  the act payload `claim` equals the header's re-derived `claim`
  UNDER THE CLAIM-EQUALITY ENCODING PINNED IN §14.10.3 (v10
  R5-C4-3: NFC of both decoded JSON string values, equal by
  code-point sequence — v9 cited §14.10.1 and "no normalization",
  both wrong), cycle comes from
  the act payload alone (plus `taskId|null` from the act payload,
  v10 R5-C4-1), and every other envelope field matches its
  listed source. "Payload not reconstructable from finding-record
  fields" is NOT a refusal cause for this op — that ONE general step
  (reconstruction from the PRIVILEGED RECORD's own fields) is the
  sole thing replaced; every general authority, channel, mapping,
  and consumption check above stands in full.
  **Identical bytes ≠ identical filing (v9 R4-C3-6 — v8 called the
  spool re-read "an idempotent re-read" without saying what the
  FILING does; idempotence lives at the record-id/effect level, not
  at the draft-byte level):** (a) REDELIVERY of the same act (same
  act id/effect id) is idempotent — replay recognizes the already-
  applied effect, consumes nothing new, appends nothing new (the
  general single-consumption rule; this sentence names its
  application to filings). (b) A NEW confirmed act over identical
  draft bytes is a NEW filing ATTEMPT with a NEW effect id: **if
  intake SUCCEEDS it** appends a
  SEPARATE `audit-finding` record **(v13 R5-C7-4: the append is
  CONDITIONAL on intake — the sentence describes the success
  outcome, never a mandate that outranks intake; an attempt that
  FAILS intake produces a refusal record and follows the
  terminal-by-refusal rule above, not an append — the two sentences
  may never both claim the same act)** — the spool reuses its
  content-addressed bytes, but spool dedup is STORAGE dedup and has
  no disposition meaning; duplicate INTENT is not a validation concept
  and is never refused at intake **AS INTENT DEDUP (v12 R5-C6-3: a
  new act over identical bytes is a new filing ATTEMPT, not an
  unconditional successful append — it remains subject to EVERY
  ordinary intake rule on its own content; e.g. a correction draft
  (`correctionOf:"A"`) resubmitted after its first correction landed
  is refused `correction-ambiguity` by lineage linearity (at most ONE
  correction per target), and a second filing of the same header else
  passes or fails intake on its own merits — what is NOT refused is
  the duplicate intent AS SUCH, never the ordinary validation)**.
  Two such findings are distinct
  findings and are dispositioned as such: any `rejected-duplicate`
  between them obeys the §14.12.2 chain table (machine-checked
  link — their repros are trivially digest-equal if falsifiable —
  or owner-authorized ⇒ UNCLEAN-until-disposition), with no special
  case. No act may refer-to/reuse another act's effect record: the
  one-act/one-effect binding is strict.
  The general verification paragraph's
  requirement is qualified accordingly: from-record reconstruction
  applies to every op EXCEPT `audit-filing`, whose stage-(3)
  mapping above is its equivalent.
  The spool lives in the EPISODE dir at `drafts/` (episode-relative;
  created by the CLI channel on first confirmation, supervisor-
  readable, never rewritten — content-addressed names make re-filing
  identical bytes a content-addressed re-read OF THE SPOOL, not a
  no-op filing — see the identical-bytes rule above).
  **Completeness & binding (v9, c7-B1):** the enumeration is CLOSED
  and COMPLETE — every privileged record kind in §14.11–§14.15 whose
  intake requires owner authority MUST have a listed op schema; a kind
  without one CANNOT receive an owner-act (refused at validation), new
  kinds require their schema added here first, AND an implementation
  conformance test walks the §14.11–§14.15 owner-authorized record
  kinds against this list (a kind in the sections with no op schema is
  a contract defect caught by the test, not at runtime surprise).
  Every payload binds EVERY authority-relevant field of its resulting
  record: the supervisor's independent reconstruction (below) checks
  both digest equality AND field presence — a resulting-record field
  that affects the disposition but is absent from the op schema makes
  the record REFUSED, never accepted on a partial digest.
  **The TTY confirmation binds the FULL supervisor-verified
  operation (v9, c7-B1; display strengthened v10, c8-M5):** the CLI
  displays the supervisor-resolved `op` and the COMPLETE canonical
  payload — EVERY field and value rendered from the exact
  supervisor-verified canonical bytes, explicit `null`s included
  (v10: a digest alone proves byte consistency of something, not
  that the operator read the right thing — informed confirmation
  requires the operator to see every authority-relevant value, e.g.
  a `survivorId` or `residualCapUsd` differing from intent), PLUS
  the canonical payload digest (for operator cross-check against
  their own channel record), BEFORE collecting the confirmation, and
  the `owner-act` record carries `op` + `payloadDigest` recomputed
  and verified by the supervisor (a CLI assertion alone never
  confirms an operation the display did not show). **Verification (v8):** the SUPERVISING
  process independently reconstructs the canonical bytes from the
  privileged record's own fields under the op schema and recomputes
  the digest; the CLI-supplied `payloadDigest` is compared against the
  supervisor's recomputation and the record is REFUSED on any
  mismatch — the CLI's digest is a claim, the supervisor's
  recomputation is the check (a malicious/deviating CLI cannot slip a
  payload by serializing differently). Confirmation of the operation
  itself binds via the interactive channel record as before; the
  compromised-supervisor and same-user limits above still apply
  unaltered. **Consumption (v7, effect-bound v10, c8-B1/c8-M5):**
  one owner-act authorizes exactly ONE privileged record — OR one
  atomic group (the successor-ratification group of §14.11.2 is ONE
  authorized effect: consumption counts the whole group once; a
  half-applied group is malformed per §14.11.2 framing, so partial
  consumption cannot occur) — validation
  refuses a second privileged record naming the same owner-act id
  (redelivery of the identical privileged record is idempotent by ITS
  record id; a different payload under a consumed act is refused);
  multi-operation intent requires multi-field payloads defined per op
  or separate acts.
  **Effect binding (v10, c8-B1):** the `owner-act` record carries
  `effectRecordIds` — the ids of the authorized privileged record(s):
  exactly one id, or exactly the member ids of the authorized atomic
  group. `effectApplied` is a replay-DERIVED state: true iff every
  named record exists in the log and validates against the act's op
  schema — **with ONE named exception (v9 R4-C3-2 — re-lands C2-2,
  which the crashed fold script dropped from the body while the
  changelog claimed it; extended to mapping refusals v10 R5-C4-2;
  made EXHAUSTIVE v11 R5-C5-5):
  a filing-class act (`audit-filing`) whose intake appended a
  conforming PERMANENT-refusal record — ANY refusal in §14.10.3's
  exhaustive permanent-filing-refusal rule (drift, mapping, the
  §14.10.2 lineage intake refusals, or a finding-schema intake
  failure; the refusal record names its diagnostic code; a fresh
  replay RECOGNIZES the durable refusal — adjudicated at the
  intake prefix and never re-adjudicated against the evolved
  prefix (v12 R5-C6-2) — so the effect is permanently un-applicable and
  class B — "the supervisor owes and can complete it" — would be
  false forever) naming the act id is TERMINAL-BY-REFUSAL — replay
  does NOT count its never-created finding as an owed record: the
  act is not class B
  (nothing is owed that intake has adjudicated and refused) and
  instead holds the boundary UNCLEAN + needs-owner (class O) through
  its refusal condition (the condition names the refusal record)
  until a conforming `filing-drift-resolution` act
  (v10: generalized to either named refusal kind; v11: to EVERY
  permanent filing refusal) clears the condition;
  the resolution act is consumed under the
  GENERAL effect rule — its effectRecordIds name the resolution
  record IT mints, which exists on append, so the clearing effect
  can never itself dangle as a missing effect.** **SECOND NAMED
  EXCEPTION — the two-phase residual-cure act (v26 R5-C18F-2):** a
  `residual-cure` act's effect IS its settlement record
  `cure-settlement-<actId>` (§14.10.3 protocol), whose ID is
  deterministically derivable from the act BEFORE it exists —
  `effectRecordIds` is the singleton of that derived id, and
  `effectApplied` is true iff the settlement exists, binds the act,
  and passes the §14.10.3 evidence check (replay recomputes it).
  The act confirms with its effect record NOT yet in existence (a
  legal state — the pre-refusal state of a refusal-fork act is the
  same shape: confirmed, effect not yet appended), so this is NOT a
  contradiction of the existence rule, it is a pre-REGISTERED effect
  identity. While the settlement is absent the act is NEITHER
  `effectApplied:true` NOR class B: settlement is owed by EVIDENCE
  ARRIVAL, not by supervisor effort, so the general "the supervisor
  owes it and can complete it" predicate is false and class B would
  block appends forever on evidence no one can compel; the act holds
  NO additional condition — an unsettled cure adds no hold beyond
  the residual-inherited uncleanliness the cure exists to clear
  (§14.12.2 chain rule, v25 R5-C18-3), which is its own unclean
  row until settlement lands. A crash between confirmation and
  settlement leaves a confirmed, unsettled cure: replay re-derives
  the pending settlement from the deterministic id and, when the
  evidence arrives and passes the check, the supervisor appends the
  settlement with that id — an unsettled cure NEVER finalizes the
  round it is live in. **CALLER SWEEP (v27 R5-C19-2 — v26 stated this
  exception HERE only, while the general effect fold, the §14.12.2 B
  row, the queue P3 predicate and the quiesce-stall rule each still
  classified a confirmed-unsettled-un-cancelled cure act as class B
  from their own text, so one prefix carried two classifications):**
  this exception governs EVERY consumer of the effect fold — a
  `residual-cure` act that is confirmed, UNSETTLED, and NOT
  CANCELLED is excluded from class B at every site (the B row, P3
  effect completion, the stall rule), each carrying this exclusion by
  named reference; "NEVER finalizes the round" means exactly: never
  a CLEAN boundary while unsettled — which is already true by the
  residual-inherited unclean condition itself, carried per §14.12.2
  until settlement lands; the cure's non-settlement adds NO
  separate hold, so it neither blocks appends (it is not B) nor
  converts through the quiesce-stall B→O route (that route converts
  supervisor-owed work; nothing is owed through the DRAIN here — an
  owed `cure-gate` completion is recovery-pass work restored before
  any boundary evaluation, never a drain/stall item, v29 G1-V29-C6-1),
  and the boundary
  the round gets while the cure is unsettled is the residual's own
  UNCLEAN + needs-owner boundary, unchanged.** An act with
  `effectApplied:false` that is in NONE of the NDR-l terminal states
  (applied excluded by `effectApplied:false`; terminal-by-refusal,
  terminal-by-damage, terminal-by-disposition, and
  terminal-by-cancellation per NDR-l are each terminal, never owed —
  v28 R5-C20P-1: the v27 text named only terminal-by-refusal here,
  re-admitting settled/cancelled/damaged acts to the owed predicate)
  **AND NOT an NDR-v exception act** (a confirmed, UNSETTLED,
  UN-cancelled `residual-cure` act — the sweep above; v27 R5-C19-2)
  **and NOT under an
  `owner-filing-integrity-fault` (v12 R5-C6-1; exclusion keyed on fault
  EXISTENCE not undispositioned, v13
  R5-C7-1 — KIND-BOUNDED v14 R5-C8-1: for the DAMAGE kinds
  (`effect-record`, `findingRef-artifact`, `act-payload`,
  `readjudication-group` — fourth kind enumerated here v18
  R5-C12-1) the exclusion
  holds in ANY state and post-disposition the act is TERMINAL-BY-DAMAGE
  (a named terminal effect state — the full closed taxonomy is
  canonical per NDR-l, v27) and is never
  re-classified as outstanding (the group kind's sole-exit
  `withdrawn` is TERMINAL-BY-DAMAGE with the claim retired —
  v19 R5-C13-1/2 corrects v18's "restores terminal-by-refusal
  standing via the superseded R1": the R1 a group names is
  fault-adjudicated INVALID and can never stand again); for
  `intake-refusal` the exclusion
  covers the OPEN fault and the `refiled` disposition (terminal-by-
  disposition — the claim stands via the accepted fresh filing), while
  `withdrawn` WITHOUT a re-adjudication outcome record is precisely
  `readjudication-owed` — THIS rule's own outstanding effect, class B
  (drain-progressing) until the outcome lands; the full precedence
  table is the §14.10.3 fault-state paragraph, and the two texts may
  never disagree; the
  exclusion from class B for damage kinds: damaged bytes are not owed
  work the supervisor can complete, so the same act is never
  simultaneously class B (blocking) and class O (owner-only); while a
  fault is OPEN it holds the boundary through its class-O fault
  condition until
  `filing-integrity-disposition` clears it)** is an **outstanding
  effect**: class B in the §14.12.2 finalization decision table (the
  supervisor owes the effect and can complete it) — no CLEAN boundary
  appends while a drained act's effect is owed
  (v11, c9-B3 precision: the UNCLEAN route via B→O conversion exists
  exactly as the §14.12.2 table defines it — `needs-owner`, effect
  still owed — but AUTHORITY never converts: the act is unconsumed
  until its effects validate), and
  an un-drained queue entry (class B) or a class-O-shaped act follows
  the queue rules — an acknowledged act NEVER closes a CLEAN boundary
  its effect has not entered.
- The orchestrator routes on `route` alone and holds no disposition
  power beyond `accepted-fix`/`rejected-refuted`/`rejected-duplicate`/
  `superseded` bookkeeping transitions (v5: `rejected-refuted` added to
  the list — it is evidence-bound, `reproRunRef` required, and carries
  no acceptance; `closed-residual` remains owner-only).

#### 14.10.5 What this section does NOT do

- No routing implementation (consumer's job, post-G2) — `route` is the
  contract the router consumes, nothing more.
- No norm state: `affectedNorm` POINTS at ratified text; it does not
  create, gate, or version it (G2, separate section).
- No convergence/stop rule: G3 owns the k-consecutive-clean +
  family-diversity condition AND the severity/opinion sign-off
  enforcement; this record only supplies its inputs (`producer.model`,
  `severity`, `verdictBasis`, close transitions).
- No autonomy claim: kickoff, design-cycle budget (G4), and finding
  partitioning (G5) are separate open compartments. G2–G5 are drafted
  in §14.11–§14.15 (DRAFT v2 after the round-0 audit, not ratified).
- No transport: records land in the local episode log; cross-host
  collection stays Q4 (file-only until transport decides).
